articles.title: ‘There’s more we want to do’ says Arteta after Como win
articles.summary: Gunners boss wants more signings before the end of the month
articles.content:
‘There’s more we want to do’ says Arteta after Como win

Gunners boss wants more signings before the end of the month

Last Update:

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta says the Premier League champions are still hoping to sign more players before the start of the season.

New signing Bruno Guimaraes impressed after his £75m switch from Newcastle as the Gunners beat Serie A side Como in a friendly on Wednesday night.

Arsenal have also signed winger Christos Tzolis this summer but were not able to recruit Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid.

And Leandro Trossard and Christian Norgaard have moved on to leave Arteta looking for more.

He said: “There is more that we want to do. Every time we have an opportunity to improve the quality of the squad we need to do that.

“The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable. We want to try and do that. We cannot promise that will do it because it does not only depend on us.

“Let’s see if Bruno can start this weekend, he only had three training sessions but he looked good. He was pushing to play minutes and play in front of our fans. You sense a strong connection immediately.”

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

The Gunners have won the Shield on 17 occasions, with this season’s match being played in Cardiff.

Arteta said: “It was a very good test against Como. It was a bit tricky today as we play a final on Sunday. To play the players and not expose them too much.

“They perform at a really high level. The scoreline should have been different, and that is where we have to improve.”

articles.title: Brilliant Brahim solo goal gives Real Madrid friendly win
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr captains Real to a comfortable enough friendly win
articles.content:
Brilliant Brahim solo goal gives Real Madrid friendly win

Vinicius Jr captains Real to a comfortable enough friendly win

Last Update:

Real Madrid continued their pre-season preparation with a 1-0 win over Deportivo.

Bernardo Silva impressed in midfield, with Brahim Diaz scoring the only goal with a wonderful solo effort before half time.

Jude Bellingham was not involved but Vinicius Jr started after his summer-long transfer links with Arsenal.

The Brazil forward signed a new six-year contract at Real last week, with the club calling the 26-year-old “one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history”.

Vinicius had one effort well cleared in a scrappy first half before Diaz opened the scoring just before the interval with a brilliant solo goal.

The Morocco attacker was sent clear by a quick throw from goalkeeper Andriy Lunin, and after chesting the ball down he ran clear of the defence to fire in neatly.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was among the half-time changes for Real, playing alongside Denzel Dumfries, with the Dutchman soon going close with a powerful header.

Lunin made an excellent late double save as Jose Mourinho’s side took the win.

Madrid’s La Liga campaign starts at Espanyol on August 22 (20:30 BST). Deportivo host Elche on August 17 (20:00).

articles.title: Arsenal hand debut to Guimaraes in friendly shootout win
articles.summary: £75m signing plays 45 minutes and scores in a shootout
articles.content:
Arsenal hand debut to Guimaraes in friendly shootout win

£75m signing plays 45 minutes and scores in a shootout

Last Update:

Bruno Guimaraes got his first runout at the Emirates and scored a penalty as Arsenal’s pre-season continued with a shootout win against Italian side Como.

The £75m signing from Newcastle played the second half of a competitive enough friendly as Arsenal fans welcomed midfielders new and old.

Como achieved their best-ever finish in Serie A last season under ex-Arsenal favourite Cesc Fabregas, coming fourth to achieve Champions League qualification.

Fabregas won the FA Cup in 2005 and reached the 2006 Champions League and 2007 EFL Cup finals during his time as an Arsenal midfielder between 2003 and 2011.

Gabriel Jesus and Eberechi Eze only played 32 minutes before being replaced as Mikel Arteta looked after his squad.

And moments later Lewis-Skelly struck, side-footing home after an error at the back from Como saw a clearance charged down.

The full-back turned midfielder has been linked with a move away from the Gunners this summer but celebrated by touching the badge on his shirt and praying to the fans.

The Italian side were able to level before the break as Martin Baturina fired in after some lovely footwork.

Guimaraes was introduced at half-time, with fellow substitute Noni Madueke going close in a scrappier second period.

Kai Havertz had the ball in the net late on but it was ruled out before the sides took on a shootout after a 1-1 draw.

England defender Trevoh Chalobah, who signed from Chelsea last week, was on the bench for Como alongside the likes of former Spain forward Alvaro Morata.

Morata was off target, along with Madueke, before new signing Christos Tzolis fired in the winner.

Arsenal now take on Enzo Maresca and Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on Sunday.

articles.title: BREAKING: Former Barcelona boss Xavi named new Netherlands manager
articles.summary: Xavi replaces Ronald Koeman
articles.content:
BREAKING: Former Barcelona boss Xavi named new Netherlands manager

Xavi replaces Ronald Koeman

Last Update:

Former Barcelona coach and captain Xavi has been named as the new manager of the Netherlands national team.

The 46-year-old has been without a job since leaving the Nou Camp in 2024 but has been chosen to replace Ronald Koeman.

He has signed a contract until the 2030 World Cup.

“It is an honour to become the coach of the Dutch national team,” Xavi said.

“As someone who came through Barcelona’s academy, with the strong influence of figures like Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that, in a way, I am a son of Dutch football.”

The Dutch parted company with Koeman – another former Barca boss – after they were knocked out of the World Cup by Morocco.

Koeman was widely criticised for a tactic of containment against the African champions in a break from the team’s traditional approach.

Former Belgium and Portugal coach Roberto Martinez was linked with the job but Xavi has instead been handed his first international role.

Xavi won the World Cup with Spain in 2010 and began his coaching career at Al Saad in Qatar before taking the job with Barcelona in 2021. He led the team to the LaLiga title in 2022-23 and won the Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona in 2023.

articles.title: Lukaku makes Fenerbahce move
articles.summary: Much-travelled striker is heading to Turkey
articles.content:
Lukaku makes Fenerbahce move

Much-travelled striker is heading to Turkey

Last Update:

Former Chelsea, Manchester United and Everton striker Romelu Lukaku has swapped Serie ​A for the Turkish Super Lig after Fenerbahce announced the signing of the Napoli goalscorer.

Fenerbahce ⁠have reportedly paid a €6 million (£5.1 million) fee plus performance-related bonuses for the former Inter Milan striker.

The 33-year-old has played for eight clubs previously and has scored over 300 goals in all competitions.

“It’s an honour and a privilege to be joining your club, to join this ⁠club with a wonderful history,” he said in a message to the Fenerbahce fans.

The veteran striker, who won the Serie A title ⁠with Napoli in 2024-25, endured a frustrating campaign last ​season ⁠that was hampered by injuries, ‌limiting him to just seven appearances across all competitions.

However, Lukaku was still called up to the Belgium squad that ‌reached the quarter-finals at the World ‌Cup, where he scored three times.

“I want to thank the coach for the trust and the belief in me as a man, first ⁠of all, and also my qualities as a football player. I’m fit, 100% ready to go,” Lukaku added.

“For me, it’s also like a little emotional moment because after many years (I’m) going back to Turkey, where I lived as a young kid, where I discovered the professional world as ‌a toddler with my dad,” added Lukaku, whose ​father Roger played for Genclerbirligi.

“It’s going to be ‌special and a very emotional ⁠moment to be back there. I’m very proud ⁠that it is with Fenerbahce.”

Fenerbahce finished second in the league last season, ‌losing the title ​to Galatasaray by three points. ‌They begin the new campaign ​against Genclerbirligi on Saturday.

articles.title: Liverpool lack characters, says former striker Aldridge
articles.summary: The Reds have work to do to challenge again says former Kop favourite
articles.content:
Liverpool lack characters, says former striker Aldridge

The Reds have work to do to challenge again says former Kop favourite

Last Update:

Liverpool ‘lack characters’ and need to work harder to compete in the Premier League this season, says former Reds favourite John Aldridge.

Liverpool won the Premier League in 2025 but were miles off the pace last season.

The Reds eventually finished fifth in the Premier League, 25 points behind champions Arsenal, with manager Arne Slot paying the price.

Andoni Iraola has come in and overseen a quiet summer so far. And with Mo Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all leaving the club Aldridge thinks the squad is light on experience.

“There were characters everywhere in the squad two or three years ago, but I think they’re lacking in that department now,” Aldridge told 101 Great Goals in conjunction with BetGoodwin.

“Players like James Milner, Jordan Henderson and Andy Robertson are exactly what you want in the dressing room and they’re hard to replace.

“The best teams I played in had characters. They made training enjoyable because you had a laugh and you looked forward to being together, but you also worked really hard. You’ve got to be serious when the time comes, but it’s still important to have fun and build team spirit.”

Aldridge won the league title and FA Cup with Liverpool in the 1980s before enjoying a prolific spell in Spain and a long spell in charge at Tranmere Rovers.

articles.title: Djed Spence close to Inter Milan move as clubs agree £27m fee
articles.summary: England defender Djed Spence is closing in on a move to Serie A giants Inter Milan after Tottenham reportedly agreed a fee of £27m for the full-back. Spence, 26, was a surprise call-up to Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup but impressed in a series of cameos on either side of the defence. […]
articles.content:
Djed Spence close to Inter Milan move as clubs agree £27m fee

Last Update:

England defender Djed Spence is closing in on a move to Serie A giants Inter Milan after Tottenham reportedly agreed a fee of £27m for the full-back.

Spence, 26, was a surprise call-up to Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup but impressed in a series of cameos on either side of the defence.

His pace and energy made him a fan favourite but he has struggled for regular action at Tottenham since moving from Middlesbrough in 2022.

And now transfers expert Fabrizio Romano says Inter have agreed a price for the former Nottingham Forest man.

Should Spence move to the San Siro he will link up with England team-mate John Stones, who signed for Inter earlier this summer after leaving Manchester City.

Spence initially endured a tough start at Tottenham, making just six appearances in his debut campaign before spending time on loan at Rennes, Leeds United, and Genoa.

His Spurs career completely turned around under Ange Postecoglou. Re-integrated into the squad for the 2024/25 season, the versatile full-back impressed on either flank, making 41 appearances across all competitions and scoring his first goals for the club.

He capped off his revival by helping Spurs win the 2025 Europa League, earning a new contract and his senior England call-up.

Tottenham are well stocked at left-back after signing Andrew Robertson from Liverpool while Spain’s World Cup winner Pedro Porro is first choice on the right.

articles.title: Lionel Messi releases emotional statement following Dad’s death and hints at retirement
articles.summary: Lionel Messi says he could not have done any more to bring a second successive World Cup trophy back to Argentina
articles.content:
Lionel Messi releases emotional statement following Dad’s death and hints at retirement

Lionel Messi says he could not have done any more to bring a second successive World Cup trophy back to Argentina

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has revealed his pain at failing to deliver a second World Cup trophy for his Dad, Jorge, who passed away last week and admitted he is not sure how long he will continue playing.

Messi’s Argentina reached the final in New Jersey last month but were unable to hold off Spain, who won 1-0 thanks to Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Jorge, who was also Messi’s long-time agent, missed the tournament after his condition deteriorated following a prolonged illness. He subsequently died aged 68 in his hometown of Rosario, on Friday.

Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you.

“I don’t know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I’m really not sure if I’ll carry on doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Table of Contents

Messi reveals Dad persuaded him to go to the World Cup

Messi gave serious consideration to not playing at the World Cup but revealed Jorge had persuaded him to give it one last shot.

Messi wrote: “Dad, you kept asking me to play in one last World Cup… just days before it began was when your condition got worse.

“It was the first time you weren’t going to be there with me at tournament… but Mom kept telling me you were going to get better and that you’d be well enough to travel.

“I kept telling you we were going to reach the World Cup final so you could make the trip, this was my mission once again.

“After every match, I waited for and missed your message. That’s when I realised how serious the situation really was.

“I couldn’t stop thinking about going as far as possible, give you more time and the chance to watch one of the games.”

Messi struggled to make an impact in the final

It was an exhausting tournament for the former Barcelona and PSG star, who captained his country to extra-time wins over Cape Verde and Switzerland before a mentally draining semi-final victory over old foes England.

And Messi conceded had nothing left to give against Spain.

He added: “We reached the final, but you couldn’t be there. I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you another one. I couldn’t.

“My legs just couldn’t give me any more. This time I tried to push beyond what my body could handle, but I couldn’t.

“I never managed to feel physically right.

“We didn’t become champions Dad, but you have no idea how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play in it… as you told me, always.”

Messi legacy lives on

Jorge was survived by his wife, Celia, and their four children: Lionel, Rodrigo, Matias and María Sol.

Messi’s boyhood club, Newell’s Old Boys, led the tributes.

“Newell’s Old Boys mourn with profound pain and sorrow the passing of Jorge Messi,” the club said.

“He was a renowned Newell’s supporter, businessman and the father of the captain of the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi.

“Jorge was the support and the person who, together with his wife, Celia, strengthened the career of the greatest player of all time with vision, rigour and affection.

“His constant support and behind-the-scenes leadership were fundamental in supporting every step of Lionel’s journey.”

Jorge worked in a steel factory in Rosario before moving to Europe when Messi joined Barcelona’s academy in 2000.

He went on to oversee his son’s career as his agent, guiding moves from Barcelona to PSG and later Inter Miami, while helping manage one of the most successful careers in football history.

Messi is currently taking time out from football and will only be considered for Miami duty when he feels ready to return to Florida. He has two years left on the three-year deal he signed in 2025.

articles.title: Rodri hopes Barcelona can agree fee with City to avoid return to Manchester
articles.summary: Rodri is hoping his move from Manchester City to Barcelona can be sorted by Friday, and save him a trip to England
articles.content:
Rodri hopes Barcelona can agree fee with City to avoid return to Manchester

Rodri is hoping his move from Manchester City to Barcelona can be sorted by Friday, and save him a trip to England

Last Update:

Rodri is desperately hoping Barcelona can agree a fee with Manchester City by Friday so that he does not have to return to England.

The 30-year-old has his heart set on a move to Camp Nou after opting to join the defending La Liga champions and snub interest from their arch-rivals Real Madrid.

Rodri is believed to be house hunting in Catalonia but is expected back at the Etihad Training Campus on Friday to enable City medics to assess his fitness following a minor back operation.

Spain’s World Cup-winning captain would rather remain in Barcelona and avoid a trip back to Manchester but that depends on whether the two clubs can agree a fee.

Barca have offered around £43million for the former Atletico Madrid midfielder but City are holding out for nearer £60m even though he has now entered the final year of his contract.

Reports in Spain suggest the two clubs will likely settle for a fee somewhere in the middle although City are acutely aware of Barca’s need to get the deal done after president Joan Laporta publicly announced the club had agreed personal terms with the player.

Rodri a priority for Barcelona as Real Madrid strengthen

Rodri’s signing is seen as key for the Catalans if they want to retain the title they have won in each of the past two seasons, and especially with Real Madrid likely to be revitalised following the return of Jose Mourinho as coach and a summer of heavy recruitment at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid have brought in the likes of Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella and club-record signing Yan Diomande as well as renewing winger Vinicius Jr on a new, long-term contract.

Barca have been quiet in comparison with Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi their only major acquisitions.

They are also waiting on news of midfielder Frenkie De Jong’s knee injury with reports suggesting the club are getting increasingly frustrated with the Netherlands international.

De Jong returned from the World Cup with a partial tear of a meniscus cruciate ligament but wants it to heal with rest and rehabilitation. Barca, though, want him to undergo surgery as they feel that would lead to a quicker recovery period.

That has led to an uncomfortable stand-off with De Jong’s method showing little sign of progress.

articles.title: Manchester City sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli for a second time
articles.summary: Manchester City have bolstered their goalkeeping ranks by signing experienced Argentine Geronimo Rulli
articles.content:
Manchester City sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli for a second time

Manchester City have bolstered their goalkeeping ranks by signing experienced Argentine Geronimo Rulli

Last Update:

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille to act as back-up to established number one Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Rulli is reported to have cost City £1.7million and will fill the same role occupied by James Trafford last season. Trafford last week joined Leeds in a £45m deal.

The 34-year-old has signed for City before, in the summer of 2016, but left midway through the following season without making an appearance.

“This is an amazing opportunity for me and one I had to grasp,” Rulli told the club’s official website. “When the chance to join Manchester City comes along you have to go for it.

“Everyone knows what an impressive club this is. City’s success over a long time has been impressive. Everyone I have spoken to about City said I had to join them because they are a club with incredibly high standards.

“Every professional wants to be in a high-performance environment and I can’t wait to get started because I know I will improve and learn, which is always my main priority.

“My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can to reach my best level.”

Table of Contents

City chief Viana delighted to bring in Rulli

Rulli has had spells with Real Sociedad, Montpellier, Villarreal, Ajax and Marseille and City’s director of football Hugo Viana was pleased to have brought in the experienced Argentina international, who was one of the aggressors in the fracas that marred the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup final against Spain.

“It’s a pleasure to welcome Gerónimo back to the club,” Viana said. “The experience he brings is obvious – he has played at the very highest level for many years.

“I have been really impressed by him during our conversations, a strong desire to join us. It’s clear we are getting a brilliant professional, as well as a top ‘keeper.

“Everyone at City is looking forward to welcoming him back to the club. The qualities he will bring are ones we need, and together with Gigio and Marcus [Bettinelli] make a great team. Our goalkeeper coaches are really happy with the group.”

City still with work to do before window closes

City are likely to be active over the closing weeks of the transfer window with both incomings and departures expected.

The headline outgoing is likely to be Spain captain Rodri, over whom City are in talks with Barcelona, while Savinho and Tijjani Reijnders could also leave.

City are believed to be close to signing Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

articles.title: Roberto Martinez unlikely to take over as Netherlands boss – agent
articles.summary: Roberto Martinez's agent has poured cold water on speculation the Spaniard was set to replace Ronald Koeman as Netherlands boss
articles.content:
Roberto Martinez unlikely to take over as Netherlands boss – agent

Roberto Martinez's agent has poured cold water on speculation the Spaniard was set to replace Ronald Koeman as Netherlands boss

Last Update:

Roberto Martinez’s agent has played down talk of his client taking over as the Netherlands’ head coach.

The role is currently vacant after Ronald Koeman walked away following Oranje’s disappointing World Cup campaign that saw them exit at the round of 32 stage against Morocco.

Koeman was widely criticised for a tactic of containment against the African champions in a break from the team’s traditional approach.

The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) has been linked with several names, including Arne Slot and Louis van Gaal, but Martinez is also reportedly a contender.

The 53-year-old has vast experience of international football after spells with Belgium and, most recently, Portugal but his representative Jesse De Preter believes the KNVB’s technical director Nigel De Jong will look elsewhere.

De Preter said: “If Nigel de Jong calls, we will talk. Traditionally, the KNVB goes for a Dutch coach and financially I suspect that the expectations are very far apart. I don’t see how this can be a deal.”

Table of Contents

Martinez would buck trend if he succeeded Koeman as Netherlands boss

The Netherlands have not had a foreign coach for 48 years with Austrian Ernst Happel at the helm during their run to the 1978 World Cup final.

Martinez would be a controversial choice given his reputation for not making the most of working with talented squads.

He led Belgium’s Golden Generation to a third-placed finish at the 2018 World Cup but could only manage a quarter-final run at Euro 2020 and a group-stage exit at the 2022 World Cup.

Martinez subsequently took over as Portugal boss but his only success was the 2024/25 Nations League.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Co were knocked out of Euro 2024 at the quarter-final stage and the World Cup earlier this summer in the round of 16.

Slot rules himself out of Netherlands search

Slot was an early contender for the Netherlands role after being sacked by Liverpool at the end of last season.

But the former Feyenoord boss would rather focus on getting back into club management.

In an interview with Voetbal International, he said: “Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration.

“That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks.

“At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.

“And [this is] why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

“I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week.

“For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me.

“It would be a great honour to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.”

articles.title: Chelsea: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Xabi Alonso put Blues back on track?
articles.summary: Chelsea once again have new management at the helm this season, but can Xabi Alonso steer them back in the right direction?
articles.content:
Chelsea: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Xabi Alonso put Blues back on track?

Chelsea once again have new management at the helm this season, but can Xabi Alonso steer them back in the right direction?

Last Update:

Chelsea head into the new Premier League season with genuine optimism after one of the busiest summers in their recent history.

A disappointing 10th-place finish in 2025/26 ended any hopes of European football, but it also prompted another major reset at Stamford Bridge.

The club turned to Xabi Alonso, whose impressive work at Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid made him one of the most sought-after coaches in Europe, with the Spaniard tasked with restoring Chelsea to the top end of the table.

Alonso has wasted little time stamping his authority on the squad. Chelsea have spent heavily once again, but unlike previous windows, there has been a clear emphasis on adding players who fit a defined tactical identity.

Morgan Rogers arrived from Aston Villa in a club-record £117m deal. Valentin Barco strengthens the midfield, while Maxence Lacroix adds much-needed pace and athleticism to the defence.

Emmanuel Emegha provides another option in attack, with highly-rated youngsters Marco Palestra, Denner and Dastan Satpaev also joining as part of the club’s long-term project.

Experience has also been added. Jordan Henderson arrives after leaving Brentford, bringing leadership to one of the youngest squads in the division, while Danny Welbeck offers proven top-flight quality and another experienced voice in the dressing room.

There are still questions to answer. Chelsea conceded too many goals last season and consistency has remained elusive despite significant investment.

But for the first time in several years, there appears to be a coherent footballing vision behind the recruitment.

Whether that translates into an immediate return to the Champions League remains to be seen.

Table of Contents

Summer Ins and Outs

IN

Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa – £117m

Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace – £52m

Marco Palestra from Atalanta – £42m

Valentin Barco from Strasbourg – undisclosed

Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg – undisclosed

Jordan Henderson from Brentford – free

Danny Welbeck from Brighton – £5m

Denner from Corinthians – undisclosed

Dastan Satpaev from Kairat Almaty – undisclosed

Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano – £16.2m

OUT

Trevoh Chalobah to Como – £31m

What do Chelsea need before the window closes?

Despite the scale of their spending, Chelsea could still strengthen in defence.

Lacroix improves the back line, but losing Trevoh Chalobah reduces depth and Alonso’s tactical approach demands defenders who are comfortable defending large spaces as well as building from the back.

The bigger priority may simply be trimming the squad. Chelsea once again have a bloated group, and several fringe players are expected to leave before the deadline as Alonso looks to create a more streamlined dressing room.

One to watch at Chelsea

Morgan Rogers.

The England international arrives carrying the weight of a British-record transfer fee, but he also looks perfectly suited to Alonso’s system.

Capable of playing through the middle, off either flank or behind the striker, Rogers offers power, creativity and ball-carrying ability that Chelsea lacked at times last season.

If he settles quickly, he has every chance of becoming one of the Premier League’s standout attacking players.

Prediction for Chelsea in the 2026/27 Premier League

Chelsea should improve significantly under Alonso.

There is finally a manager with a clearly defined tactical identity and the quality of the squad is undeniable.

The lack of European football could also prove a major advantage, allowing Chelsea to focus solely on domestic competitions while many of their rivals juggle continental commitments.

A title challenge may come a season too early given the volume of new arrivals, but Chelsea look well placed to return to the Champions League places.

101 Great Goals Prediction: 4th

articles.title: Former Man United and Barcelona star Depay vows to take action after Corinthians backtrack on contract offer
articles.summary: Memphis Depay is looking for a new club after a contract extension with Corinthians was taken off the table
articles.content:
Former Man United and Barcelona star Depay vows to take action after Corinthians backtrack on contract offer

Memphis Depay is looking for a new club after a contract extension with Corinthians was taken off the table

Last Update:

Memphis Depay has hit out at Corinthians, calling their behaviour “unacceptable” after the Brazilian club withdrew a planned contract extension.

The Netherlands forward, who remains the Orange’s leading goalscorer, joined Corinthians on a two-year deal in 2024 and Depay claims there was an agreement in place for their relationship to continue into next year.

However,  Corinthians have now backtracked citing financial concerns, and the 32-year-old was unimpressed.

He wrote on social media: “This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department. Some people decided however to breach this engagement.

“I didn’t want this situation and always respected the club throughout the process, but now I am forced to react strongly in order to preserve my interests.

“In the upcoming days I will speak publicly but rest assured that I will not leave this unacceptable behaviour unsanctioned.”

Corinthians defend Depay snub

Former Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and Manchester United forward Depay has scored 20 goals in 79 appearances for Corinthians, helping them win the Copa do Brasil and the Supercopa do Brasil.

But a statement confirmed he would not be remaining with the Sao Paulo club.

It read: “Corinthians has decided not to renew the contract of athlete Memphis Depay. This decision was made solely and exclusively in consideration of the financial health of our institution, which demands a rigorous balance and responsibility in the management of available resources.

“We would like to express our deep gratitude to the player Memphis Depay and his entire team, who since the beginning of the negotiations have sought the best possible agreement.

“It became clear that taking on a new commitment of this magnitude would not be compatible with the financial balance we need to preserve to ensure the institution’s sustainability.

“We recognise that this was a difficult decision, but it was undoubtedly necessary for the future of Corinthians.”

BREAKING: Chelsea complete deal for Pep Chavarria

Chelsea have added another player to their already bloated squad by signing defender Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano

Last Update:

Chelsea have completed the signing of left-back Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano for a fee of £16.2million.

The 28-year-old is the replacement for fellow Spaniard Marc Cucurella who left Stamford Bridge for Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chavarria has signed a five-year contract after making his name with Real Zaragoza and then becoming a key part of a Rayo side that secured successive eighth-placed finishes in La Liga and qualified for last season’s Conference League final.

Table of Contents

Slow burner Chavarria excited by Chelsea move

Chavarria has not taken the typical path to the Premier League but he is delighted to have secured a move to the West London club.

He told Chelsea’s official website: “I’m so excited to get started. This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success.

“There are a lot of people who have helped me get to this moment and I have to thank my family. They have always supported me and today is only possible because of them.”

Chavarria joins an already bloated Chelsea squad

New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has not been slow in adding to an already swollen squad that contains 41 players.

Chavarria is the club’s ninth addition this summer and will compete with Jorrel Hato to start on the left of Chelsea’s back four while Marco Palestra, another new signing, can play on both flanks.

Alonso has presided over a mixed pre-season campaign with two wins from five games on their tour of Asia. Chelsea take on Real Sociedad at the weekend in their final tune-up before opening their Premier League campaign at West London neighbours on Monday, August 24.

articles.title: Manchester United: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Carrick’s men challenge for the title?
articles.summary: While many of their top-four challengers start the season with new managers, Manchester United have opted for continuity under Michael Carrick. They finished third last season. Can they go two better in 2026/27?
articles.content:
Manchester United: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Carrick’s men challenge for the title?

While many of their top-four challengers start the season with new managers, Manchester United have opted for continuity under Michael Carrick. They finished third last season. Can they go two better in 2026/27?

Last Update:

Even the most ardent Manchester United fan would have struggled to foresee the huge impact Michael Carrick would have on the club following his arrival as interim coach in January.

United were seventh when he succeeded Ruben Amorim on a temporary basis but a remarkable run of form saw them finish in third place, marking a return to the Champions League following a two-year absence.

That achievement meant it was impossible for the United hierarchy to look elsewhere and Carrick was duly given the job on a permanent basis. With his feet under the table, the hard works starts now for the 45-year-old as he looks to bolster his squad.

Midfield was clearly an area of concern, especially with Casemiro departing, and the signings of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans appear solid, if slightly unspectacular, additions.

Tynan Thompson has arrived from Tottenham but he is one for the future, meaning United’s problem area in defence has still to be addressed.

Harry Maguire enjoyed a resurgence under Carrick but he is now 33 while Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martinez seem to spend as much time on the treatment table as they do the pitch.

Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven both have potential but former United hero Paul Scholes would like to see a top-class centre-half brought in.

He told The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast: “I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing]. You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You’d like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

“Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They’ve got the young lad Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he’s still going to make mistakes. He’s young.

“Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league].”

Further forward, there is the Marcus Rashford conundrum.

The England winger has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 following a falling out with Amorim and has spent the past 18 months on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

He proved his match-changing ability at Camp Nou once again and, if Carrick can get a tune out of the 28-year-old and rekindle his hunger to pull on the red shirt, then Rashford would enhance any team in world football.

It is also a big season for Benjamin Sesko. The Slovenian arrived 12 months ago and a disrupted pre-season meant he never got in a rhythm, despite ending the 2025/26 campaign as the club’s joint top-scorer in the league.

Sesko was a prolific marksman during his time at Salzburg and RB Leipzig and if he can hit the goals trail then United could be in for a strong season both domestically and in Europe.

Good enough to win the league? Probably not but a top-four spot ought to be a certainty.

Table of Contents

Summer Ins and Outs at Manchester United

IN

Karl Darlow – free agent

Andrey Santos from Chelsea – £48m

Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa – £35m

Tynan Thompson from Tottenham – £4m

OUT

Altay Bayndir to Celta Vigo – season-long loan

Andre Onana to Trabzonspor – season-long loan

Casemiro – free agent

Jadon Sancho – free agent

Rasmus Hojlund to Napoli – £43m

Tyrell Malacia – free agent

Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough – £14m

What do Manchester United need before the window closes?

As mentioned, a central defender is likely to top Carrick’s list.

It wouldn’t be a surprise to see a move for a right-back either with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui fairly uninspiring options.

United also have just one centre-forward in Sesko. But with Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha both able to play in the number nine role, Carrick may opt to deploy funds elsewhere.

One to watch at Manchester United

Shea Lacey has impressed in pre-season while 15-year-old JJ Gabriel has already been tipped as a future superstar at Old Trafford. But we’re going to go with a more familiar name who lost his way a touch last season: Amad Diallo.

Having made a name for himself with a series of sparkling displays in the 2024/25 campaign, the Ivory Coast winger struggled to replicate that form last season, scoring twice and adding three assists in 32 Premier League games. The talent is there, as shown again at the World Cup. Expect big things this year from the 24-year-old.

Prediction for Manchester United in the 2026/27 Premier League

It’s tough to see United slugging it out for the title with the likes of Arsenal and Manchester City. But with Liverpool and Chelsea starting the season under new leadership, it is not difficult to see Carrick’s side being the best of the rest.

101 Great Goals Prediction: 3rd

Tottenham third kit 26/27: Watch Sandro Tonali video as Spurs launch new shirt

All you need to know about Tottenham's 2026/27 third kit

Last Update:

Premier League side Tottenham have unveiled their new third shirt as part of the club’s kit for the 2026/27 season.

The release, which was announced in August, was launched by a campaign entitled ‘Driven by Belief’ and featured club-record signing Sandro Tonali.

Spurs stars Victoria Pelova, Amanda Nilden, Signe Gaupset and Jun’ai Byfield were among the players joining Tonali to unveil the design.

The club say the kit is “ready for a new era” as head coach Roberto De Zerbi takes charge at the start of a season for the first time, having joined in March and sealed safety for his side on the final day of 2025/26.

Table of Contents

Tottenham third kit 2026/27 full design details

The Nike kit is inspired by Tottenham’s purple away shirts between 1994 and 1999, a period that culminated in the club winning the EFL Cup, although they wore white in the 1998/99 final against Leicester City.

Premier League icons to have donned the shirt include Ian Walker, Gary Mabbutt, Darren Anderton and prolific strikers Jurgen Klinsmann, Teddy Sheringham and Les Ferdinand.

Spurs say the kit represents a “vision for the future” of a “highly anticipated” new season featuring “exciting” additions across both squads.

Playmaker Tonali, defender Nilden and midfielders Pelova and Gaupset are shown “putting in work” behind the scenes before “entering the big stage”.

How to buy Spurs 26/27 third kit

The kit is available from Tottenham’s online shop along with the club’s new home and away shirts, which were released in June.

How much does the 26/27 Tottenham third kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Tottenham replica shirt is £90 or £135 for the elite version, which is described as the “exact authentic design worn by the players at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium”.

Youth shirts start at £70. A baby kit is available for £55. The shorts cost between £35 and £50.

Accompanying socks cost £20. Name and number printing is available at extra cost and was free for child kits at the time of release.

When does Spurs’ 2026/27 Premier League season start?

Tottenham start away in London as they aim to improve on consecutive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League, losing 39 top-flight matches along the way. Here are the key details.

articles.title: Emery: ‘Don’t compare Villa with Man City, Chelsea, Man United, Liverpool or Arsenal’
articles.summary: Aston Villa face PSG in the Super Cup 2026 on Wednesday
articles.content:
Emery: ‘Don’t compare Villa with Man City, Chelsea, Man United, Liverpool or Arsenal’

Aston Villa face PSG in the Super Cup 2026 on Wednesday

Last Update:

Head coach Unai Emery says Aston Villa will not be at “our best” against Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup 2026 and has dismissed talk of the Europa League holders rivalling some of the richest clubs in the Premier League.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, defender Ezri Konsa and striker Ollie Watkins have not travelled with the Villans to Salzburg for the game against the Champions League winners as the trio recover from the World Cup while their teammates build towards the new top-flight season.

“If they were here, maybe we would have more chances,” said Emery. “If we are comparing with teams like Manchester City, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool or Arsenal, we are competing with them but we don’t have the power yet.”

Table of Contents

Aston Villa: Why Emery downplays Premier League standing

In Emery’s three full seasons in charge, Villa have risen from top-flight also-rans to two fourth-placed finishes either side of one in sixth place.

The Spaniard guided them to the Conference League semi-finals and Champions League quarter-finals before winning the Europa League in style last season.

Despite that success – and finishing above Liverpool and Chelsea – Emery endured two difficult spells in 2025/26 when Villa failed to win any of their first five matches and took nine points from 10 games between January and March.

“We achieved the objective after a very difficult season,” reflected the 54-year-old. “In August, we had a very difficult moment.

“One thing I appreciate is to be happy with the way we are doing [things] – don’t compare us with other teams or clubs.

“Sometimes they are over us, sometimes they are under us. Keep going, keep being resilient in bad moments, like we showed last year.”

Super Cup 2026: PSG ‘favourites’ vs Aston Villa

PSG are the most feared team in Europe after becoming European champions in consecutive campaigns but Emery says lifting the trophy would be “a special moment”.

“I am looking forward to playing,” added Emery, calling the match a “test” against opponents he regards as “favourites”.

“We are having a good pre-season. [This match is] very important for our careers as a coach, as players, as a club – it’s a trophy.

“It’s one thing that can make us proud of how we are and how we got here. We can have a huge motivation to achieve our best.

“[The] 6,000 supporters from Birmingham give us the responsibility as well to try to play for them. We are going to compete.”

When is the Super Cup 2026? Date, kick off time

The match takes place at Salzburg’s RB Arena on Wednesday, August 12 at 20:00 BST (15:00 ET / 12:00 PT).

Where to watch the Super Cup: TV channel, live online stream

In the UK, live coverage is on TNT Sports 1 and TNT Sports Ultimate, with streaming on HBO Max.

Vitinha votes for outsider trio as Ballon d’Or winners: ‘It would be normal’

Vitinha discussed the Ballon d'Or before the Super Cup 2026

Last Update:

Vitinha says he would favour “a Parisian” in the Ballon d’Or vote by voting for three Paris Saint-Germain outsiders to win the most prestigious prize in football.

While the likes of Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Rodri are favourites for this year’s award, midfielder Vitinha believes PSG’s Fabian Ruiz, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia or Ousmane Dembele deserve the trophy.

“There are a lot of good players who can win this year,” said the Portugal international, via PSG’s website.

“For me, it would be normal for a PSG player to win it like Khvicha Kvaratskhelia after his Champions League season, Ousmane Dembele after his great season or Fabian Ruiz, who has won everything.

“I vote for a Parisian.”

Table of Contents

Ballon d’Or 2026: Who are the favourites?

Here’s the top 10 likeliest Ballon d’Or winners according to bookmakers on August 11 2026.

Why Fabian Ruiz, Dembele, Kvaratskhelia could win Ballon d’Or

Midfielder Fabian Ruiz has embellished his trophy cabinet like no other player since 2024, playing a key part in PSG’s consecutive Champions League trophies, as well as EURO 2024 and World Cup 2026 glory for Spain.

Having been the Player of the Season in the Champions League when Paris won their first-ever title in 2024/25, prolific France forward Dembele scored eight times in 13 appearances and was named in the Team of the Season as his side retained their trophy.

Dazzling Georgian winger Kvaratskhelia produced an extraordinary 10 goals and seven assists during the 2025/26 Champions League, succeeding Dembele as organisers’ Player of the Season less than 18 months after his debut for the club.

When is the Ballon d’Or 2026?

The 70th edition of ceremony will take place on October 26 2026 in London. Dembele is the holder.

Super Cup 2026: PSG ‘eager’, says Vitinha

PSG face Europa League holders Aston Villa in the Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday, having beaten Tottenham on penalties in last season’s showpiece.

“We are eager to play this game and know it’s not just a win, but a trophy,” Vitinha told UEFA.

“We’ve been making history but we have hunger to do more and we know it’s very difficult to play these types of games. We’re going to take advantage of it.”

The match starts at 20:00 BST (15:00 ET / 12:00 PT). In the UK, live coverage is on TNT Sports 1 and TNT Sports Ultimate, with streaming on HBO Max.

articles.title: Arsenal: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can the Gunners go back to back?
articles.summary: Arsenal head into the new Premier League season as the team to beat. But will Mikel Arteta's men retain their crown after a slightly underwhelming summer?
articles.content:
Arsenal: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can the Gunners go back to back?

Arsenal head into the new Premier League season as the team to beat. But will Mikel Arteta's men retain their crown after a slightly underwhelming summer?

Last Update:

After a 22-year wait to be crowned champions of England, Arsenal have a unique opportunity to go back to back.

The Gunners may not thrill with a style of football centred around defensive solidity and set-piece excellence but they were deserving winners in 2025/26 as Mikel Arteta justified the club’s decision to stick with him despite several near misses.

Arteta is now the longest-serving manager in the top flight and will start his seventh season in charge with a home game against newly promoted Coventry on August 21.

His longevity provides a stability not seen in the majority of Arsenal’s title rivals with Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea all starting the season with new men at the helm.

That’s not to say it has been a perfect summer for the red half of North London. The chance to make a statement signing in Vinicius Jr came and went with the winger opting to remain at Real Madrid. Had the Brazilian swapped the Santiago Bernabeu for the Emirates, it would have been the ultimate indication of Arsenal’s ambition to become the best side in Europe.

You could argue they came close last term, reaching the Champions League final, but a dreadfully timid display in losing to Paris Saint-Germain illustrated a lack of belief that they can cut it with the continent’s elite.

They could find a route to European success blocked once again with PSG’s young side looking seemingly invincible but matters should be more straightforward domestically.

Arsenal go into the season as favourites and with some justification, although you could make a case they will start the 2026/27 campaign weaker than they finished the last one.

France international, and defensive lynchpin, William Saliba is sidelined for an indefinite period with a back problem, meaning his formidable partnership with Gabriel will be put on hold.

Leandro Trossard has also departed. The Belgian was an unsung hero of the title triumph, scoring vital goals at important times, none more so than his late strike at West Ham in May.

Christos Tzolis is his replacement and, while he has made a good early impression, he is likely to require a period of adaptation from the Belgian Pro League to the physicality of the English top flight.

Bruno Guimaraes has joined from Newcastle but it’s debatable as to whether he strengthens their best XI. He seems more likely to be used as Declan Rice’s replacement when the England international needs a break.

Table of Contents

Summer Ins and Outs

IN

Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle – £75m

Piero Hincapie from Bayer Leverkusen – £45m

Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge – £34m

Illan Meslier – free agent

OUT

Leandro Trossard to Besiktas – £15.3m

Christian Norgaard to Everton – £7m

Jakub Kiwior to Porto – £14.7m

Karl Hein to Werder Bremen – £2.5m

What do Arsenal need before the window closes?

Defensive cover is still required with the long-term availability of Saliba unknown. Arsenal have been linked with John Stones and Ezri Konsa but the former has now joined Inter Milan. Cristhian Mosquera, Hincapie and Riccardo Calafiori can all play in the centre but none bring the same physical qualities as Saliba.

Another left-winger may also be on Arteta’s shortlist given the failed pursuit of Vinicius Jr.

There will likely be several departures with Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira, Ethan Nwaneri and Reiss Nelson all seemingly surplus to requirements.

One to watch at Arsenal

We think this could be the season that Viktor Gyokeres proves he is a 25-goal-a-season striker in the Premier League but the one to watch has to be Max Dowman.

The 16-year-old made fleeting appearances last season but that was enough to mark him out as a star of the future. A pathway to the first-team is not straightforward with England duo Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke both operating in his preferred right-wing slot but that will enable Arteta to introduce him carefully.

Despite his tender years, Dowman has the ability to be a match-changer and he will undoubtedly make his mark over the coming months.

Prediction for Arsenal in the 2026/27 Premier League

It’s difficult to disagree with the bookies: Arsenal are the favourites and for good reason. They could arguably have done more to bolster their squad this summer but their sense of familiarity in the dugout and on the pitch makes them the team to beat.

101 Great Goals Prediction: 1st

articles.title: Former Arsenal defender says swap deal involving Lewis-Skelly and Rashford would benefit all parties
articles.summary: Marcus Rashford has been linked with Arsenal in a deal that would see Myles Lewis-Skelly move in the opposite direction
articles.content:
Former Arsenal defender says swap deal involving Lewis-Skelly and Rashford would benefit all parties

Marcus Rashford has been linked with Arsenal in a deal that would see Myles Lewis-Skelly move in the opposite direction

Last Update:

Former Arsenal defender Lee Dixon believes a deal that would see Marcus Rashford and Myles Lewis-Skelly swap clubs would benefit all parties.

Manchester United forward Rashford is back at Old Trafford after loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona and could make his first appearance for his boyhood club since December 2024 in Wednesday night’s friendly against Leeds in Dublin.

His long-term future remains uncertain, however, leading to speculation he could make a late move away from Old Trafford before the transfer window closes on September 1.

Lewis-Skelly could also be heading out of the exit door following Arsenal’s capture of former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes. The 19-year-old played in midfield to great effect towards the end of last season and can also operate on the left of a back four.

Lewis-Skelly has been linked with United and with Arsenal needing a left-sided forward following their failed pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr, it has been suggested the two players could change clubs this summer.

Dixon, who made over 450 appearances for the North London club and won the league title four times, believes it’s a rare case of an exchange deal that would suit both the players and clubs involved.

He told BestBettingSites: “Would I swap them? You know what, I probably would. And that’s nothing against Myles Lewis-Skelly; it’s about giving him the freedom to go and expand his game elsewhere.

“With Marcus Rashford, he’s a player who needs an arm around his shoulder, and [Arsenal boss Mikel] Arteta would be great for him. Give him that love, give him the freedom to play on that left side, and yeah, I’d like to see him in an Arsenal shirt.

“I have my reservations about whether he’s consistently a top-class player, but based on what Arsenal have in the squad now, he’d be a good addition.”

articles.title: What were they smoking? Former Chelsea star Mikel mocks Arsenal fans for thinking they could sign Vinicius Jr
articles.summary: Jon Obi Mikel says one Premier League triumph in 22 years does not make Arsenal a big club and has mocked their fans for thinking Vinicius Jr would ever move to the Emirates
articles.content:
What were they smoking? Former Chelsea star Mikel mocks Arsenal fans for thinking they could sign Vinicius Jr

Jon Obi Mikel says one Premier League triumph in 22 years does not make Arsenal a big club and has mocked their fans for thinking Vinicius Jr would ever move to the Emirates

Last Update:

Former Chelsea midfielder Jon Obi Mikel has mocked Arsenal supporters for thinking they could sign Vinicius Jr and insisted the Gunners are not one of the game’s “big boys”.

Arsenal publicly pursued Vinicius Jr this summer while he engaged in a stand off with Real Madrid over a new contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Fans of the North London club, who clinched the Premier League title for the first time since 2004 last season, were excited at the possibility of the Brazil superstar moving to the Emirates but their hopes were dashed when the winger signed a new six-year deal at Madrid last week.

And Mikel, who made nearly 250 appearances for Arsenal’s London rivals Chelsea, was quick to stick the boot in.

He told The Obi One Podcast: “I don’t know what the Arsenal fans were expecting.

“You win the league after 22 years and then you all of a sudden think: that’s it, you’ve arrived, you’re one of the big boys again. No, you’re not.

“They’ve just been humbled because I said it: there’s no way Vinicius Junior is leaving Real Madrid to go to Arsenal, a club that’s won one title in 22 years. This guy wins titles, he’s won lots of titles at Real Madrid. He wants to win titles season after season, the Champions League, La Liga, competing year after year and winning those titles.

“He’s tasted what it feels like winning the Champions League, Arsenal have never won the Champions League. Zero.

“You expect a player who has won the Champions League with Real Madrid to leave that, everything that he’s built at Real Madrid, and the squad that Jose Mourinho is assembling right now? They look to me like a team that at the end of the season, you probably see them in the Champions League final.

“There’s some team there at Real Madrid when you look at the players that they have. You expect him to leave that and go to a team that has won one league title in 22 years? F***ing hell.”

‘Vinicius Jr was just using Arsenal’

Mikel repeated his claim that Vinicius Jr was merely using Arsenal’s interest to get an improved deal at Madrid.

He added: “All the Arsenal fans when I said that before, in my DMs, I saw messages, ‘We’ve clipped this, we’ve sent this video, and when it happens we’re absolutely going to come on here and destroy you…’

“I was looking at it and thinking that’s just my opinion. I never thought he was going to leave.

“He was using you guys [Arsenal] to get a better deal, he was using them to get a better deal. I have no idea why Arsenal fans would genuinely believe that Vinicius Junior was going to go from Real Madrid to Arsenal. If you ask anybody… I think it was only Arsenal fans who believed that was going to happen. I don’t know what they were smoking.”

Arsenal have signed Greece winger Christos Tzolis to replace the departed Leandro Trossard on the left of their attack. Their summer recruitment has also included moves for former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes and ex-Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

articles.summary: Wembley is in use so the curtain raiser will head down the M4
articles.content:
Why has the Community Shield between Manchester City and Arsenal been switched from Wembley to Cardiff?

Wembley is in use so the curtain raiser will head down the M4

Last Update:

The 2026 Community Shield will not be played at its usual home of Wembley this Sunday with the game instead taking place 150 miles away in Cardiff.

The season’s ‘traditional curtain raiser’, which this year will be contested by FA Cup winners Manchester City and Premier League champions Arsenal, has had to be switched.

Wembley has already been booked and so the teams and fans will re-locate to the Welsh capital.

An FA statement read: “The 2026 FA Community Shield will be played at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday 16 August.

“The ‘curtain raiser’ for the new football season is traditionally played on the weekend before the Premier League begins.

“Due to alterations to the 2026-27 football calendar, next season’s Premier League will begin over the weekend of Saturday 22 August, and Wembley Stadium connected by EE is unavailable on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August due to pre-planned concerts.”

Table of Contents

Who is performing at Wembley?

Wembley has already been booked for Canadian singer-songwriter The Weeknd.

The R&B artist, whose real name is Abel Makkonen Tesfaye, will perform in London for five nights, from August 14 to August 19.

It means the FA will again use Cardiff as its base as it did when Wembley was being refurbished.

The statement added: “The Welsh national stadium has a rich history of hosting major football events, including the FA Community Shield on six occasions between 2001 and 2006, and it provides a neutral venue for the competing clubs as well as one of the largest capacities in the United Kingdom for fans to attend.”

Where to watch the Community Shield

Manchester City versus Arsenal kicks off at 3pm on Sunday afternoon.

You can watch it on TNT Sports 1 and stream via HBO Max.

articles.title: Manchester City: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Enzo Maresca bring the title back to the Etihad?
articles.summary: Manchester City enter a new era without Pep Guardiola at the helm. Can they dethrone Arsenal and win back the Premier League title?
articles.content:
Manchester City: Season preview, ins and outs, one to watch and prediction – can Enzo Maresca bring the title back to the Etihad?

Manchester City enter a new era without Pep Guardiola at the helm. Can they dethrone Arsenal and win back the Premier League title?

Last Update:

Manchester City’s first season without Pep Guardiola for more than a decade marks the beginning of a new era.

After Arsenal ended their wait for a Premier League title last season, the club acted quickly by appointing former assistant and ex-Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, who arrives with the task of restoring the Cityzens’ domestic dominance.

Guardiola departed having transformed City into one of the greatest sides English football has ever seen, but despite lifting both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup last term, finishing second in the league was viewed as falling short of expectations.

Maresca inherits a squad still packed with elite talent, led by Erling Haaland, who once again finished among Europe’s most prolific goalscorers, but this summer has also highlighted the need for evolution rather than revolution.

The headline arrival has been Elliot Anderson in a £116m move from Nottingham Forest, with the England midfielder viewed as the long-term heartbeat of City’s midfield. Youngsters Jeremy Monga and Pierce Charles have also arrived, while further reinforcements could yet follow before the transfer window closes.

There have been notable departures, too. James Trafford has moved to Leeds United, John Stones and Bernardo Silva have both left as free agents as well.

The biggest storyline, however, surrounds Rodri. Barcelona continue to pursue the Ballon d’Or winner and City are already working on a deal for Lille wonderkid Ayyoub Bouaddi in anticipation of a possible exit.

Losing Rodri would undoubtedly change the complexion of City’s season and remains the key issue to resolve before deadline day.

Even so, there is optimism around Maresca’s appointment. He knows the club inside out, understands Guardiola’s principles and has already shown during his managerial career that he is capable of implementing an attractive possession-based style while adding his own tactical ideas.

Table of Contents

Summer Ins and Outs

IN

Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest – £116m

Jeremy Monga from Leicester City – £10m

Pierce Charles from Sheffield Wednesday – £3m

Mathys Detourbet from Troyes – undisclosed

OUT

James Trafford to Leeds United – £40m

Nathan Ake to Fenerbahce – £8.5m

Manuel Akanji to Inter Milan – undisclosed

Reigan Heskey to Cologne – £6m

Jahmai Simpson-Pusey to Cologne – undisclosed

John Stones to Inter Milan – free

Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid – free

What do Manchester City need before the window closes?

Everything depends on Rodri’s future.

If the Spain international remains, City’s midfield already looks among the strongest in Europe with Anderson, Nico Gonzalez, Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovacic providing support.

Should Rodri leave, though, replacing arguably the world’s best holding midfielder becomes almost impossible.

Bouaddi is an outstanding young talent and City are pushing hard to complete a deal, but expecting an 18-year-old to immediately fill Rodri’s boots would be unrealistic.

Additional defensive cover may also be required following the departures of Stones.

One to watch at Manchester City

Elliot Anderson.

The £116m price tag inevitably brings pressure, but the England midfielder looks tailor-made for Maresca’s system.

His energy, ball-carrying ability and intelligence without possession should allow him to thrive alongside City’s established stars.

Whether he becomes Rodri’s long-term midfield partner or eventually his successor, Anderson appears set to become one of the Premier League’s best midfielders over the coming years.

Prediction for Manchester City in the 2026/27 Premier League

Replacing Guardiola was never going to be easy, but City have appointed someone who knows exactly how the club operates.

Maresca inherits one of the league’s strongest squads and, provided Rodri stays, there is every reason to believe City will mount another serious title challenge.

However, Arsenal remain the benchmark after last season and their continuity could prove to be the difference over 38 matches.

101 Great Goals Prediction: 2nd

articles.title: Johnson completes move to Everton with McNeil heading to Crystal Palace
articles.summary: Brennan Johnson's unhappy at spell at Crystal Palace is done and he is now an Everton player
articles.content:
Johnson completes move to Everton with McNeil heading to Crystal Palace

Brennan Johnson's unhappy at spell at Crystal Palace is done and he is now an Everton player

Last Update:

Brennan Johnson has outlined his reasons for joining Everton after completing his switch from Crystal Palace.

Johnson has moved to Merseyside with Dwight McNeil going in the opposite direction, bringing an end to his unhappy eight-month spell at Selhurst Park.

The Wales international joined Palace for £35m from Tottenham but failed to make much of an impression and the Eagles were happy to cut their losses and take a chance on long-time target McNeil instead.

Palace’s loss could be Everton’s gain with the 25-year-old excited at the move to the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

He told evertontv: “I’m so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it’s a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

“I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I’ve shown previously, and that’s a massive thing for me – the fact he knows and believes in what I can do. For me, listening to him – a manager who is so experienced and someone who has been so successful – it was really nice to hear.

“I want to bring all of my attributes. First and foremost, I’ll work for the team, the fans, and represent the club properly. I know that’s something that’s definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I’ve got.

“The incredible fanbase that Everton has, whether it’s home or away, is something I’ve always felt. It’s a massive honour to be here and play for them now.”

McNeil leaves Everton for Palace

McNeil leaves Everton after making 128 appearances, scoring 15 goals.

The 26-year-old will now continue his career in South London.

He told the club’s official website: “I’m really happy to be here, and looking forward to the challenge ahead.

“The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.”

articles.title: Diomande’s former boss confident teenager can thrive on the right and form deadly trident at Real Madrid with Vinicius and Mbappe
articles.summary: Yan Diomande has been backed to shine at Real Madrid, by the man who gave him his La Liga debut 18 months ago
articles.content:
Diomande’s former boss confident teenager can thrive on the right and form deadly trident at Real Madrid with Vinicius and Mbappe

Yan Diomande has been backed to shine at Real Madrid, by the man who gave him his La Liga debut 18 months ago

Last Update:

Yan Diomande’s former coach Borja Jimenez has backed the Ivorian to be a success at Real Madrid and says he will have no problem in switching to the right side and forming a new-look front three with Vinicius Jr and Kylian Mbappe.

The 19-year-old joined Madrid last week from RB Leipzig for a club-record fee of £107million that could rise further with add-ons, signing a seven-year deal at the Santiago Bernabeu.

It was another step in a remarkable rise to prominence with Diomande only making his senior debut 18 months ago, for Leganes against Madrid in March 2025.

A move to Germany followed, with Diomande scoring 13 goals and adding nine assists in 37 games in all competitions.

He will now be thrust into the limelight in the Spanish capital but Jimenez is confident his protege can handle the step-up.

Table of Contents

We knew Diomande was special, says Jimenez

He told AS: “Even in Yan’s first training session, you could see an individual talent that could do things that were of another level. That first week showed it was not an isolated event but that he had an enormous capacity for improvement.

“We then carried out specific work after training focused on his decision-making and understanding the game, which is where he adapted the fastest.

“In the end, our job was to simplify things: I told him that when he had the ball at his feet, he decided. My job was to get him the ball in the best way so that he could exploit his innate talent.

“From the first week we knew that he was special and that he was going to contribute to us from the first day. At the end of the year I said publicly that in one or two years his value would double or triple, and the truth is that I have fallen short, because it has multiplied by five or six times.

“Those of us who are in day-to-day football and have been training for 10 or 12 years, we were very clear that Yan possessed totally different qualities.”

Diomande will thrive on the right at Real Madrid – Jimenez

Vinicius Jr’s decision to renew his contract after months of speculation means the position on the left of Madrid’s attack belongs to the Brazilian but Jimenez says Diomande will have no problem in switching to the right.

He added: “I would say that 70% of his minutes in Germany were played on the right wing. It is true that with us [Leganes] the vast majority of his minutes were on the left, but with Ivory Coast in the World Cup we have seen him appear frequently on the right.

“He won’t have any problem playing on either side.”

A move from Leipzig to the goldfish bowl of Madrid is another issue that Diomande will have to cope with but Jimenez insists the teenager will take it all in his stride.

He added: “Yan is made differently and transmits an incredible hunger. It is evident that at Real Madrid he will quickly realise that the demand and media overexposure have nothing to do with what he has lived so far, but he fully trusts in his ability to show that he is a different player.

“Time will tell, but there were doubts about his performance in Germany and he ended up being chosen as the best young player. There were also doubts about his role in the World Cup and he showed that he is very good. I think the same thing will happen in Madrid, despite the environment. I have no doubt that from the first day he will lift the Bernabéu with his game.”

articles.title: Trump says ‘fantastic’ Infantino should remain FIFA chief
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump says critics need to lay of FIFA chief Gianni Infantino
articles.content:
Trump says ‘fantastic’ Infantino should remain FIFA chief

US president Donald Trump says critics need to lay of FIFA chief Gianni Infantino

Last Update:

Donald Trump has described embattled FIFA chief Gianni Infantino as “fantastic” and said ousting him would be a “terrible mistake”.

Infantino continues to cling on to his job despite the controversy surrounding his now abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme that proposed to sell off just over 20% of commercial rights to the organisation’s major tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cup.

The Swiss managed to retain the support of FIFA last week but that has not changed the opinion of some of the game’s major confederations with UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC writing an open letter on Monday that accused Infantino of breaking trust “through deception”.

US president Trump, who was awarded FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize by Infantino prior to the hosting of the World Cup in the United States, as well as Canada and Mexico, says critics need to lay off.

He wrote on Truth Social: “FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again.”

Had FFE gone ahead, the investor group would have been led by Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared.

Table of Contents

Confederations maintain pressure on Infantino to go

The support of the US president will have little influence on those looking to get rid of Infantino.

The letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC made clear their desire for change.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” it read.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.”

Reports claim the letter should be viewed as an opportunity for Infantino to resign voluntarily and leave office with dignity.

FIFA hits back and backs Infantino

FIFA came out fighting at the weekend, accusing critics of conducting a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine both the organisation and its president.

But the three confederations argued FIFA’s subsequent apology over the handling of the FFE proposal failed to address the central issue.

“It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong,” the letter said.

“There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgement.

“Not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve.”

Although FIFA has pledged to present a report on the episode at the next FIFA Council meeting, expected in October, the three confederations insist any investigation must be conducted independently.

“It fails to recognise that proper governance in the face of such a profound lack of judgement would require that such a review be conducted by a fully independent third party,” the letter added.

articles.title: Tottenham: Micky van de Ven signs new five-year contract
articles.summary: Van de Ven made 45 appearances for Spurs last season
articles.content:
Tottenham: Micky van de Ven signs new five-year contract

Van de Ven made 45 appearances for Spurs last season

Last Update:

Tottenham defender Micky van de Ven has signed a new contract with the club.

Van de Ven has been a key player since joining from Wolfsburg in 2023, with his previous deal expiring in 2029. His new deal reportedly runs until 2031 and will see him earn a signifcant increase in salary.

The Netherlands defender was rumoured to be seeking a departure from North London towards the end of last season after narrowly avoiding relegation, but his new contract will be a show of faith in the club’s direction under manager Roberto De Zerbi.

He said: “It’s a special moment to sign a new deal and a proud moment for me and my family.

“I’ve always loved Spurs, from the first day I stepped in here. I love the club, I love the fans and I’ve developed really well here.

“It’s clear the direction the club wants to go in and I want to be a part of it. I’m excited about what’s to come.”

Van de Ven ‘one of the best centre-backs in Europe’ claims Tottenham boss De Zerbi

Van de Ven is approaching 100 games for Spurs and was part of the side who won the Europa League in 2025, with his later bicycle kick clearance off the line helping them beat Manchester United 1-0.

Roberto De Zerbi added: “Micky is one of the best centre-backs in Europe and an important player for us.

“He has the qualities, mentality and ambition that we want at Tottenham Hotspur, and I am very happy that he has decided to continue his journey with the club.

“We are building something strong here, and players like Micky are an important part of that future. His decision to sign a new contract shows his belief in what we are creating together.”

articles.title: Endrick set to remain at Real Madrid after Aston Villa links
articles.summary: Endrick is set to be part of Jose Mourinho's plans at Real Madrid
articles.content:
Endrick set to remain at Real Madrid after Aston Villa links

Endrick is set to be part of Jose Mourinho's plans at Real Madrid

Last Update:

Endrick is set to remain at Real Madrid this season despite interest from a number of European clubs including Aston Villa, according to The Athletic.

The Brazilian youngster had been strongly linked with a loan exit from the Bernabeu, with Unai Emery’s Villa reported to be long-term admirers who were exploring a potential move.

But Endrick, who enjoyed a promising loan at Ligue 1 side Lyon last term, is now set to remain with Los Blancos and will enjoy more of a first-team role under Jose Mourinho.

The former Palmeiras youngster is set to have more opportunities on the right-hand side this season, with Mourinho not viewing Bernardo Silva or Federico Valverde as regular options there.

He can also operate as an alternative central striker option to Kylian Mbappe and new signing Carlos Espi.

Endrick could still leave in January, according to the report, just as he did last season when he scored eight goals in 21 appearances in all competitions.

Overall, he has featured 40 times for Madrid since joining for €35million in 2023, scoring seven times.
