articles.title: Newcastle boss Jaissle reveals Guimaraes future decided before he arrived
articles.summary: New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says he did not have a choice on Bruno Guimaraes' future.
articles.content:
Newcastle boss Jaissle reveals Guimaraes future decided before he arrived

New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says he did not have a choice on Bruno Guimaraes' future.

Last Update:

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle has admitted Bruno Guimaraes’ departure was already decided before the pair held their first conversation, with the midfielder closing in on a £75 million move to Arsenal.

The Brazilian is expected to complete his long-awaited switch to the Gunners after the two clubs finally reached an agreement, ending his three-year spell at St James’ Park.

Jaissle revealed he only had a brief opportunity to speak with Guimaraes during Newcastle’s training camp in Spain before the midfielder said his goodbyes to team-mates and staff.

“I met him quickly, but the decision was already made,” Jaissle said.

“It was a nice conversation. He’s a fantastic player and a great human being. It’s tough but for him now it’s the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage.

“We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes.”

Guimaraes is set to become the latest high-profile departure from Newcastle, following Anthony Gordon’s move to Barcelona, Sandro Tonali’s switch to Tottenham and Alexander Isak’s transfer to Liverpool over the past year.

Jaissle determined to kickstart new era

Despite the loss of several key players, Jaissle insists Newcastle must embrace the opportunity to begin a new era.

“This is a challenge and there are so many transitions at the moment,” he said.

“Many big players left – legends of the club – but we need to see it as a chance.

“Not having too many excuses now, just thinking forward about what we can influence.

“Control the controllables, I used to say, and I’m sure there will be progress this season.”

The Magpies have already spent around £146 million this summer, focusing on young talent from across Europe.

Goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur, and winger Bazoumana Toure have all arrived, with 24-year-old Hornicek the oldest of the club’s new signings.

Jaissle, who previously enjoyed successful spells with RB Salzburg and Al-Ahli, believes he is ready for his first experience in the Premier League.

“This is something I don’t have on my CV, but that’s normal in football,” he said.

“At one point it has to be your first step and I’m now at that moment after being successful in Saudi Arabia and Austria.

“Everyone was dreaming about being a part of the Premier League and now here we are.”

Newcastle begin their 2026-27 Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool on August 23.

articles.summary: Uruguay legend Diego Forlan is the national team's new head coach
articles.content:
Uruguay: World Cup ‘idol’ Diego Forlan named new Celeste manager

Uruguay legend Diego Forlan is the national team's new head coach

Last Update:

Diego Forlan has been named the new head coach of the Uruguay national team following Marcelo Bielsa’s exit in June.

The Celeste failed to advance from the World Cup 2026 group stage, drawing with Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde and losing to Spain.

A Uruguayan FA statement called Forlan “one of the most important figures” in their history, adding that the 47-year-old will also take over the Under-20 team.

La vuelta de la leyenda 😉 pic.twitter.com/cllfYv4aLC

Diego Forlan: Uruguay FA full statement

“Forlan returns to where he left an indelible mark,” added the FA of the 2010 World Cup top scorer and Golden Ball winner.

“A role model, icon, and emblem of an unforgettable generation, the best player of the 2010 South Africa World Cup returns now to contribute his experience, leadership, and profound knowledge of international football from a technical position.

“The new coach will begin working immediately with the under-20 team. There, he will lead a project aimed at developing young talent, supporting their growth, and strengthening their path to the senior national team.

“His first challenge at the helm of the senior national team will come during the September-October international window, when Uruguay plays its FIFA friendly matches. It will mark the beginning of a new era, with one of its greatest idols once again at the helm.

“Having scored 36 goals in 112 appearances for Uruguay, won the Copa America in 2011 and played a decisive role in the historic fourth-place finish in South Africa, Forlan understands the meaning of representing his country like few others.

“His return reaffirms the [association’s] identity, ambition and commitment to a project that combines training, experience, and a strong sense of belonging.”

Diego Forlan’s first game in charge will come against Japan on September 24, before facing South Korea four days later on September 28.

articles.title: UEFA boycott remains in place after FIFA stands behind controversial president Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: FIFA needs to do more to convince UEFA that change will follow after Gianni Infantino was backed to remain as president
articles.content:
UEFA boycott remains in place after FIFA stands behind controversial president Gianni Infantino

FIFA needs to do more to convince UEFA that change will follow after Gianni Infantino was backed to remain as president

Last Update:

UEFA says its boycott of FIFA competitions remains in place and reiterated its lack of confidence in Gianni Infantino.

FIFA is hoping the noise around its embattled president will dissipate after his botched attempt to sell-off stakes in the organisation’s premium events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup, ended in embarrassment and acrimony.

Infantino held talks with FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and members of the FIFA Management Board in the Moroccan city of Rabat yesterday and, while it was admitted that mistakes were made regarding the FFE proposal, the Swiss lawyer was empowered to continue in his role.

That stance has infuriated UEFA, who last week announced its member associations had agreed not to take part in FIFA-organised events until fundamental change had taken place.

In a statement released to 101 Great Goals, UEFA said on Thursday: “UEFA’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

“First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

“These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds.

“Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.”

Table of Contents

What did FIFA say regarding Infantino?

Infantino went to Rabat, essentially, to save his job after the FFE scheme was widely panned by UEFA and fellow confederations AFC (Asia) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean), as well as most commentators.

But he emerged unscathed having received the “full support” of FIFA’s Management Board and, more surprisingly, Grafstrom, who the day before had penned an internal letter to staff that described the last week as a “sad and reproachable series of events.” He also said it created “turmoil which is difficult to comprehend and accept.”

The FIFA statement read: “Following a meeting in Rabat, the FIFA secretary general and members of the FIFA Management Board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for president Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations. In turn, the FIFA president reiterated his full support for the FIFA secretary general and the FIFA Administration for their necessary and outstanding work in the delivery of his vision.

“It was discussed and agreed that the processes, communications and interactions between the president, the secretary general and the FIFA Management Board that support the delivery of this vision can and should always be continuously improved in terms of their effectiveness and efficiency.

“The great work of the FIFA Administration that ensured a successful delivery of the World Cup was acknowledged, and which would not have been possible without the FIFA president, the FIFA secretary general and FIFA Administration speaking as one voice and working as one team.

“In this regard, FIFA’s top management is fully confident that the outcomes of today’s meeting will strengthen FIFA’s governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner while continuing our mission to develop the game around the world.

“The meeting also addressed the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, where mistakes made were acknowledged. It was agreed that it was not the intention for the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations to feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently. It was further acknowledged that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“In a separate letter to the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations, an apology was made for these errors together with a commitment to ensure they do not happen again. A review will now be conducted, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.

“As previously communicated, the FFE proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table. With the project withdrawn, it was agreed that FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation. There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework.

“FIFA will work closely with the relevant stakeholders to examine how it can further support the development of the game through the FIFA Forward programme for the benefit of FIFA’s 211 Member Associations, the Confederations and the Regional Associations.”

What was the FFE proposal?

The initial idea was to sell a percentage of the commercial rights to FIFA’s flagship events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to investors and form a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

FIFA said Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – would lead the investor group.

It had been reported Infantino would become the chief executive of FFE and command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

articles.title: Yan Diomande: Real Madrid complete £107m transfer deal for Leipzig and Ivory Coast winger
articles.summary: All the details as Real Madrid sign Yan Diomande from Leipzig
articles.content:
Yan Diomande: Real Madrid complete £107m transfer deal for Leipzig and Ivory Coast winger

All the details as Real Madrid sign Yan Diomande from Leipzig

Last Update:

Real Madrid have signed Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from Leipzig for an initial £107 million on a seven-year contract.

The fee is the largest ever paid by the 15-time European champions and will include add-ons of around £8.6m, according to the Guardian, who reported that the combined sums will eclipse the total of £115m the club paid Borussia Dortmund for Jude Bellingham in 2023.

Madrid teased Diomande’s arrival via a mock-up of a text exchange in which the 19-year-old told Madrid he was “so excited to be there soon”.

👀📱 pic.twitter.com/a6sjlBBmJV

Table of Contents

Yan Diomande: Why Real Madrid have signed winger

Madrid are lacking wingers and will have been impressed by Diomande’s outstanding season at Leipzig, which saw him end with the Bundesliga Rookie of the Season award.

Lightning-quick Blancos forward Vinicius Junior’s future is also uncertain, with the Brazil international yet to sign an extension to his contract beyond 2027 with Premier League holders Arsenal hovering.

Diomande has long been linked with Madrid but there was a hitch earlier this week when his former agents, Maximal Management – led by ex-Leeds United winger Max Gradel – lodged a complaint with FIFA after it emerged that Roc Nation, founded by rap star Jay-Z, were now looking after the player’s interests.

Leipzig managing director Marcel Schafer also appeared to refer to a post by transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano when he accused “self-proclaimed signing experts” of prematurely reporting the deal had been completed.

Having helped Ivory Coast reach the last 32 at the World Cup 2026, Diomande returned to Leipzig last Monday but had not been training with the squad.

As a deal with Madrid loomed, Leipzig were thought to be trying to ensure Diomande remained injury-free.

Yan Diomande stats

Born in the Ivorian capital of Abidjan, Diomande moved to the US as a 15-year-old and came through the DME Academy in Florida.

La Liga side Leganes signed Diomande in November 2024, giving him his debut in a 3-2 defeat at Madrid the following March.

In Leganes’ penultimate home match of the campaign, Diomande opened his account to help his side beat Espanyol 3-2.

Two months later, Leipzig activated Diomande’s release fee of around £17.2m. A run of goals in three consecutive games opened his Bundesliga account between October and November, followed by a hat-trick at home to Eintracht Frankfurt the following month.

Only five players bettered Diomande’s combined 20 goals and assists in his debut season in the Bundesliga in 2025/26, also winning 75 more duels than anyone else in the division, comfortably leading the way in successful dribbles per match and recording the fifth-highest speed.

Here are some of Diomande’s key figures from last season in all competitions.

Yan Diomande Ivory Coast record

An Ivory Coast debutant in October 2025, Diomande scored in his first two senior international appearances and struck again during a win over Burkina Faso at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

Having scored twice during World Cup qualification and set up a goal against Curacao to send Ivory Coast to the finals, Diomande proved predictably electric at the tournament.

A starter in all four of his country’s matches, Diomande helped The Elephants to an opening win over Ecuador and produced another assist in their victory over Curacao.

When will Yan Diomande play for Real Madrid?

Madrid’s next friendlies are against Ferencvaros on Saturday (18:00 BST) and Deportivo on Wednesday (20:00).

They then take on Schalke on August 16 (16:00) and visit Espanyol in their Liga opener on August 22 (20:30).

articles.summary: Mohamed Salah has joined the third-placed side in last season's Super Lig
articles.content:
Mohamed Salah: Trabzonspor seal Liverpool icon on free transfer

Mohamed Salah has joined the third-placed side in last season's Super Lig

Last Update:

Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor on a two-year deal following his departure from Liverpool.

The Turkish club confirmed the signing on Thursday after Salah arrived in Trabzon a day earlier to complete the move. He will be officially unveiled at Papara Park later on Thursday evening.

Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish Super Lig last season to secure Europa League play-off qualification.

They also lifted the Turkish Cup and will hope Salah’s arrival can strengthen their bid to challenge for a first league title since the 2021-22 campaign.

Salah, 34, ended his Liverpool contract a year early at the end of last season and was mobbed when he wore the Super Lig side’s shirt after landing in Istanbul on Wednesday.

Table of Contents

Mohamed Salah: Premier League icon joins Trabzonspor

Writing on social media in July, Salah’s lawyer and advisor, Ramy Abbas Issa, explained that his client had avoided holding talks “just for the sake of noise”.

Salah left Liverpool after nine years and helped his country make history with their first-ever win at a World Cup before being dramatically ousted by holders Argentina in a last-16 classic at the 2026 edition.

Some bookmakers had offered Besiktas as favourites to sign Salah last month, followed by any other Turkish club.

Saudi clubs had also been considered in the running, with European sides deemed dark horses to lure the former Chelsea, Roma, Basel and Al-Mokawloon player.

Mohamed Salah: Liverpool stats

Salah top-scored in the Premier League as the Reds won the title in 2024/25 in their first season under Arne Slot.

That was the fourth time Salah had been the leading marksman in the English top flight, although he struggled last season and made his dissatisfaction with the doomed Slot clear during Liverpool’s troubled title defence.

A forgettable end to his career at Anfield has done little to diminish Salah’s status as one of the greatest players of all time.

As well as the 2018/19 Champions League, Salah won every major domestic trophy at least once with Liverpool and is their all-time leading contributor of goals and assists in the Premier League.

Only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt have outscored Salah for the club. Here are his key Liverpool stats.

Mohamed Salah salary

Two-time African Footballer of the Year Salah signed a deal in July 2022 making him the highest-paid player in Liverpool’s history.

Abbas Issa told a Harvard Business School study in 2023 that Salah earned at least £1 million a week in total income, boosted by factors such as his lucrative endorsements.

Following months of speculation, Salah signed a new deal until 2027 with Liverpool in April 2025.

When will Mohamed Salah play for Trabzonspor?

Trabzonspor visit Kasimpasa, who finished three points above the relegation zone in last season’s Super Lig, in their 2026/27 opener on August 15 (17:00 BST).

The Black Sea Storm finished five points behind Fenerbahce and eight shy of Galatasaray in 2025/26.

They will be at home in the first leg of the Europa League play-offs on August 20, with their opponents yet to be decided.

articles.content:
Brighton’s Baleba to miss start of the season with injury and closes door on Manchester United move

Carlos Baleba will miss the start of the new Premier League season.

Last Update:

Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba is a doubt for the start of the 2026-27 season after suffering an ankle ligament injury during pre-season.

The Seagulls are hopeful the problem is not a long-term setback, although the Cameroon international is expected to spend a spell on the sidelines.

Baleba missed Brighton’s 4-3 friendly win over Strasbourg on Saturday after sustaining the injury.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side still have pre-season fixtures against Roma and Bologna before beginning their competitive campaign with a UEFA Conference League qualifier against Tromso or CFR Cluj on August 20.

Brighton then host Aston Villa in their opening Premier League match three days later.

The 22-year-old attracted interest from Manchester United towards the end of last season, but a move never materialised.

United had broadly agreed personal terms with Baleba last summer and continued to monitor his progress throughout the 2025-26 campaign before opting to strengthen their midfield with the signings of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans instead.

Baleba made 31 Premier League appearances last season, his third campaign with Brighton following his move from Lille in 2023.

Brighton have been active in the transfer market this summer, bringing in Luka Vuskovic, Michael Svoboda, Pascal Struijk, Costinha and Zadok Yohanna.

articles.content:
BREAKING: Vinicius Junior on verge of signing new Real Madrid contract

Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior is set to stay at the club and sign a new contract amid interest from Arsenal.

Last Update:

Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior is set to sign a new contract at the club amid transfer interest from Arsenal.

According to reports, the Brazilian is on the verge of accepting the new terms provided by the Spanish giants, after two years of negotiations.

With just one year left on his current deal, Vinicius was pushing closer to terms that would see him among the highest-paid players on the planet, alongside team-mate Kylian Mbappe.

And it appears he will get what he is after, and Arsenal’s transfer pursuit of the 26-year-old will end in failure.

It is not all doom and gloom for the Premier League champions, though, as they are set to land Vinicius’ international team-mate, Bruno Guimaraes.

Newcastle have sanctioned the £75million sale of their captain, who will partner Declan Rice in the middle of the park.

For Vinicius Junior, another new era begins under Jose Mourinho.

The Los Blancos boss has reportedly been on the phone to his star winger every day in an attempt to get him to renew his contract, as he looks to bridge the gap between his side and Spanish champions Barcelona.

Much of the concern about the Brazilian’s renewal centred around his image rights, and an initial signing on bonus.

articles.title: Argentina commemorate World Cup win over England with ‘National Football Teams Day’
articles.summary: Argentina have put celebrations in place for their World Cup win over England.
articles.content:
Argentina commemorate World Cup win over England with ‘National Football Teams Day’

Argentina have put celebrations in place for their World Cup win over England.

Last Update:

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has officially declared July 15 as ‘National Football Teams Day’ to commemorate Argentina’s dramatic 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England in 2026.

The decision was approved unanimously during Wednesday’s AFA executive council meeting, with the governing body describing the win as one of the most memorable moments in the country’s football history.

In a statement, the AFA said: “The date was chosen to commemorate the Albiceleste’s great and historic victory over England in the semi-final of the 2026 World Cup.

“The team, led by Lionel Scaloni, were trailing the English side by a single goal but, thanks to goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, managed to turn the result around and send the whole country into a frenzy, with people flooding the streets in celebration.”

Argentina came from behind in the closing stages of the semi-final, scoring twice in the final five minutes to book a place in a second consecutive World Cup final.

Win marred by controversial scenes

The victory was followed by controversy, however, as Argentina’s players unveiled a banner reading “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” (The Malvinas are Argentinian), referring to the Falkland Islands.

The display prompted criticism in England, with the UK government calling on FIFA to investigate the political message.

Argentina went on to lose the World Cup final to Spain, with the match ending in violent scenes that resulted in FIFA opening disciplinary proceedings against Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and assistant coach Roberto Ayala.

The AFA also faced investigations over the Falklands banner, as well as allegations of racist abuse and inappropriate chanting.

Argentina president Javier Milei defended the players’ actions, describing the banner as “perfectly valid” and saying it reflected “a sentiment shared by all Argentines”, although he acknowledged FIFA could impose sanctions.

articles.title: Arsenal receive financial injection after striking new deal with Emirates
articles.summary: Premier League champions Arsenal have signed a lucrative new deal with main sponsor Emirates
articles.content:
Arsenal receive financial injection after striking new deal with Emirates

Premier League champions Arsenal have signed a lucrative new deal with main sponsor Emirates

Last Update:

Arsenal have renewed their sponsorship deal with Emirates, extending the longest front-of-shirt partnership in the Premier League.

The airline’s name will continue to be displayed on the champions’ kit and training gear while they will also hold the club’s stadium naming rights for another seven years.

The new deal will provide significant investment and maintains a partnership that started in 2006 as boss Mikel Arteta looks to strengthen his squad ahead of the new season. The extension is worth a reported £70million a season, an increase on the current £45m.

Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick told the club’s official website: “Winning the Premier League is an incredibly proud moment in our club’s history and one that belongs to everyone connected with Arsenal. Emirates has been an integral part of this success – standing alongside us throughout this journey and sharing in the defining moments, challenges and successes that have shaped our club over the past two decades.

“Winning the title gives us the opportunity to be more ambitious and build on where we are today. Our renewal reflects a shared belief in Arsenal’s future and a shared determination to keep moving forward. The best partnerships, like the best teams, never stand still. Together, we’ll continue to challenge and build on the strong foundations we have built together, with the confidence and ambition that our greatest achievements still lie ahead.”

New Arsenal deal displays mutual trust – commercial chief

Juliet Slot, Arsenal’s chief commercial officer, added: “Our partnership with Emirates has become one of world sport’s most defining. Together we’ve always looked beyond traditional partnership and towards creating experiences that bring supporters closer to Arsenal, finding new ways to connect with our global community.

“Today, we’re in the strongest position we’ve ever been in together. That’s built on two decades of trust, shared ambition and a commitment from us both to keep pushing forward. We’ve built incredibly strong foundations and, as our club enters this exciting new era, I cannot wait to see new history made together.”

Arsenal already boast one of the deepest squads in the top flight but their limitations were exposed on the European stage in May when they were beaten 1-0 by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final.

The Gunners are on the brink of signing Brazil international midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for a fee of £75million while they are believed to have sounded out Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr over a move to North London.

Gavi reveals shocking new pink haircut after fulfilling World Cup pledge

Spain and Barcelona midfielder Gavi has proved a man of his word after ditching his conventional haircut for a radical new look

Gavi to return to Barcelona with interesting new look

articles.title: BREAKING: Barcelona make move for Rodri in bid to beat Real Madrid to Spain captain’s signature
articles.summary: Rodri was expected to join Real Madrid but they now face competition from arch rivals Barcelona
articles.content:
BREAKING: Barcelona make move for Rodri in bid to beat Real Madrid to Spain captain’s signature

Rodri was expected to join Real Madrid but they now face competition from arch rivals Barcelona

Last Update:

Barcelona have made a shock move to try to sign Spain captain Rodri from Manchester City.

The 30-year-old has less than 12 months left on his contract at the Etihad and has been targeted by Real Madrid this summer with president Florentino Perez performing a u-turn after previously suggesting the club were not interested in the former Atletico Madrid midfielder.

But with no sign of a deal being struck, it has allowed Madrid’s La Liga rivals Barcelona to make their move.

Table of Contents

De Jong injury complicates matters for Barcelona

Rodri would fit in perfectly at Camp Nou given Barca’s style of play is similar to that employed by both City and Spain. He won the 2024 Ballon d’Or and was awarded the Golden Ball for best player at the 2026 World Cup after leading Spain to the title.

Barca are exploring the possibility of bringing him to Catalonia due to doubts over the fitness of Netherlands midfielder Frenkie de Jong.

De Jong suffered a tear of the MCL in his right knee at the World Cup but opted against surgery, preferring a ‘conservative method of treatment’, albeit that may change depending on his progress.

If an operation is required then De Jong would be sidelined for several months, leaving Barca a man light in a key position.

Where does this leave Real Madrid?

Madrid opened talks with City last week but transfer guru Fabrizio Romano said no agreement was reached due to City’s belief that other clubs would enter the race and therefore ramp up the price.

Madrid, now under the returning Jose Mourinho, are looking to bolster their squad after two seasons without a major trophy. One contributing factor has been the lack of experience in midfield following the departures of Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

Rodri would provide that after proving at the World Cup he was back to his best after struggling to regain top form following a cruciate ligament injury in September 2024.

City have been attempting to persuade him to sign a new deal but the offer has been left on the table for several months and it seems the Etihad club have accepted the player wishes to move on.

What has Rodri said about a possible move back to Spain?

Rodri, who is currently recovering from a minor back operation, has flirted with the idea of moving back to his homeland for several months, saying in March: “Having played for Atlético [in 2018-19] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid. There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

His departure would be a major blow to new City boss Enzo Maresca.

Speaking in his first press conference as City boss last month, Maresca expressed calm over the speculation.

“First of all, we have to say that around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said.

“So I’m not worried about that, it’s normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup – he is one of the best players.

“I think every manager wants to have Rodri, because he’s a top player.

“But now, surgery [on a back problem] on Monday, and then he needs holiday, he needs to rest, recovery, and then he will be back here with us.”

articles.title: FIFA backs Infantino in vow over World Cup
articles.summary: FIFA says 'mistakes' were made around its World Cup stake plans
articles.content:
FIFA backs Infantino in vow over World Cup

FIFA says 'mistakes' were made around its World Cup stake plans

Last Update:

Gianni Infantino’s hugely controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup “should have been handled differently”, the governing body has said in a statement backing its under-pressure president.

FIFA was forced to withdraw the Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which faced fierce criticism from across the game and led to European body UEFA and its members threatening a boycott of the organisation’s tournaments.

Infantino had offered FIFA’s 211 member associations £30 million each if they backed private investment in tournaments, defending the proposals as recently as Friday before backing down and accepting the idea had created “divisions”.

Table of Contents

What have FIFA said? Full statement on World Cup plan

Following a meeting in Rabat, the FIFA Secretary General and members of its Management Board “reaffirmed their full support” for Infantino as “the only official elected” by the associations.

Earlier on Wednesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Infantino’s failure to consult senior advisers including FIFA’s chief operating officer and board members “should be fatal”.

Carney said Infantino committed a “fatal” governance failure by not consulting senior advisers, including FIFA’s chief operating officer and board members.

“It was discussed and agreed that the processes, communications and interactions between the FIFA President, the FIFA Secretary General and the FIFA Management Board that support the delivery of [Infantino’s] vision can and should always be continuously improved in terms of their effectiveness and efficiency,” FIFA said.

“The great work of the FIFA Administration that ensured a successful delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 was acknowledged, and which would not have been possible without the FIFA President, the FIFA Secretary General and FIFA Administration speaking as one voice and working as one team.

“In this regard, FIFA’s top management is fully confident that the outcomes of today’s meeting will strengthen FIFA’s governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner while continuing our mission to develop the game around the world.”

Gianni Infantino: FIFA will not ‘tolerate attacks on integrity’

The statement said “mistakes” had been “acknowledged” around the investment proposal. “It was agreed that it was not the intention for the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations to feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently,” it added.

“It was further acknowledged that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“In a separate letter to the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations, an apology was made for these errors together with a commitment to ensure they do not happen again.

“A review will now be conducted and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.

“As previously communicated, the FFE proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table.

“With the project withdrawn, it was agreed that FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

“There are always lessons to be learned and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience.

“In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework.

“FIFA will work closely with the relevant stakeholders to examine how it can further support the development of the game through the FIFA Forward programme for the benefit of [our] Member Associations, the Confederations and the Regional Associations.”

FIFA World Cup proposal

The initial idea was to sell a percentage of the commercial rights to FIFA’s flagship events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to investors and form a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

FIFA said Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – would lead the investor group.

It had been reported Infantino would become the chief executive of FFE and command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

articles.title: Why Matthias Jaissle could not turn down ‘exceptional’ Newcastle
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle is Newcastle's new manager
articles.content:
Why Matthias Jaissle could not turn down ‘exceptional’ Newcastle

Matthias Jaissle is Newcastle's new manager

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle has called Newcastle “one of the biggest clubs in European football” after being named the Magpies’ new boss on a four-year deal.

Jaissle, 38, has succeeded Eddie Howe, who left after nearly five years in charge on Friday, with the Premier League side paying Saudi club Al Ahli £9.5 million for the German’s services, according to Sky Sports.

“When Newcastle United come your way, you take notice,” Jaissle said. “The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be.

“I have followed the club’s journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see.

“I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking. There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.”

This is Matthias Jaissle ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/qntbfh0bQo

Table of Contents

Matthias Jaissle: Newcastle manager’s reaction in full

“It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United,” added Jaissle. “This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

“My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day. I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions.

“I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward.

“I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United.”

What have Newcastle said about Matthias Jaissle?

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson called Jaissle “one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football”.

“I’m thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United,” said Hopkinson. “We have conducted a thorough process and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role.

“He possesses all the qualities we were looking for. His track record of success, leadership qualities and relentless drive to improve make him an exceptional fit for Newcastle United.

“We believe he is the right person to lead the club into the next phase of our journey.”

Sporting director Ross Wilson praised Jaissle’s “leadership style and football philosophy” as being “strongly aligned with our sporting vision”.

“His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process,” revealed Wilson.

“He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.

“His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity.

“We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward.”

Matthias Jaissle stats, manager record

Jaissle is relatively unknown in the UK but has carved out a big reputation in Asia, helping Al-Ahli to back-to-back Champions League successes.

Jaissle’s playing career was disrupted when the centre-back suffered a serious knee injury playing for Hoffenheim against Hannover in 2009.

He was never the same when he returned and eventually hung up his boots in 2014.

Ralf Rangnick had brought him to Hoffenheim but had subsequently moved on to Leipzig and offered Jaissle the opportunity to start his coaching career in the German club’s youth department.

Jaissle gradually worked his way through the ranks – leaving briefly to become Alexander Zorniger’s assistant at Danish club Brondby – before being named head coach of the Under-18s at Salzburg, who like Leipzig are part of the Red Bull network of clubs.

Promotion followed, first when he was named boss of Salzburg’s feeder club FC Liefering and then shortly afterwards came the top job, succeeding Jesse Marsch.

Aged 33, he had the biggest job in Austrian football and he ran with it, developing a reputation for high-energy, high-press football as Salzburg, who had a hugely talented squad that included the likes of Benjamin Sesko, Karim Adeyemi, Noah Okafor and Brenden Aaronson, cruised to a league and cup double in his first season in charge.

Matthias Jaissle Al Ahli record

Jaissle repeated the feat in the 2022/23 season before being sacked after it emerged he had been discussing a switch to Al-Ahli.

“Yes, you’re not the first person to see it as a remarkable move,” he told The Athletic in January.

“But back then, it was really spontaneous. I wish the timing had been different, but sometimes that’s how it is in football. There’s interest, or an offer, and then you need to decide quickly.

“But for me, the thought back then was obviously — and let’s be completely honest — that financially it was something I just had to consider. But the other part was the chance to coach a team who had just got promoted into the first league, with a huge fanbase and with some big stars – some superstars, really – and it was a big step for me.”

Howe repeatedly refused to discuss Saudi’s human rights record – claiming he didn’t have time to research it properly – but Jaissle admitted he had given it thought.

“Yes, I’d read the headlines but at the same time I was aware that the country was taking some positive steps to open up,” he claimed. “There is a positive energy, that things are better than before and will keep getting better in the future. Not just in the club but across the city and country, especially among the young people.

“Obviously, change doesn’t happen overnight. It will take time. It’s growing so fast and that gives you hope for the future. I’ve seen for myself that in many ways they are on the right path.

“And I wanted the challenge. I wanted to coach abroad, in a different culture, and to work in English, which is not my native language.

“So, I saw it as a chance to develop as a coach. I’m still young, but I felt I was experienced enough to manage the expectations and the players, and to lead the team in the way that I had in Salzburg and for my style of play to be recognisable.”

He took over an Al-Ahli squad packed with players who had carved out a reputation in Europe’s major leagues – Roberto Firmino, Riyad Mahrez, Franck Kessie and goalkeeper Edouard Mendy while Ivan Toney joined shortly after.

Al-Ahli recorded third, fifth and third Pro League finishes in his three seasons in charge but his real success came continentally with Champions League trophy wins in 2025 and 2026.

Matthias Jaissle playing style

Jaissle is a disciple of Rangnick and the Red Bull system that is built on high press.

He said: “I want stress on the opponent as soon as possible. And when we win the ball, I want to go as quickly as possible towards the opponent’s goal. I’m very vertical in that approach.”

At Salzburg he showed his versatility by adopting different systems domestically in games where his side would dominate possession and in Europe where they would have to sit back.

“In Austria, we often faced teams who played a low block, but adaptation was always really important,” he explained. “In the league, we could play our way, using the identity we had in the academy, up through Liefering, and into the first team.

“But sometimes in the Champions League, I would try to do the same thing. You can’t always do that. You have to be smarter. There are times in the game where you have to play deep, which was not natural to us, and when you have to change the depth of your back four or alter the space between the defenders.

“That helped prepare me for coming to Saudi Arabia. I had a squad that was completely different in profile, and I had to think much more game-to-game about formation, how and when to press, and that forced me to become much more flexible — to develop as a coach.”

articles.summary: Martin O'Neill is in hospital is recovering from a procedure
articles.content:
Celtic boss O’Neill in hospital recovering from ‘small procedure’

Martin O'Neill is in hospital is recovering from a procedure

Last Update:

Celtic have confirmed manager Martin O’Neill is recovering in hospital after undergoing what the club described as a “small procedure”.

The 74-year-old is expected to be discharged within the next couple of days, with the Scottish champions providing an update after speculation over his absence.

“In response to speculation, we can confirm that Martin O’Neill has undergone a small procedure in hospital,” Celtic said in a statement.

“We would envisage Martin being released from hospital in the next day or two and, on behalf of Martin, we would like to thank supporters for their kind wishes.

“We would ask that the privacy of Martin and his family is respected.”

No details have been released regarding the nature of the procedure.

O’Neill present for opening day win

O’Neill was in the dugout on Monday as Celtic opened the new Scottish Premiership season with a 1-0 victory over Dundee.

The Northern Irishman was appointed on a permanent basis in June after two separate interim spells last season, signing a one-year contract with the option of a further 12 months.

His return to Celtic came almost 20 years after his first spell in charge, replacing Brendan Rodgers on an interim basis last October before handing over to Wilfried Nancy in December.

However, Nancy’s reign lasted only eight matches before O’Neill was brought back for a second interim spell, guiding Celtic to a Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup double.

Those successes convinced the club to hand him the role permanently following talks with major shareholder Dermot Desmond.

articles.title: Real Madrid icon warns Vinicius Junior off Arsenal transfer: ‘There’s no going back… it happened to Ozil too’
articles.summary: Madrid legend Predrag Mijatovic says Vinicius Junior should stay
articles.content:
Real Madrid icon warns Vinicius Junior off Arsenal transfer: ‘There’s no going back… it happened to Ozil too’

Madrid legend Predrag Mijatovic says Vinicius Junior should stay

Last Update:

Vinicius Junior would swiftly regret joining Arsenal and should stay at Real Madrid even if he is not a starter, according to a Champions League winner for Los Blancos.

Predrag Mijatovic, who scored the only goal when Madrid beat Juventus in the 1998 Champions League final, says Vinicius Junior should extend his contract beyond 2027 and end Arsenal’s hopes of signing the 26-year-old.

“It’s better to be second choice at Real Madrid, even if you’re behind [Kylian] Mbappe, than first at any other team in the world.” Mijatovic told El Larguero (via Mundo Deportivo).

“This is exactly what can happen to Vinicius or anyone else who has left: you leave upset, angry because you’re not valued and so on… I’ve heard all these stories 1,500 times.

“And then you run into this same player 20 days or a month later in London, Paris or wherever, and the first thing he says is ‘my God – how wrong I was.'”

Table of Contents

Vinicius Junior: Why Madrid hero says Brazil star should stay

Mijatovic claimed that even Mesut Ozil, who left Madrid for Arsenal in 2013 because he believed head coach Carlo Ancelotti did not believe in him, rued the switch.

Ozil made the decision after Ancelotti succeeded current Madrid boss Jose Mourinho and went on to establish himself as one of the finest playmakers in Premier League history during almost nine years at Arsenal.

“When you want to go back, there’s no going back,” said Mijatovic, the winner of the Liga Best Foreign Player award in 1996 and the Ballon d’Or runner-up in 1997 as part of a three-year spell with Madrid.

“And all for two or three million euros. Which is a lot of money, but with 20 million you live exactly the same. I’ve experienced this myself and it happened to Ozil, too.”

Also a Liga and Spanish Super Cup winner with Madrid, Mijatovic left to spend two seasons at Fiorentina, winning the Italian Cup before finishing his career with Levante.

Vinicius Junior transfer news: What the forward says

Vinicius Junior said on Tuesday that Mourinho had told him his expectations during gruelling training sessions after the forward’s return from the World Cup with Brazil.

Mourinho met Vinicius Junior for the first time since his reappointment in May for a second tenure at the club.

“Very well,” the 26-year-old replied when Madrid’s official channel asked how he felt, sitting on a ball and smiling.

“[I’m] getting to know the new manager, the new players and working really hard. He wants me to be just as I’ve always been: happy, positive and playing. We all finished completely dead on our feet.”

Vinicius Jr: Will Real Madrid forward join Arsenal?

Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta smiled broadly but dodged the question when he was repeatedly asked about Vinicius Junior after his side’s friendly win at Girona on Saturday.

Mourinho voiced worries over the lack of training time he will have with key senior players including Vinicius Junior after his team’s draw with Fiorentina on the same day, saying he would “like to have three weeks” with him.

Vinicius Junior holds control over the situation, with his willingness to sign a new deal dictating whether the reigning Premier League champions could make him a statement signing.

Madrid’s enthusiastic coverage of Vinicius Junior’s return perhaps emphasise that the 15-time European champions are expecting him to stay.

The club have posted footage of both of Vinicius Junior’s first sessions preparing for the 2026/27 season, titling the second “Vini Jr is back!” in capital letters.

Vinicius Junior: What Arsenal said

Arteta said Arsenal are “very active, trying to improve and evolve the team”. “That’s clear,” added the Spaniard.

“We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

Vinicius Jr stats: Best FIFA, La Liga, Champions League

Signed from Flamengo for a reported fee of around £39.4 million in 2018, Vinicius Junior’s individual honours include the 2023/24 Champions League Player of the Season award and the 2024 Best FIFA Men’s Player honour.

He was the Ballon d’Or runner up to Rodri in the same year. Here’s a look at the trophies Vinicius Junior has won with Madrid.

Real Madrid schedule: When does Vinicius Junior’s season start?

Madrid’s competitive season starts away to Espanyol on August 22 (20:30 BST). Arsenal kick off a day earlier at home to Coventry City (20:00).

articles.title: Alonso insists Chelsea are making progress despite poor performance in defeat to Juventus
articles.summary: Edon Zhegrova scored the only goal as Juventus beat Chelsea at Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong
articles.content:
Alonso insists Chelsea are making progress despite poor performance in defeat to Juventus

Edon Zhegrova scored the only goal as Juventus beat Chelsea at Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea are “taking little steps forward” despite another defeat on their pre-season tour of Asia on Wednesday.

The Blues were beaten 1-0 by Juventus in Hong Kong and produced a lifeless display in a game punctuated by niggly fouls and numerous substitutions.

The return of Mykhailo Mudryk following a 20-month absence due to a drugs ban was the highlight for Chelsea, who could not conjure up any response after falling behind to Edon Zhegrova’s brilliant goal midway through the second half.

Mudryk came on for the last eight minutes but had little time to impress with Alonso’s side still searching for any kind of fluidity on a tour that saw them scrape a wild 6-4 win over the A-League’s worst team, the Western Sydney Wanderers, followed by a 2-1 defeat to a Tottenham side that played with 10 men for almost the entirety of the second half.

Alonso said: “We have been together for three weeks so it’s early days to talk about everything but we are taking little steps forward and many more that we will take in the future for sure.”

Table of Contents

It’s a process, says Chelsea boss Alonso

The former Real Madrid boss suggested there were elements of the performance he liked, adding: “I think we started pretty well. The first 30-35 minutes we played with good control, we have created a few chances but in the last few minutes, a little bit like last Saturday, we lost a little bit of control.

“In the second-half there were many changes, the game was not that controlled. But for sure it’s a process, it’s minutes for everyone and now we have two more [games] before we go back to London and start the season.”

Mudryk only joined the squad in Hong Kong over the weekend after his suspension was lifted last week and Alonso was delighted to see him take to the field. “I’m really pleased for him,” he said. “It was emotional for everyone from the club to see him back, especially when I told him before the game that my idea was that he could play 10-15 minutes.

“He was thrilled. After such a long period, to be back on the pitch, it was a great feeling for him and a great feeling for everyone.

“It was more than a football decision. It was a human decision and emotional decision to give him this boost, to feel the great support that he got and the great reception when he came on the pitch.”

Palestra and Quenda impress for Chelsea

Chelsea had 21 players on the bench at Kai Tak Stadium while the likes of Enzo Fernandez as well as new signings Valentin Barco, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Morgan Rogers are still on their post World Cup break.

Alonso needs to trim a bloated squad but he did reserve words of praise for two of his new signings, Marco Palestra and Geovany Quenda.

He said: “Yeah, happy with Geo. After he missed the last week in Australia, he wasn’t there but he came a couple of days ago and to play 45 minutes after the little injury… he’s been very good. Happy that he could have these minutes.

“And Marco for sure is having a great impact. You see his power. He repeats up and down, big stamina, quality as well in the last third. So we are impressed with him. Happy that we have Marco in the squad and that he gives solutions. He’s a flexible player so it’s going to be very interesting to work with him.”

Cole Palmer and Levi Colwill missed the game but Alonso said they were left out due to minor injuries and could play at the weekend against AC Milan in Jakarta.

What’s next for Chelsea?

Chelsea have two games left on their pre-season tour. All times are UK.

8 August: Chelsea v AC Milan (Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, Jakarta, 13:00)

11 August: Johor Darul Ta’zim v Chelsea (Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, Johor, 13:00)

articles.content:
Maresca heaps praise on Manchester City players after first win

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was pleased with his side's performance in the pre-season win over K-League All-Stars.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca praised his players’ effort after they secured a 3-1 pre-season victory over the K-League All Stars in sweltering conditions in Seoul.

The Italian oversaw his first win since succeeding Pep Guardiola, with Rayan Ait-Nouri, Tijjani Reijnders and Divin Mubama all finding the net before half-time as City eased to the win on their Asia tour.

Temperatures reached around 36 degrees Celsius at kick-off, but Maresca was pleased with the way his side coped with the extreme heat.

“For us the result is always important, even if it is a friendly game, but the most important thing is to see the effort of the players, especially in this weather,” he said.

“Also, compared to the last game, in some aspects we did some things better.

“The good thing is the players tried to adapt. They made an effort for 95 minutes.

“Since day one, the players are putting in the effort and I can see that they trust the job we are doing and, for me, this is the main thing.”

Maresca expecting key players back next week

The win followed City’s opening pre-season draw with Inter Milan and came with several senior players still absent following their involvement at the 2026 World Cup.

Maresca expects the squad to improve further once those players return to training ahead of the new campaign.

“The reason why is because around eight or nine players are still not here with us,” he added.

“But the important thing is when they are here they make the effort to do the things we have been trying to do since day one.

“Also we need them to trust what we want, that is important and then when the rest of the players arrive there is no doubt we will be even better.”

articles.title: Manchester United Women name Olid as new boss
articles.summary: Eva Olid will replace Marc Skinner as coach of Manchester United Women
articles.content:
Manchester United Women name Olid as new boss

Eva Olid will replace Marc Skinner as coach of Manchester United Women

Last Update:

Eva Olid has been named the new coach of Manchester United Women.

Spaniard Olid enjoyed great success at Hearts, leading the Edinburgh club from the second division to their first Premier League title in May.

The 40-year-old has signed a two-year contract at United and succeeds Marc Skinner, who left the club by mutual consent earlier this week after five years in charge.

Olid told the club’s official website: “The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true.

“The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an Academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team and an exceptional group of support staff.

“There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential.

“I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud.”

Johnson delighted to have secured Olid signature

Matt Johnson, director of women’s football at Manchester United, added: “Eva is an outstanding coach with an incredible determination to succeed. Her remarkable achievements at Heart of Midlothian showcased her ability to maximise the potential of individual players whilst also implementing an exciting style of football. We are delighted that she will now bring those qualities to Manchester United.

“Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era. She shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players, a tradition deeply embedded in our club’s history and culture, as well as improving established senior internationals, both of which form an integral part of our vision for long-term, sustainable success.”

articles.title: Debutant Welbeck comes close but Chelsea frustrated by Juventus in Hong Kong
articles.summary: There was little for an enthusiastic Hong Kong crowd to get excited about as Chelsea and Juventus played out a largely turgid first 45 minutes
articles.content:
Debutant Welbeck comes close but Chelsea frustrated by Juventus in Hong Kong

There was little for an enthusiastic Hong Kong crowd to get excited about as Chelsea and Juventus played out a largely turgid first 45 minutes

Last Update:

Danny Welbeck came close to a debut goal as Chelsea struggled to break Juventus down in their latest game on their pre-season tour of Asia.

Welbeck was handed a first start in a Chelsea shirt following his surprise move from Brighton and the experienced former England international had the Blues only real chance in a largely dire opening 45 minutes at Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong.

The chance was created by another debutant, teenage winger Geovany Quenda, after 13 minutes with a beautifully whipped in cross picking out Welbeck but the 35-year-old’s flicked header flew wide of the target.

The early stages were littered with niggly fouls and the odd hefty challenge with both sides looking to set down a marker – much to the delight of an enthusiastic crowd.

Bar Welbeck’s header and a wayward shot from Quenda, there was very little for the locals to get excited about with no efforts on target in the opening half hour.

Juve offered more of an attacking threat as half-time approached, the lively Jeremie Boga sending in two crosses, the first dropped by Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, who did much better with the second.

Sanchez was also called into action on the stroke of half-time to keep out a Boga shot, the Spaniard getting down well to ensure the game remained goalless at half-time.

Table of Contents

CHELSEA TEAM NEWS

Mykhailo Mudryk was named among the substitutes and could make his first appearance in 20 months. The Ukraine winger has not played since November 2024 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium. His case was resolved last week and Mudryk jumped on the first available flight to Hong Kong.

Cole Palmer and Levi Colwill missed out with minor knocks.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Hato, Fofana, Adarabioyo, Palestra; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Quenda, Gittens, Joao Pedro; Welbeck

Chelsea Substitutes: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Sarr, Subuloye, Anselmino, Acheampong, Diakite, Essugo, Lavia, Walsh, Watson, Kellyman, Satpayev, Kavuma-McQueen, Estevao, Mudryk, Neto, Jackson, Delap

JUVENTUS TEAM NEWS

Juventus can no longer call upon Dusan Vlahovic, released at the end of his contract, so a fit-again Arkadiusz Milik led the line.

Juventus: Di Gregorio; Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Celik; Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Boga, Miretti, Cambiaso; Milik

Juventus Substitutes: Perin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremer, Koopmeiners, Yildiz, Zhegrova, Rugani, Arthur, David, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi

How to watch Chelsea v Juventus: TV and online streams

Chelsea v Juventus kicked off at 12:30pm UK time on Wednesday August 5, which is 7:30pm local time in Hong Kong. In the UK, the match will be shown live on Chelsea’s in-house streaming service, CFC.

articles.title: Luis Figo attacks Gianni Infantino, describing his World Cup sell-off plan as ‘deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour’
articles.summary: Luis Figo has demanded Gianni Infantino leave his position as FIFA president in a remarkable attack on the Swiss
articles.content:
Luis Figo attacks Gianni Infantino, describing his World Cup sell-off plan as ‘deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour’

Luis Figo has demanded Gianni Infantino leave his position as FIFA president in a remarkable attack on the Swiss

Last Update:

Luis Figo has launched an extraordinary attack on FIFA president Gianni Infantino, describing his attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed”.

The former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Portugal star lashed out at Infantino, whose plan has now been abandoned following widespread opposition that has left him clinging on to his role as the head of the global game’s governing body.

The initial idea was to sell a percentage of the commercial rights to FIFA’s flagship events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to investors and form a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). FIFA said Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – would lead the investor group.

It had been reported Infantino would become the CEO of FFE and command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

Figo was deeply unimpressed and, in a letter published in the Daily Mail, wrote: “I could write 10,000 words on the problems at FIFA. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go.

“I have loved football all my life. I was a professional player for 20 years. And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game.

“But what I have seen exposed in the last 10 days is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed.

“The man who would do that – the man who would try to force through such major changes just to enrich himself and his friends – is a relic of the game’s past and should have no part in its future.”

Table of Contents

Infantino fights to save his job

Infantino is currently in Moroccan city Rabat, meeting other senior FIFA officials, many of whom have already distanced themselves from the idea.

The Swiss will continue to fight to save his job but Figo, who is an adviser to UEFA – the most outspoken of the confederations in the desire to see Infantino sacked, is adamant he should go now.

He added: “None of this comes as a surprise when you consider the litany of abuses he has inflicted on football’s reputation; from suspending and reversing disciplinary decisions to breaking the laws of the game over a half-time show, nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends.

“Football does need a discussion about money. But not the money that could go out of the game to investors or on bloated administrator salaries.

“I mean the money that should be spent on building pitches and training coaches to make sure that every child in the world has the chance to fall in love with the most beautiful sport on the planet.

“I mean the $5bn in FIFA’s reserves for a start. How many shares could that buy in this grubby, underhand plot? All of them! So there is no need for outside investment after all.”

Infantino has lied and deceived – Figo

Figo continued: “This plan – like the Super League before it – was blown apart by the media exposing every devious twist and turn before its advocates had their messaging straight. And thank goodness it was.

“Infantino has debased the office of FIFA president that he promised to elevate. He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.

“He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the FIFA Peace Prize winner [Trump].

“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

articles.title: Vinicius Junior holds crunch contract talks with Real Madrid after rejecting latest offer
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior is undergoing another round of contract talks on Wednesday.
articles.content:
Vinicius Junior holds crunch contract talks with Real Madrid after rejecting latest offer

Vinicius Junior is undergoing another round of contract talks on Wednesday.

Last Update:

Real Madrid will hold a crucial meeting with Vinicius Junior’s representatives on Wednesday as the club looks to resolve growing uncertainty over the Brazilian’s future.

According to El Larguero, Vinicius has rejected Madrid’s latest contract offer, reportedly worth €22 million (£19m) per season until 2031, with Arsenal said to be leading the race for his signature if a new deal cannot be agreed.

The Brazil international’s current contract expires in 2027, meaning he could leave on a free transfer next summer if he chooses not to renew.

Former Real Madrid player and sporting director Pedja Mijatovic believes the situation is becoming increasingly difficult for the Spanish giants.

“Now we know what Real Madrid are offering him and Vinicius has rejected it,” Mijatovic said on El Larguero.

“At this point in the summer, with one year left on his contract, this whole situation clearly tells me that Vinicius is not about to renew.”

The former Montenegro international suggested the financial details of any new proposal are no longer the main issue.

“He can ask for €30m, €35m or €25m, it doesn’t matter. At this stage, he’s already thinking about or evaluating other offers because he’s a great player.”

Arsenal still pushing for winger

Mijatovic also claimed Arsenal are pushing hard to bring the winger to the Premier League.

“Arsenal are very interested in signing him. I have information from England that says Arsenal want to go all out to sign him.”

He added that Madrid may have to consider selling the 26-year-old rather than risk losing him for nothing.

“If he doesn’t want to renew, then at least you have to make an important transfer. We’ll see what happens, but by August there is still no clarity. If you can’t convince him to renew, you have to consider bringing in a lot of money for him.”

articles.title: Mohamed Salah lands in Istanbul ahead of Trabzonspor switch
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah has arrived in Turkey and is expected to sign for Trabzonspor later on Wednesday
articles.content:
Mohamed Salah lands in Istanbul ahead of Trabzonspor switch

Mohamed Salah has arrived in Turkey and is expected to sign for Trabzonspor later on Wednesday

Last Update:

Mohamed Salah has landed in Istanbul and been pictured wearing the shirt of Trabzonspor as he closes in on a move to the Turkish Super Lig club.

Salah, 34, left Liverpool in June after nine hugely successful years on Merseyside. He scored 257 goals for Liverpool, trailing only Ian Rush (346) and Roger Hunt (285) on the Reds’ all-time list, and won nine trophies, including two Premier League titles and one Champions League crown.

He had been heavily linked with a move to Besiktas but that deal stalled, allowing Trabzonspor to step in.

Salah will undergo a medical in Istanbul this morning and then fly to Trabzon later on Wednesday. He has already started undergoing his social media duties, posting a video from the flight in which he said: “Everywhere is Trabzon for us.”

Trabzonspor confirm negotiations are underway

Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish Super Lig last season and won the Turkish Cup. They will play in Europa League qualifying later this month.

“Negotiations ​have been ⁠launched ‌to transfer professional footballer Mohamed ‌Salah, who ‌is in a ⁠free status, to our club,” the club said in a statement last night.

Salah signed a two-year deal at Anfield in April 2025 towards the end of a brilliant 2024/25 campaign that saw him score 29 Premier League goals and provide 18 assists, equalling the league record for most goal involvements in a season.

But a difficult season for him and the club in 2025/26 saw him muster just seven league goals and seven assists. He also fell out with then Reds boss Arne Slot with Salah publicly criticising the team’s playing style following a 4-2 defeat to Aston Villa, calling for a return to the “heavy metal attacking” football that made Liverpool so feared under Jurgen Klopp.

The contract was terminated with both parties declaring the desire to move on. Saudi Arabia had seemed the most likely destination for Salah but he will instead spent the next few seasons in Trabzon, a small city on the Black Sea coast.

articles.title: BREAKING: Arsenal set to sign Guimaraes after fee agreed with Newcastle
articles.summary: Arsenal are set to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fee of £75million
articles.content:
BREAKING: Arsenal set to sign Guimaraes after fee agreed with Newcastle

Arsenal are set to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fee of £75million

Last Update:

Newcastle have accepted an offer of £75million from Arsenal for captain Bruno Guimaraes, according to widespread reports this morning.

The Brazil international has been agitating for a move to North London for some time and will now leave Newcastle’s pre-season training camp in La Manga to sign for the Gunners.

The deal had been dragging on for several weeks with Arsenal’s initial bid of under £60m rejected by Newcastle who maintained they did not want to sell the 28-year-old.

But the two sides remained at the negotiating table with Newcastle keen not to repeat the mistakes of last summer when they tried to retain striker Alexander Isak only to sell him late in the window to Liverpool and struggle to find suitable replacements.

Guimaraes joined Newcastle in January 2022 for a fee in the region of £42m and has made 153 Premier League appearances, scoring 30 goals and adding 26 assists. His former club Lyon are due 20 per cent of the profit Newcastle will make on the player.

Table of Contents

Worrying summer for Newcastle

His exit is another blow to Newcastle who have lost fellow key players Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer. Gordon went to Barcelona while Tonali opted to join Tottenham for combined fees in the region of £170m.

In their stead, the Tyneside club have recruited several young players after reforming their transfer model.

On Monday, they announced their fifth signing of the summer with the arrival of Czech goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Hornicek is the second goalkeeper to be recruited, following Ewen Jaouen through the door.

Newcastle have also signed Bazoumana Touré, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba since the end of last season following a disappointing 12th-placed finish in the Premier League.

There has also been a change in the dugout with Eddie Howe leaving the club. Matthias Jaissle is his replacement and has been in Spain conducting training this week, even though the club have yet to formally announce his arrival from Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Ahli.

Guimaraes deal a welcome boost for Arsenal

While it has been a concerning summer for Newcastle, Arsenal have made quiet progress to improve a squad that clinched the Premier League title last season.

Piero Hincapie has made his loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent while Greece winger Christos Tzolis joined from Club Brugge to replace the departed Leandro Trossard. Arsenal have also snapped up free agent goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

Arsenal are still in the market for a marquee arrival with boss Mikel Arteta admitting they are looking to be ambitious this summer. They are reported to have sounded out the representatives of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr, who has less than 12 months left on his deal at the Santiago Bernabeu, although the smart money is on the Brazilian signing a bumper new deal in the Spanish capital.

articles.content:
Florentino Luis: Ipswich complete £16m transfer from Burnley

Ex-Portugal youth international Florentino Luis has joined Ipswich

Last Update:

Newly-promoted Ipswich Town have signed Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis on a five-year deal.

The 26-year-old made his loan move from Benfica to the Clarets a permanent one in June and has now moved on for a reported fee of £16 million.

Florentino was a key part of former Burnley manager Scott Parker’s team in their unsuccessful fight to avoid relegation from the Premier League and made 33 appearances in total.

Secured. 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/9PV7JwtqOG

Table of Contents

Florentino Luis: Ipswich transfer ‘brilliant’

“It feels brilliant to be a part of this club,” Florentino said.

“I think I will be very happy here. I like how the club sees the future and there are a lot of good players.

“How the club is thinking to the long-term is one of the main reasons I came here.

“I can bring experience and balance to the team, between defence and attack, and I like to bring the connection.”

Ipswich Town: Premier League schedule

Ipswich are back in the top flight after finishing second behind Coventry in the Championship last season.

Manager Kieran McKenna stepped down after that promotion, with former Bournemouth boss Gary O’Neil taking the reins.

Ipswich begin their Premier League campaign at home to Sunderland on August 22..
