articles.title: Arsenal third kit 26/27: Watch video, full details on new shirt and strip
articles.summary: All you need to know about Arsenal's 2026/27 third kit
articles.content:
Arsenal third kit 26/27: Watch video, full details on new shirt and strip

All you need to know about Arsenal's 2026/27 third kit

Last Update:

Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal have unveiled their new Adidas third shirt as part of the club’s kit for the 2026/27 season.

The release, which was announced in August, means the Gunners will play in yellow for the first time in five seasons, with forward Kai Havertz offering his seal of approval while calling the kit “very cool”.

An accompanying film features stars including model and actress Adwoa Aboah and players Noni Madueke, Steph Catley and Martin Zubimendi.

Eberechi Eze, Alessia Russo, Gabriel Martinelli, Olivia Smith, Piero Hincapie and Chloe Kelly are among the figures to have played a key role in the launch.

Table of Contents

Arsenal third kit 2026/27 full design details

The kit is inspired by the club’s ‘Arsenal State of Mind’ slogan, which aims to combine “creativity, joy and belonging” with landmarks, familiar faces and memorable moments from club history.

An updated version of the club’s lightning graphic is part of the fabric, described as a “contemporary expression of a symbol that has long been woven into Arsenal’s story”.

“The idea was that when you face adversity, it’s a way of always seeing the positive side in every situation, to overcome it with a fun twist,” said filmmaker Fx Goby, describing the concept of the slogan to Arsenal’s official channels.

“[Arsenal] wanted to build a film together; a little story where we could see several situations where you face an obstacle and then instead of choosing to be angry or mad, you just try to make something positive out of it.

“That’s what guided the whole process for the story we wrote together.”

How to buy Arsenal 26/27 third kit

The kit is available from Arsenal’s online shop. “She’s amazing,” Goby said of Aboah, who has appeared on the cover of British Vogue.

“I knew her and, when we started putting some names down and thinking ‘okay, who could be the perfect person for this project?’, she came first very, very quickly for many reasons.

“She’s an Arsenal fan, so that was important. She’s beautiful but she’s also a great actress and she’s got a very iconic face.

“It was important that we could translate that face into animation and we could recognise her instantly. It was perfect because she embodied everything that we needed for this project.”

How much does the 26/27 Arsenal third kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Arsenal replica shirt is £85 or £90 for a long-sleeved version, while the authentic versions start at £120, with personalised or player names and numbers available at an additional cost.

Youth shirts start at £60. A baby kit is available for £40. The shorts cost between £30 and £38.

Accompanying socks cost between £16 and £20. A range of other clothing and items in the third-kit colours are available, including bags and footballs.

Goby called Arsenal’s players “really cool” during their modelling duties. “It was a big day and they had a lot of shoots that day,” he revealed.

“They were just super sweet, super loving, very pro, very kind. Martin [Odegaard] is a little bit shy, so he spoke in Spanish to me, and then everybody was like ‘oh, Martin speaks Spanish?’

“[They are] very, very lovely people – really super sweet. It was funny because I don’t know all the players very well, so I’m not as starstruck as other people in the team.”

When does Arsenal’s 2026/27 Premier League season start?

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield at Wembley Stadium on August 16 at 15:00 BST (10:00 ET / 07:00 PT).

Mikel Arteta’s team host the first match of the Premier League season against promoted visitors. Here are the key details.

articles.title: Friendlies: Kamara scores on Villa return as Bayern also win on tour
articles.summary: Villa will soon be in Super Cup action
articles.content:
Friendlies: Kamara scores on Villa return as Bayern also win on tour

Villa will soon be in Super Cup action

Last Update:

Aston Villa midfielder Boubacar Kamara marked his return from injury with a goal as Villa continued their 2026 summer tour of Southeast Asia with a convincing 3–1 victory over Thai League 1 side BG Pathum.

Unai Emery’s side handled the oppressive 34°C heat and humidity effectively, securing their second consecutive pre-season win following their opening 3–1 triumph over the Indonesia All Stars in Jakarta.

Villa established complete command of the contest in the first half, striking twice before the break to build a comfortable 2–0 lead.

The visiting Premier League side dominated possession and pressed high, forcing turnovers against the Thai League Cup holders and demonstrating sharp attacking movement in the final third.

Emi Buendia got on the end of a slick team move to open the scoring before Victor Lindelof headed a second.

New signing Alejandro Garnacho played the first half while the likes of Kamara, John McGinn and Pau Torres all got some game time after the break.

Kamara fired in a third shortly after coming on, with the midfielder returning from his latest knee injury.

Villa are in the UEFA Super Cup final against Paris Saint-Germain on 12 August 12. Villa now head to Hong Kong for their final leg of the Asian tour, where they will face Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium on 7 August.

No Kane but Bayern also win on tour

Bayern Munich left some big names behind after their World Cup exploits but still picked up a hard-fought 2–1 victory over K League 1 outfit Jeju SK FC at the Jeju World Cup Stadium in Seogwipo-si.

The German champions took early command of the encounter and found the breakthrough in the 11th minute. Following a chaotic clearance inside the Jeju penalty box, Felipe Chaves reacted quickest to pounce on the loose ball, neatly slotting past the goalkeeper to put Bayern ahead.

Jeju responded almost immediately with a stunning piece of skill just four minutes later. Striker Mateus Aias executed a remarkable rainbow flick inside the 18-yard box to evade defenders Kim Min-jae and Hiroki Ito, cutting the ball back for Lee Chang-min to fire home.

With mainstays such as Harry Kane and Michael Olise rested, Vincent Kompany gave extended minutes to academy prospects and squad players. Bayern re-established their lead before the interval as Bastian Assomo, 16, fired in.

articles.summary: The Gunners look set to get their man
articles.content:
Arsenal ‘close’ to deal for Newcastle captain Guimaraes

The Gunners look set to get their man

Last Update:

Arsenal’s summer-long pursuit of Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes appears to be close to an end.

The Premier League holders want the Brazil midfielder and with Eddie Howe leaving Newcastle last week the way appears clear for the move to be done.

Transfer guru David Ornstein says the deal is now close to ‘a total agreement.’

The Gunners have pursued the former Lyon midfielder for much of the summer.

Intermediaries are thought to have been involved and even though Newcastle have baulked at suggestions Arsenal were willing to offer £70m, it is believed an offer in the region of £80m would be enough to make a breakthrough.

Losing Guimaraes would be another huge blow for Newcastle, although it is thought they are privately resigned to their star man moving on.

Boss  Howe left the club last week while two of their most experienced players Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have moved to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively for combined fees in the region of £170m.

They have signed Bazoumana Touré, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba since the end of last season following a disappointing 12th-placed finish in the Premier League.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta would not be drawn directly on Guimaraes over the weekend, but said the club were “very active” and “very ambitious in what we want to do”.

“We need to increase the competition internally,” he added.

“We need to make sure we identify the things that we don’t have in the team.”

articles.title: Vinicius Jr hints his future lies at Real Madrid in potential blow for Arsenal
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr has been linked with a move from Real Madrid to Arsenal but his latest words suggest he will be staying in the Spanish capital
articles.content:
Vinicius Jr hints his future lies at Real Madrid in potential blow for Arsenal

Vinicius Jr has been linked with a move from Real Madrid to Arsenal but his latest words suggest he will be staying in the Spanish capital

Last Update:

Vinicius Jr has given his strongest indication yet that he will be playing for Real Madrid this coming season.

The Brazil international returned to the Spanish capital this week following his extended summer break due to the World Cup amid speculation he could be on the move with Arsenal reported to have opened talks with his representatives over a transfer to North London.

Vinicius Jr has less than 12 months remaining on his Madrid contract but talks over a renewal have stalled with the club not willing to meet his demands.

Reports in Spain have suggested the two parties have returned to the negotiating table and the 26-year-old certainly appeared to be taking the longer term view when he discussed the season ahead with Madrid TV.

Asked about the training sessions under new Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, he said: “It has gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new players and training very hard. Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful and enjoying my football.

“We have to prepare physically so that during the season we have fewer injuries and thus be able to count on everyone.”

Vinicius Jr spent the second half of the summer having chin reconstruction and hanging out with his girlfriend Virginia Fonseca but has been hard at work following his return to Madrid’s Valdebebas training complex.

He added: ”Yesterday double [session], today one session. So let’s go. Today we did a bit in the gym and a bit of work to load the legs. It has been good and we have all left very tired, but now it is time to rest for tomorrow. The pre-season is like this and we have to be prepared.”

Table of Contents

What’s happening between Vinicius and Arsenal?

It was reported on Monday that Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had taken personal ownership of the club’s pursuit of Vinicius Jr.

Spanish daily AS suggested Arteta has made it clear to the player’s camp that he would be central to Arsenal’s longer-term ambitions as they look to take the next step from Premier League champions to European champions.

Arsenal reached the final of the Champions League last season but their limitations were exposed with a dreadfully negative performance against Paris Saint-Germain that suggested Arteta was not convinced his side was good enough to go toe-to-toe with Luis Enrique’s men.

The signing of Vinicius would alter that dynamic and give greater gravitas to what Arsenal are trying to achieve.

We are ambitious, says Arsenal boss Arteta when asked about Vinicius Jr

Asked specifically about Vinicius Jr following Saturday evening’s 4-1 win in Spain against Girona, Arteta refused to divulge too much but confirmed the Gunners were looking to make significant steps forward this summer.

“We are very active, trying to improve and evolve the team,” the Spaniard said. “That’s clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

Diomande could, eventually, be Vinicius Jr replacement at Madrid

Losing Vinicius Jr would be a major blow to Madrid, although they appear set to have a ready-made replacement in Yan Diomande.

The transfer of the Ivory Coast international to the Bernabeu is being held up due to an issue with a former agent, according to reports, but the 19-year-old RB Leipzig winger is still expected to be a Madrid player by the time they get their Liga season underway at Espanyol.

Vinicius Jr stats: Best FIFA, La Liga, Champions League

Signed from Flamengo for a reported fee of around £39.4 million in 2018, Vinicius Junior’s individual honours include the 2023/24 Champions League Player of the Season award and the 2024 Best FIFA Men’s Player honour.

He was the Ballon d’Or runner up to Rodri in the same year. Here’s a look at the trophies Vinicius Junior has won with Madrid.

Real Madrid schedule: When does Vinicius Junior’s season start?

Madrid’s competitive season starts away to Espanyol on August 22 (20:30 BST). Arsenal kick off a day earlier at home to Coventry City (20:00).

articles.title: ‘I have to be a leader’ says Foden as he starts new Man City chapter
articles.summary: The 26-year-old has already played 225 league games for City
articles.content:
‘I have to be a leader’ says Foden as he starts new Man City chapter

The 26-year-old has already played 225 league games for City

Last Update:

Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden says he is ready to step up and be a leader at the club as they begin life after Pep Guardiola.

The legendary City boss left the club at the end of the season after a decade in charge which saw them win 20 trophies.

Foden, 26, has played all of his club football under the Spaniard until now.

And, with Enzo Maresca now in charge, the six-time Premier League winner says he is ready to be a focal point after missing out on the World Cup.

He said: “I’ve been at the club for so long, I’m one of the longest serving here so this season I have to be one of the leaders, one of the captains.

“I’m looking forward to that new responsibility and trying to take leadership.”

City have seen John Stones, Bernardo Silva and Nathan Ake all leave this summer while Rodri is linked with a move to Real Madrid.

Foden could find himself as the most experienced player come the start of the Premier League season and he is relishing playing under a new manager.

“I’ve found it good. All I’ve known is Pep Guardiola so to go to a new manager is just a fresh start,” he said.

“I’m enjoying it. I’m enjoying the coaching staff and the way we’re playing and the things we’re doing in training. I’m excited for the season and hopefully we’re going to have a really good year.

“It’s very similar to how we played under Pep but there’s obviously still things that are a little bit different.

“I don’t want to give too much away but the defending is a little bit different, how we set up. We have different ideas of playing out from the back, a variety of things on the ball.

“There are different things but the lads are very comfortable because we want to build from the back and try and create.”

City face the K-League All-Stars in Seoul on Wednesday as part of their pre-season tour of Asia.

articles.title: ‘There are things we need to do’ – New City boss Maresca expecting some signings
articles.summary: Where do last season's runners-up need to strengthen?
articles.content:
‘There are things we need to do’ – New City boss Maresca expecting some signings

Where do last season's runners-up need to strengthen?

Last Update:

New Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is expecting to add to his squad before the end of the summer transfer window as he prepares for the Premier League season.

City have, of course, lost talismanic manager Pep Guardiola but also seen key players leave.

John Stones has signed for Inter, Bernardo Silva joined Real Madrid while Nathan Ake joined Turkish side Fenerbahce.

Goalkeeper James Trafford could also leave, while City have so far only signed Elliot Anderson for the first-team picture.

City face the K-League All-Stars in Seoul on Wednesday as part of their pre-season tour of Asia, and Maresca said before the game that he expects to see some new faces at the club soon.

“Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,” he said.

“But at the same time, as we already know, the club lost important players in terms of experience like Bernardo [Silva], John [Stones] and Nathan [Ake]. For sure, there are things that we need to do.

“James [Trafford] is still a City player.

“There are things to do because the transfer window is open and when it’s open anything can happen.

“It’s just August and then from September when it closes it will be different.”

This season’s transfer window closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday, 1 September.

City have been linked with breakout World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi as well as Pedro Neto from Maresca’s former club Chelsea.

Key midfielder Rodri has consistently been linked with a move to Real Madrid.

Italian Maresca, a former assistant to Guardiola at City, has signed a three-year deal at the Etihad, having won the Championship with Leciester and the Club World Cup and Conference League at Chelsea.

City lost to Inter Milan on penalties in Hong Kong last week.

articles.title: Liverpool away kit 2026/27: All you need to know
articles.summary: The key details on Liverpool's 2026/27 away kit
articles.content:
Liverpool away kit 2026/27: All you need to know

The key details on Liverpool's 2026/27 away kit

Last Update:

Twenty-time Premier League champions Liverpool have released their new Adidas away kit as part of the club’s strips for the 2026/27 season.

The shirt, which was unveiled in July as part of the club’s pre-season tour of the US, is white and red and features a fabric pattern drawing inspired by historic Anfield match tickets.

Alexander Isak, Grace Fisk, Florian Wirtz, Ceri Holland, Virgil van Dijk, Trey Nyoni and Hugo Ekitike are among the players to have helped with the launch.

Here are the key details on the release, including the story behind the design and how to buy the new kit.

Table of Contents

Liverpool away kit: When will Premier League side wear new shirt?

Liverpool wore the kit for the first time against Wrexham on July 29 at Yankee Stadium in New York City.

Their next away match is their Premier League opener against Newcastle on August 23 (16:30 BST).

Liverpool away kit 2026/27 full design details

The kit is based on the away look Liverpool adopted between 1985 and 1988, winning the Premier League during the first and third of those seasons and the FA Cup in 1986.

A clean white base is accompnied by strawberry red and grey detailing on the V-neck collar and sleeve cuffs, with the heritage Liver Bird crest returning on the chest alongside Adidas’ Trefoil logo.

“These two iconic symbols reinforce the jersey’s connection to the club’s history, celebrating a partnership and period that remain deeply embedded in football culture,” Liverpool say.

References to vintage ticket stubs and “archival graphic elements” are “integrated throughout”. The aim is to create texture and depth, as well as “paying tribute to generations of supporters who have passed through the turnstiles”.

How to buy Liverpool 26/27 away kit

The kit is available from Liverpool’s online shop, stores and some Adidas retail locations.

How much does the 26/27 Liverpool away kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Liverpool replica shirt is £85 or £90 for a long-sleeved version, while the authentic versions start at £120, with personalised or player names and numbers available at an additional cost.

Youth shirts start at £60. A baby kit is available for £40. The shorts cost between £30 and £38.

Accompanying socks cost between £20. A range of other clothing and items in the away colours are available.

When does Liverpool’s Premier League season start and end?

Liverpool’s season starts with that game against Newcastle at St James’ Park on August 23 and ends at home to Bournemouth – new head coach Andoni Iraola’s former team – on May 30 (16:00 BST).

articles.title: Lionel Messi makes €80k donation to help with rebuild after Madrid fires
articles.summary: Lionel Messi made the gesture after fires ripped through an area near the Spanish capital of Madrid
articles.content:
Lionel Messi makes €80k donation to help with rebuild after Madrid fires

Lionel Messi made the gesture after fires ripped through an area near the Spanish capital of Madrid

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has donated €80,000 to help rebuild an area west of Madrid that has been devastated by fire.

The Sierra Oeste, a rural mountain region located less than an hour away from the Spanish capital, has been ravaged by the blazes caused by heatwaves and prolonged dry spells. Over 60,000 people have been affected with 43 houses destroyed and another 300 badly damaged.

The rebuild is now underway and Messi has donated to the cause.

The president of the Community of Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, wrote on X: “Leo Messi has donated €80,000 for the reconstruction of Madrid’s Sierra Oeste. I want to thank you and tell you that we hope to see you soon to give you the applause you deserve.”

Messi continues to donate to charity

Messi’s philanthropic works often goes under the radar but he supports children’s health, education, and social causes primarily through the Fundación Leo Messi and his long-standing role as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

The 39-year-old Argentine retains a special bond with Spain, even though he spent his entire Liga career in the fiercely independent region of Catalonia.

He moved to Barcelona in 2000 as a 13-year-old and made it his home – winning 34 trophies and scoring 672 goals – before leaving for Paris Saint-Germain in 2021. He now plays for Inter MIami in the United States.

Messi has won eight Ballons d’Or and is widely regarded as the greatest footballer of all time.

articles.title: Mudryk could make sensational Chelsea return tomorrow after 20 months on the sidelines
articles.summary: Winger Mykhailo Mudryk could be involved as Chelsea play Juventus in Hong Kong Wednesday
articles.content:
Mudryk could make sensational Chelsea return tomorrow after 20 months on the sidelines

Winger Mykhailo Mudryk could be involved as Chelsea play Juventus in Hong Kong Wednesday

Last Update:

Mykhailo Mudryk could make an immediate return to the Chelsea squad for tomorrow’s pre-season friendly with Juventus after serving his drugs ban.

The Ukraine winger has spent 20 months on the sidelines after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium. His case was resolved last week and Mudryk jumped on the first available flight to Hong Kong to join Chelsea’s tour of Asia.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso was delighted to see the 25-year-old link up with his team-mates and the former Shakhtar Donetsk man could be thrust straight into tomorrow’s game with the Serie A side at Kai Tak Stadium.

Alonso said: “We are thrilled Misha could be with us. You could see his smile, the great feeling for him to be back. Fitness level, we will see. He has been working hard. Now it’s about trying to do things with his team-mates.”

Asked if he could feature against Juve, Alonso added: “He came directly from the airport to the hotel. Yesterday was more about the feelings and emotions than to assess fitness level. But yes, he could play. Ninety minutes [is] too early. He can be selected, he can play.

“He’s been a long time training on his own. It’s different – he needs to be involved with team-mates. He’s really professional. Now it’s about growing progressively.”

Mudryk has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge with newly promoted Coventry believed to be one of the clubs interested.

Alonso said: “No decision made. We need to assess, he is a special player but it is a special case so we need to be sensitive.”

Midfielder Moises Caicedo also paid tribute to Mudryk’s strength of character.

The Ecuador international said: ”I am happy for him. It is not easy to stop playing. He is really strong, he is a strong man. Everyone is happy to have him back. For sure he is going to come back stronger and he is going to keep doing what he does.”

Table of Contents

Why was Mudryk banned?

Mudryk was handed a four-year sanction by an independent regulatory commission after testing positive for a low concentration of the banned substance meldonium in October 2024.

But changes to WADA’s rules mean that if Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations (ADVRs) would have resulted.

However, following talks between Mudryk and the Football Association, with the agreement of WADA, the Ukraine international has accepted that he had committed the ADRVs he was charged with and agreed to a period of ineligibility equal to the time already served.

In a statement, the FA confirmed Mudryk was no longer ineligible and can now resume his career.

What has Mudryk said?

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 and admits it has been a hugely challenging period in his life.

He said: “After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.

“I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future. This has been the most difficult period of my career.

“As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance. My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.

“I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period. I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my team-mates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout.

“I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case. My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch. Thank you to everyone who continued to believe in me. I look forward to the next chapter of my career.”

Chelsea now focused on reintegrating Mudryk into first-team squad

Mudryk joined Chelsea in January 2023 from Ukrainian club Shakhtar Donetsk in a deal worth an initial £59million, signing a contract until 2031.

He made 53 appearances for the West London club before being suspended.

His return is a boost for Chelsea, and new boss Alonso in particular.

A Chelsea statement read: “From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

“We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

“We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.”

articles.title: Neymar hints at retirement in December
articles.summary: Santos forward Neymar is pondering retirement after a brilliant career that included trophy-laden spells at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain
articles.content:
Neymar hints at retirement in December

Santos forward Neymar is pondering retirement after a brilliant career that included trophy-laden spells at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain

Last Update:

Brazil’s record goalscorer Neymar has suggested he could retire when his Santos contract expires in December.

The 34-year-old returned to his boyhood club in January 2025 after successful spells in Europe with Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain and an injury-ravaged stint with Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal.

He has struggled for fitness over the past 18 months but did manage to make the Brazil squad for the World Cup, making two appearances and scoring once.

The injuries are likely to have taken a toll and Neymar admitted all options were on the table when it comes to his future plans.

He said: ”I don’t know how long [I will continue playing]. I have a contract with Santos until December. I intend to fulfill the contract, honour the Santos shirt in the best possible way and then I will think when my contract ends if I stay, if I leave, if I stop playing or if I continue.”

Table of Contents

Neymar wants to end 2026 on a high

Neymar stressed the short-term goal was to end the season well with Santos, starting with tonight’s Brazil Cup tie against Remo – a match he will reportedly start on the bench.

He added: “I really don’t know what I’m going to do. Until December there is time, but let’s go little by little, game by game, I’m feeling good physically. That’s what matters.

“I am 100% at the coach’s disposal. As everything comes out at Santos before the players know, they have already published that I will be on the bench.

“I hope to be ready to help and bring victory to the Big Fish.”

Is Neymar’s brilliant career coming to an end?

Neymar left Santos for Barca aged 21 in 2013 and went on to enjoy a fantastic career at Camp Nou, forming one third of the famous MSN trident that also included Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, and winning two La Ligas and one Champions League crown.

He joined PSG in 2017 for a world record transfer fee of around £200million and helped the Parisians to five Ligue 1 crowns.

A ruptured ACL sustained on international duty with Brazil in 2023 disrupted his time in Saudi and the national team, although he remains the five-time World Cup winners’ record scorer with 80 in 130 appearances.

articles.content:
Fulham confirm double signing of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid

Last Update:

Fulham have completed the signing of striker Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid for a reported £34million.

The 22-year-old Spaniard has signed a five-year deal at Craven Cottage and reunites with former Real boss Alvaro Arbeloa, who is now in charge of the Whites.

Garcia was the top scorer at last year’s Club World Cup and has scored 13 goals in 51 appearances for the LaLiga giants.

Garcia said: ”I’m very grateful, very happy to be here.

”I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they’ve put in me, and I’m very, very excited to start.”

Garcia is Arbeloa’s first signing of the summer since replacing Marco Silva as manager, with the ex-Liverpool right-back leaving Real at the end of last season.

Tony Khan added: “I’m thrilled to welcome Gonzalo García to Fulham! Gonzalo is a very talented young striker, and he is excited to come to Fulham and play in the Premier League.

“We all believe that Gonzalo will be a tremendous addition to the squad and will prove to be an excellent player for the Club under Álvaro’s leadership! Come on Fulham!”

Fulham sign Palacios after Garcia confirmed

He will be joined by fellow Real youngster Cesar Palacios at Craven Cottage, with the 21-year-old’s arrival announced roughly 30 minutes after Garcia’s.

Palacios, 21, has joined for a reported £8.5m and has signed a five-year deal with the club holding an option to extend by 12 months.

Meanwhile, 18-year-old midfielder Thiago Pitarch has also been strongly linked with a move from Los Blancos.

articles.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal: Real Madrid to resume contract talks this week
articles.summary: Vinicius has entered the final year of his Real Madrid contract
articles.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal: Real Madrid to resume contract talks this week

Vinicius has entered the final year of his Real Madrid contract

Last Update:

Real Madrid are set to resume contract talks with Vinicius Junior this week amid interest from Arsenal, according to the BBC.

The Gunners have reportedly stepped up their interest in the Brazilian winger, with Mikel Arteta personally driving efforts to land the 26-year-old this summer.

Vinicius’ future at Real has been uncertain for some time, with contract talks dragging out over the last 18 months with no resolution.

His current deal expires in 2027, so it is the last summer the LaLiga giants can demand a fee for one of their star plauers.

Table of Contents

Is Vinicius leaving Real Madrid?

Vinicius returned to Real Madrid for pre-season training on Monday following an extended break after the World Cup.

He is working with new manager Jose Mourinho for the firs time, with the Portuguese boss reportedly keen for the Brazil star to remain in the Spanish capital.

Vinicius is said to be keen to sign a new deal at Real, but the fact that this is the last summer to demand a fee means a move is likely if a deal can’t be struck in the coming days.

Despite reports of feeling undervalued by the club, the two-time Champions League winner has described Real as “the club of my dreams” and said he hopes to remain there “for many years”.

Can Arsenal pull off a move for Vinicius Jr?

With a new addition on the left a priority, Arsenal are said to be ramping up their efforts to land Vinicius, with the Gunners boss making it clear to the player’s camp that he is central to their hopes of success in the future.

That may well convince the forward to make the move, with reported doubts over Vinicius’ future role in Real’s star-studded team.

When asked about Vinicius after a 4-1 pre-season win over Girona, Arteta said they were looking to be ambitious this summer.

“We are very active, trying to improve and evolve the team,” the Spaniard said. “That’s clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

articles.title: ‘Jadon was not on trial with the club’: Non-league Flixton deny Sancho transfer rumour
articles.summary: Sancho is without a club after leaving Manchester United
articles.content:
‘Jadon was not on trial with the club’: Non-league Flixton deny Sancho transfer rumour

Sancho is without a club after leaving Manchester United

Last Update:

Non-league club Flixton have been forced to deny rumours they are set to sign former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho on social media.

Sancho, 26, left Man Utd upon the expiry of his contract this summer and is yet to find a new club, and was subsequently pictured training with 10th-tier Flixton in the North West Counties Division.

Rumours, albeit far-fetched rumours, circulated that he may be set to drop down to the non-league side, forcing them to play down the links to the once £73million player.

“To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions,” Flixton wrote in a statement on Instagram.

“He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.”

Table of Contents

What next for Sancho?

After falling out with manager Erik ten Hag three years ago at Old Trafford, Sancho has spent time on loan at Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa, but has failed to make enough of an impact to convince any to sign him permanently.

That said, Sancho enjoyed some success at all three of those loan spells, reaching the Champions League final with Dortmund, before scoring in the final as Chelsea won the Conference League in 2025.

He was then part of the Villa team who won the Europa League in May, coming on in the final as Unai Emery’s men beat Freiburg.

As a free transfer, Sancho will surely not be without a club before long, with a switch to Europe or the Middle East believed to be his next potential options.

‘Jadon is a world-class footballer’

He certainly has the backing of Flixton to resurrect his career, with the Greater Manchester club speaking glowingly of the England international for his behaviour while using their facilities.

They added: “After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

“Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of.

“He deserves respect both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.”

articles.title: Flick claims Barcelona still need to sign a striker ahead of new season
articles.summary: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick says the club need to bring in a striker.
articles.content:
Flick claims Barcelona still need to sign a striker ahead of new season

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick says the club need to bring in a striker.

Last Update:

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has admitted the club need to strengthen their attack before the new season as they continue their search for a long-term replacement for Robert Lewandowski.

The Spanish champions are targeting Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, with club president Joan Laporta confirming Barcelona have submitted an offer worth around €100 million for the Argentina international.

Speaking on Monday, Flick acknowledged Barcelona are still looking to add a new No. 9.

“We have to wait,” he said. “I have total confidence with Deco and we know that we have to do something. It depends also on Ferran’s situation and then we will see what happens.”

Barcelona’s plans are also being shaped by uncertainty over Ferran Torres, who has entered the final year of his contract.

The Spain international, who scored the winner in the World Cup final, has been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and several Premier League clubs, while Barcelona remain open to offering him a new deal.

Torres admitted his future remains undecided.

“I currently have a contract with Barca, but in football you never know,” he said.

“I’m just waiting to make the right decision. I don’t know yet.”

Flick confident players can step up

If Torres departs and Barcelona fail to sign a new striker, Flick believes he already has players capable of filling the role.

Summer arrivals Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi can both play through the middle, while Lamine Yamal has also been used centrally.

“Lamine has played in one or two matches with us and I think he’s a fantastic player, a world-class player, so he also can adapt to this,” Flick said.

“But at the end of the day, the focus with Lamine is more as a No. 7, but we will see what happens.

“I think Gordon and also Adeyemi can play on both sides. They can also play as a No. 9. So we have a lot of options actually. We will see.”

articles.title: Chelsea agree £25m sale of Chalobah to Como
articles.summary: Trevoh Chalobah is leaving Chelsea for Como.
articles.content:
Chelsea agree £25m sale of Chalobah to Como

Trevoh Chalobah is leaving Chelsea for Como.

Last Update:

Como have reached an agreement to sign Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah in a deal worth more than £30 million.

The 27-year-old is expected to sign a long-term contract with the Serie A club, where he will take on a leadership role under head coach Cesc Fabregas after Como secured Champions League qualification with a fourth-place finish last season.

Chelsea will receive an initial fee of £25.7m, with a further £5.1m in performance-related add-ons following lengthy negotiations between the two clubs.

The overall package is close to Chelsea’s original valuation of £30m plus £5m in bonuses, with Como finally reaching an agreement after making several offers since early June. Inter Milan had also shown interest in the England international.

Fabregas, who played for both Chelsea and Arsenal during his career, has been pushing to bring Chalobah to Como for more than six months.

The move will end Chalobah’s near 20-year association with Chelsea, having joined the club’s academy as a youngster before progressing into the first team.

His departure is part of Chelsea’s ongoing efforts to trim Xabi Alonso’s squad ahead of the new season.

The Blues strengthened their defence earlier this summer by signing Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for £52m, adding further experience and physicality to the back line.

Chelsea still have a wealth of central defensive options, including Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Tosin Adarabioyo, Josh Acheampong, Benoit Badiashile, Aaron Anselmino, Axel Disasi and Mamadou Sarr.

The club are also looking to move on Disasi and Badiashile before the transfer window closes, while Sarr or Acheampong could be sent out on loan, potentially to another Premier League side.

articles.title: LA Galaxy manager claims Casemiro agreed to join before late Inter Miami switch
articles.summary: Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro said he would join LA Galaxy, according to the general manager.
articles.content:
LA Galaxy manager claims Casemiro agreed to join before late Inter Miami switch

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro said he would join LA Galaxy, according to the general manager.

Last Update:

Los Angeles Galaxy general manager Will Kuntz has claimed Casemiro initially told the MLS club he “only wanted to play” for them, as Major League Soccer continues its investigation into the Brazil midfielder’s move to Inter Miami.

The former Manchester United midfielder joined Lionel Messi’s side on a free transfer in July, signing a deal through the end of the 2027 MLS season, with the option to extend until June 2029.

Casemiro made his first appearance since the World Cup in Sunday’s 2-2 draw against the Columbus Crew, scoring an unfortunate own goal as Miami were held.

Speaking after LA Galaxy’s goalless draw with FC Dallas, Kuntz addressed the ongoing MLS review into the transfer.

“It is true that Casemiro called and said that he always wanted to play for Inter Miami,” Kuntz said.

“It’s also true that came two months after he told us that he only wanted to play for the Galaxy.”

The investigation centres on MLS discovery rights, a league mechanism that gives one club priority to negotiate with a player if they decide to move to Major League Soccer.

MLS confirmed it had opened an investigation shortly after Casemiro’s move was announced.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete,” a statement read.

“While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the Discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.”

MLS discovery rights

Under MLS rules, each club can hold discovery rights on up to five players at any one time, giving them first refusal should those players wish to join the league.

LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights before Inter Miami acquired them as part of the agreement that paved the way for the transfer.

The California club confirmed a settlement had been reached but said the details would remain confidential until the investigation concludes.

Casemiro has previously insisted he made his intentions clear throughout the process.

“I left it very clear to them that I wanted to join Miami,” he said.

“In the end, it’s a city I love. My wife, my kids and I are always here when we have days off. We know the city.

“When I spoke to the Galaxy, I made it very clear which team I wanted to join in MLS and that is Inter Miami because of the project, the hope and, of course, to play with the best player of all time.”

He also claimed that he joined the club to play with Messi himself.

articles.title: BREAKING: Chelsea confirm signing of Jordan Henderson
articles.summary: Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea on a two-year deal following his release by Brentford
articles.content:
BREAKING: Chelsea confirm signing of Jordan Henderson

Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea on a two-year deal following his release by Brentford

Last Update:

Chelsea have completed the signing of experienced midfielder Jordan Henderson.

Henderson has penned a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge after leaving Brentford by mutual consent last week.

The 36-year-old has been recruited by new Blues boss Xabi Alonso to add some nous to a young dressing room and follows on from the signing of another veteran, former Brighton striker Danny Welbeck, over the weekend.

Henderson told the club’s official website: “Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

“I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

“For me, it’s about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I’m very excited to get going.”

Henderson will provide Chelsea with know-how

Henderson started out at Sunderland before a big-money move to Liverpool in 2011. He made 492 appearances for the Merseyside club, taking over from Steven Gerrard as captain and lifting six major trophies, including the Premier League and Champions League.

A short, ill-advised move to Al-Ettifaq in Saudi Arabia was followed by a spell with Ajax before he joined Brentford.

Henderson has also made 91 appearances for England and was a member of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for this summer’s World Cup.

He played just six minutes at the tournament, though, featuring in the closing stages of England’s 2-0 Group L victory against Panama before breaking his arm in the celebrations that followed the win against Mexico at the Azteca Stadium.

articles.title: Leipzig deny Diomande to Real Madrid deal is done and mock Romano for premature ‘Here We Go’
articles.summary: RB Leipzig chief Marcel Schafer insists no agreement has been reached for Yan Diomande to join Real Madrid and says Fabrizio Romano went too early with his trademark 'Here We Go'
articles.content:
Leipzig deny Diomande to Real Madrid deal is done and mock Romano for premature ‘Here We Go’

RB Leipzig chief Marcel Schafer insists no agreement has been reached for Yan Diomande to join Real Madrid and says Fabrizio Romano went too early with his trademark 'Here We Go'

Last Update:

RB Leipzig sporting director Marcel Schafer has denied a deal has been struck with Real Madrid for the sale of Yan Diomande and mocked transfer guru Fabrizio Romano for suggesting otherwise.

Romano first reported the two clubs had agreed a fee, believed to be in the region of £102million, on July 26 and accompanied a picture of the Ivory Coast winger with his trademark ‘Here We Go’ slogan on social media platform X.

And with personal terms reportedly already negotiated, it was seen as a matter of time before the 19-year-old’s move to the Santiago Bernabeu was formally announced.

Table of Contents

Agent spat provides potential blocker for Diomande’s Madrid move

However, there has been a hold-up with Diomande’s former agents Maximal Management – led by ex-Leeds winger Max Gradel – lodging a complaint with FIFA after it emerged Roc Nation, founded by rap star Jay-Z, were now looking after the player’s interests.

And Leipzig have now thrown another spanner in the works by suggesting the deal is not as advanced as initially thought.

Schafer told Sky Sports Germany: “It is clear that some self-proclaimed signing experts reported a few days ago that the agreement was closed or they gave him the ‘here we go’. It’s just not like that. We haven’t reached that stage yet.”

It would still be a major surprise if Diomande did not end up at the Santiago Bernabeu this summer with Schafer confident the agent issue would not prove to be a blocker.

He added: “There has been a change of agents. Our point of contact now is Roc Nation – that was made very clear to us by Yan. I don’t think a transfer will fall on that, if there is a transfer in the first place.”

Diomande training alone with Madrid deal in balance

Diomande returned to Leipzig last Monday after an extended summer break following his exertions at the World Cup but has not been training with the squad.

It is believed the Bundesliga club are trying to ensure he remains injury free in case a deal with Madrid can be struck.

New Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will be eager there is no hitch in their pursuit of Diomande with the future of Vinicius Jr still uncertain.

The Brazil winger was pictured training with the Spanish giants this morning for the first time since he returned from South America. The 26-year-old has less than 12 months remaining on his current deal, prompting interest from Arsenal.

articles.title: Celtic discover Champions League opponents as Rangers prepare for Europa League
articles.summary: Celtic will face the Austrian champions in their Champions League play-off.
articles.content:
Celtic discover Champions League opponents as Rangers prepare for Europa League

Celtic will face the Austrian champions in their Champions League play-off.

Last Update:

Celtic have been drawn against Austrian champions LASK in the Champions League play-off round.

Martin O’Neill’s side will host the first leg on either August 18 or 19 before travelling to Austria for the return fixture a week later, with a place in the league phase at stake.

LASK secured their second Austrian Bundesliga title last season, ending a 61-year wait for domestic glory, and qualified directly for the play-off round alongside Celtic.

Although several lower-ranked opponents were available in the draw, the Austrian champions are widely viewed as one of the toughest possible opponents due to the strength of their domestic league.

Rangers discover Europa League opponents

Elsewhere, Rangers will face either Northern Irish champions Larne or Georgian side Iberia Tbilisi in the Europa League play-off round if they overcome Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok in the third qualifying round.

The Ibrox club will host the first leg on August 20.

Should Rangers be eliminated by Jagiellonia, they will instead drop into the Conference League play-offs, where they would meet either Czech side Jablonec or Latvian champions RFS.

Hearts, who dropped into the Europa League after their Champions League qualifying defeat to Sturm Graz, will face either AGF Aarhus of Denmark or Azerbaijan’s Sabah if they get past Benfica.

If the Edinburgh club lose to Benfica, they will instead enter the Conference League play-offs against either Estonian side Paide Linnameeskond or Austrian outfit Rapid Vienna.

Motherwell will take on Bundesliga side Freiburg in the Conference League play-offs if they eliminate HJK Helsinki in the current qualifying round.

Hibernian, meanwhile, will face either Swedish club IFK Gothenburg or Belgian side Gent if they progress past North Macedonian champions Shkendija.

articles.title: Pochettino signs new deal to remain as USA head coach
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has signed a new deal with US Soccer and will be tasked with building on the team's successful World Cup campaign
articles.content:
Pochettino signs new deal to remain as USA head coach

Mauricio Pochettino has signed a new deal with US Soccer and will be tasked with building on the team's successful World Cup campaign

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino has committed to leading the USA men’s national team through to 2030 after signing a new four-year contract.

The Argentine joined US Soccer in September 2024 and, despite a rocky start, justified his lucrative salary by guiding the team to the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup where they were beaten by Belgium.

That match, and the fall-out to the defeat, was dominated by the issue of Folarin Balogun’s suspended red card following discussions between FIFA chief Gianni Infantino and US president Donald Trump, but the USA’s performances over the summer were largely excellent.

That has prompted US Soccer to dig deep once again although financial support has come via a philanthropic gift from Kenneth C Griffin, the founder and CEO of Citadel and founder of Griffin Catalyst. Additional support has been provided by Scott Goodwin, Adam Freede and several commercial partners.

“Mauricio and his staff believe in the future of soccer in the United States and our new project allows us to build on the progress of the USMNT and the momentum of US Soccer,” said CEO and secretary general JT Batson.

“We know we have a lot of work to do to achieve our clear ambitions, including competing to win men’s World Cups and having soccer become the most played sport in every community. I couldn’t be more excited that Mauricio and team are committed to partnering with all of us to do the hard work to bring those ambitions to life.”

Table of Contents

Pochettino makes his mark with the USA

Having enjoyed spells in Europe with the likes of Tottenham and Paris Saint-Germain, it had been expected Pochettino would be tempted back by a job in the top five leagues.

But he has opted to remain in the States and work with an exciting young team that has developed under the 54-year-old and now plays his trademark, high press, high energy football.

“Working together with US Soccer over the past two years, it has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men’s national team program even stronger,” said Pochettino.

“The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here. We are excited by the opportunity to bring all our experience and knowledge to even more areas of US Soccer while helping strengthen the pathways for players, coaches and teams across the Federation. We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field.”

Pochettino changes culture at US Soccer

For so long seen as a closed shop, Pochettino ended a culture seen as comfortable and ensured every call up to the squad was justified, even though that meant high-profile players being left out.

In total, 62 players have earned a cap under Pochettino since October 2024, coming from 16 different leagues in 12 different countries.

The 2030 World Cup is the long-term target but, before then, the US will compete in the 2027 and 2029 CONCACAF Nations Leagues and the 2027 and 2029 Gold Cups.

“Mauricio has built a culture where players trust the group, trust the process and trust each other,” said US Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone.

“We saw the impact of that belief in the way the team grew, competed and performed on the world’s biggest stage. That culture, and the staff who helped build it, are exactly what we want to continue investing in for the men’s national team now and for the future. We are also excited about the experience and perspective Mauricio and his staff can bring across US Soccer as we strengthen our pathways and seek to impact the broader soccer landscape in the United States.”

articles.title: FA withdraw support for FIFA President Infantino as pressure builds
articles.summary: The English Football Association have withdrawn their support for FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.
articles.content:
FA withdraw support for FIFA President Infantino as pressure builds

The English Football Association have withdrawn their support for FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.

Last Update:

The English Football Association is set to withdraw its support for FIFA president Gianni Infantino following the collapse of his controversial plan to sell stakes in the governing body’s competitions to private investors.

The move comes as UEFA considers legal action over the proposal, while the Football Association of Wales has publicly withdrawn its backing for Infantino’s bid to remain FIFA president.

Infantino’s leadership has come under increasing pressure after UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation all opposed the investment plan, forcing FIFA to abandon the proposal.

The governing body had intended to create a commercial subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to manage its flagship competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, while allowing external investors to purchase minority stakes.

According to The Telegraph, UEFA has informed Infantino it is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints” in relation to the proposal.

The European governing body has also demanded that FIFA preserve all documents connected to the plan, including emails, instant messages, text messages, written correspondence and meeting notes involving FIFA officials, member associations, broadcasters, sponsors and financial institutions.

UEFA has requested confirmation within five business days that the documents will be retained and protected from deletion.

FIFA has been approached for comment.

Infantino bribe backfires

Infantino had written to all 211 FIFA member associations promising each nation $40 million (£30 million) if they backed the proposal, with an initial payment of $20 million (£15 million) available ahead of a September 19 deadline.

The proposed investment was expected to be led by American venture capital firm Thrive Eternal, founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

Despite the growing backlash, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait and Sri Lanka have publicly backed Infantino’s leadership.

The Swiss official remains eligible to seek a fourth and final term as FIFA president at next March’s Congress, where he would require the support of at least 106 of the organisation’s 211 member associations.

However, pressure is also mounting within FIFA’s governing structure.

An extraordinary FIFA Council meeting could be called if at least 19 of its 37 members request one, with the meeting required to take place within two weeks.

The council includes nine representatives from UEFA, seven from the Asian Football Confederation, five from Concacaf, six from the Confederation of African Football, five from CONMEBOL, three from Oceania, as well as Infantino and FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

articles.title: Semenyo sings Maresca’s praises as Manchester City star prepares for fresh start
articles.summary: Antoine Semenyo has hailed new Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca.
articles.content:
Semenyo sings Maresca’s praises as Manchester City star prepares for fresh start

Antoine Semenyo has hailed new Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca.

Last Update:

Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo says Enzo Maresca’s attacking approach is “music to my ears” after getting an early taste of the new head coach’s tactics during the club’s pre-season opener.

City were beaten on penalties by Inter Milan in Hong Kong in Maresca’s first game in charge, but the Italian’s emphasis on attacking wing play was evident throughout the contest.

Semenyo started the match and caused constant problems for Inter full-back Andy Diouf with his pace and direct running, helping create Divin Mubama’s goal before being replaced at half-time.

Teenage winger Ryan McAidoo also impressed off the bench, with Maresca later describing both players as the type of wingers he wants in his system.

“When he got appointed, that was the first thing I thought about because when you’ve played Chelsea previously when he was there, his wide men were always high and quite free,” Semenyo said.

“So that was one of the things that excited me the most when he got appointed and it’s exciting for me as a winger. I get to have one-v-one situations most of the game and I am looking forward to it.

“I have had individual meetings with him on how he wants to set up, how he wants to play his wide men and just overall as a team.

“I think his ideas are great, quite similar to Pep, but if you watched the Inter game, you would have seen a couple of his ideas play out and it was good.

“Enzo is just [telling me to] stay out wide and when you get the ball, just create opportunities. So it is music to my ears.”

Semenyo joined City as ‘next step’

Semenyo joined City from Bournemouth in a £65 million deal during the January transfer window after attracting interest from Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea.

The Ghana international said Manchester City was the obvious choice for the next step in his career.

“I owe Bournemouth everything to be honest,” he said. “They helped my Premier League career flourish and the management, the staff behind the scenes, they were all amazing and made everything so smooth.

“I just wanted the next step to be the big one and Manchester City was the option.

“Pep spoke to me beforehand and he said, ‘Look, when you come, I am going to make you a better player’.

“You want to get better, you want to improve every season and he definitely helped me with that in the first five months, but obviously it’s sad for him to leave.”

Semenyo scored 21 goals for club and country last season, including the winner in City’s FA Cup final victory over Chelsea, while also helping the club lift the Carabao Cup.

articles.title: Newcastle’s difficulties continue with captain Bruno Guimarães failing to join pre-season camp as Arsenal hover
articles.summary: Bruno Guimarães will belatedly join up with Newcastle today but his delayed arrival is another indication of his desperation to leave the club and join Arsenal
articles.content:
Newcastle’s difficulties continue with captain Bruno Guimarães failing to join pre-season camp as Arsenal hover

Bruno Guimarães will belatedly join up with Newcastle today but his delayed arrival is another indication of his desperation to leave the club and join Arsenal

Last Update:

Bruno Guimaraes failed to arrive in La Manga yesterday to meet up with the Newcastle squad for a pre-season training camp but is now belatedly on his way to Spain.

Newcastle captain Guimaraes was granted an extended summer break following his participation in the World Cup with Brazil but was supposed to join his team-mates, and new boss Matthias Jaissle, yesterday.

Newcastle are said to be relaxed about the situation but it will do little to appease fans angry at Guimaraes’ eagerness to quit the Tyneside club and move to Arsenal.

The Gunners have pursued the former Lyon midfielder for much of the summer but reports on Tyneside suggest a formal club-to-club bid has yet to be made, despite suggestions the Premier League champions have successfully negotiated personal terms with the player.

Intermediaries are thought to have been involved and even though Newcastle have baulked at suggestions Arsenal were willing to offer £70million, it is believed an offer in the region of £80m would be enough to make a breakthrough.

Newcastle enduring a miserable summer

Losing Guimaraes would be another huge blow for Newcastle, although it is thought they are privately resigned to their star man moving on.

Boss Eddie Howe left the club last week while two of their most experienced players Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have moved to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively for combined fees in the region of £170m.

In their stead, Newcastle have opted for youth in a marked shift to their transfer policy.

This morning they announced their fifth signing of the summer with the arrival of Czech goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Hornicek is the second goalkeeper to be recruited, following Ewen Jaouen through the door.

Newcastle have also signed Bazoumana Touré, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba since the end of last season  following a disappointing 12th-placed finish in the Premier League.

Jaissle is the new man in the dugout and while he has already been working in La Manga with the players, his arrival has yet to be formally announced.

Jaissle will swap Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia for the Premier League, having twice claimed the Asian Champions League title with the Pro League club.

articles.title: Arsenal ramp up interest in Vinicius Jr with Mikel Arteta now orchestrating pursuit of Real Madrid star
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta is so eager to see Vinicius Jr play for Arsenal he has taken the unusual step of leading the club's pitch to the Real Madrid winger
articles.content:
Arsenal ramp up interest in Vinicius Jr with Mikel Arteta now orchestrating pursuit of Real Madrid star

Mikel Arteta is so eager to see Vinicius Jr play for Arsenal he has taken the unusual step of leading the club's pitch to the Real Madrid winger

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta has taken personal ownership of Arsenal’s pursuit of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr as the Gunners look to make a huge splash in the transfer market.

The Brazil winger has less than 12 months remaining on his Madrid contract and, despite the issue rumbling on for well over a year, there is still no sign of the Spanish giants persuading him to agree to a renewal.

Vinicius Jr is reported to be unsure whether he will be key to the new Madrid under Jose Mourinho after two trophyless seasons at the Santiago Bernabeu. And while the club are desperate to retain one of their key assets, the fact they are not willing to meet the 26-year-old’s wage demands means the door is ajar for a move away.

That has alerted Arsenal and Spanish daily AS are reporting Arteta is so eager to prise Vinicius Jr out of the Spanish capital, he has become actively involved in the club’s pitch.

AS suggest Arteta has made it clear to the player’s camp that he would be central to Arsenal’s longer-term ambitions as they look to take the next step from Premier League champions to European champions.

Arsenal reached the final of the Champions League last season but their limitations were exposed with a dreadfully negative performance against Paris Saint-Germain that suggested Arteta was not convinced his side was good enough to go toe-to-toe with Luis Enrique’s men.

The signing of Vinicius, who is expected back in Madrid on Monday after a summer spent at the World Cup and undergoing chin reconstruction, would alter that dynamic and give greater gravitas to what Arsenal are trying to achieve.

Table of Contents

We are ambitious, says Arsenal boss Arteta when asked about Vinicius Jr

Asked specifically about Vinicius Jr following Saturday evening’s 4-1 win in Spain against Girona, Arteta refused to divulge too much but confirmed the Gunners were looking to make significant steps forward this summer.

“We are very active, trying to improve and evolve the team,” the Spaniard said. “That’s clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

Diomande could, eventually, be Vinicius Jr replacement at Madrid

Losing Vinicius Jr would be a major blow to Madrid, although they appear set to have a ready-made replacement in Yan Diomande.

The transfer of the Ivory Coast international to the Bernabeu is being held up due to an issue with a former agent, according to reports, but the 19-year-old RB Leipzig winger is still expected to be a Madrid player by the time they get their Liga season underway at Espanyol on August 22.

articles.title: Newcastle make first signing of post-Howe era by snapping up Hornicek
articles.summary: Newcastle may still be waiting for confirmation of Matthias Jaissle's arrival on Tyneside but that has not stopped their spending with Lukas Hornicek the latest recruit
articles.content:
Newcastle make first signing of post-Howe era by snapping up Hornicek

Newcastle may still be waiting for confirmation of Matthias Jaissle's arrival on Tyneside but that has not stopped their spending with Lukas Hornicek the latest recruit

Last Update:

Newcastle have signed Czech goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek from Braga after meeting his release clause of £25.7million.

The 24-year-old has penned a five-year deal on Tyneside and becomes the second goalkeeper to arrive at St James’ Park this summer, following Ewen Jaouen through the door.

Newcastle have also signed Bazoumana Touré, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba since the end of last season after changing their recruitment model to target younger players.

However, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon have moved on, while captain Bruno Guimaraes is still agitating for a move for Arsenal, departures that are believed to have contributed to the exit of head coach Eddie Howe last week.

Matthias Jaissle is expected to be named the new Newcastle boss in the next 24 hours after compensation was agreed with his current club Al-Ahli.

Hornicek told the club’s official website: “The last few days have been an emotional rollercoaster from when I first heard about the move and now I’m so happy to be here. It’s a brilliant opportunity in a new league, which I’m very excited about.

“From the very first moment I arrived here, I received a fantastic welcome and really felt the warmth of the club. Everyone has been brilliant in helping me settle in.

“I know Newcastle is a huge football city, with 52,000 fans at St. James’ Park creating an incredible atmosphere and pushing the team every game. I can’t wait to play in front of them.”

Hornicek is one of Europe’s top young goalkeepers – Wilson

It has been a turbulent pre-season for Newcastle but sporting director Ross Wilson was pleased the club were still recruiting ahead of their first game, at home to Liverpool on August 23.

Wilson said of one-time Czechia International Hornicek: “I’m delighted to welcome Lukáš to Newcastle United. His progress in recent years has been remarkable and he has firmly established himself as one of Europe’s top young goalkeepers.

“We knew there would be no shortage of clubs interested in acquiring Lukáš this summer after everything he achieved last season, but it quickly became evident how keen he was to be a part of what we are building here.

“I’m really pleased we’ve able to conclude the deal swiftly, which has enabled Lukáš to join the squad during the opening days of our pre-season training camp in Spain.  Being here for the next week will only benefit him as he gets to know his new team-mates and coaching staff.”

articles.summary: Chelsea have added another new signing to their ranks this summer.
articles.content:
Chelsea sign Barco from Strasbourg on seven-year deal

Chelsea have added another new signing to their ranks this summer.

Last Update:

Chelsea have completed the signing of midfielder Valentin Barco from Strasbourg on a seven-year contract.

The 21-year-old becomes the Blues’ sixth arrival of the summer, following the signings of Morgan Rogers, Danny Welbeck, Emmanuel Emegha, Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra.

Chelsea have not disclosed the transfer fee.

Barco will link up with Enzo Maresca’s squad immediately and join the club’s pre-season tour ahead of next week’s friendly against Juventus in Hong Kong.

The Argentina international made one appearance at the 2026 World Cup as his country finished runners-up to Spain.

He also made headlines after being slapped by England midfielder Jude Bellingham following Argentina’s semi-final win.

Barco began his career with Boca Juniors before joining Brighton in 2024 in a deal worth £7.9 million.

After spending a season on the south coast, he moved to Strasbourg following a successful loan spell and established himself in Ligue 1.

He is the second player to swap Strasbourg for Chelsea this summer, with both clubs owned by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

The move is the 13th transfer completed between the two clubs since the start of last season.

articles.title: Real Madrid issue statement after FIFA U-turn as pressure grows on Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: Real Madrid have released a statement welcoming FIFA’s withdrawl of plans to sell off a minority stake in the World Cup as pressure on president Gianni Infantino grows. Infantino’s controversial World Cup plan sparked backlash from across the football landscape, with UEFA delcaring they had “lost confidence” in the Swiss administrator’s leadership following the collapse […]
articles.content:
Real Madrid issue statement after FIFA U-turn as pressure grows on Gianni Infantino

Last Update:

Real Madrid have released a statement welcoming FIFA’s withdrawl of plans to sell off a minority stake in the World Cup as pressure on president Gianni Infantino grows.

Infantino’s controversial World Cup plan sparked backlash from across the football landscape, with UEFA delcaring they had “lost confidence” in the Swiss administrator’s leadership following the collapse of his plans.

The investment proposal would have seen FIFA sell stakes in competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups to private investors, with member associations offered $40million (£30m) in return for backing the plans.

Now Real have made an official statement welcoming the withdrawal of the plans and supporting UEFA’s efforts to prevent them from coming to fruition – but stopped short of mentioning Infantino specifically.

A statement read: “Real Madrid welcomes FIFA’s decision to abandon its proposal for the partial sale of the commercial rights to its competitions.

“Our club believes this is good news for football, its institutions, and above all, for the millions of fans of our beloved sport.

“Real Madrid wishes to express its gratitude to UEFA, the confederations and federations, and all the institutions that firmly and responsibly opposed this project. Their unity and sense of duty protected football at a crucial moment.

“Clubs are the foundation upon which international football and the World Cup are built. They are the ones who discover, train, develop, and provide the national teams with the players who make these major competitions possible.

“International football and the World Cup are, above all, events of public interest, and they constitute a heritage that belongs to nations, fans, and society as a whole.

“Therefore, we believe they should never be treated as mere financial assets to be traded for the benefit of a select few.

“Real Madrid firmly opposes any attempt to sell future commercial revenue from competitions without assuming any of the associated costs or risks.

“It is the clubs that bear these costs and risks, and any initiative that seeks to appropriate future football revenue without assuming the responsibilities that generate it is unacceptable and should never be considered again.”

articles.title: Garnacho aims dig at Chelsea after making Aston Villa debut in Indonesia
articles.summary: Garnacho left Chelsea after only one season
articles.content:
Garnacho aims dig at Chelsea after making Aston Villa debut in Indonesia

Garnacho left Chelsea after only one season

Last Update:

Alejandro Garnacho aimed a subtle dig at Chelsea after playing his first game for Aston Villa since joining on a season-long loan.

The Argentine has made the switch to Villa Park from Chelsea initially on loan but with an obligation to buy, only a year after he left Manchester United to join the Blues.

He will be hopinh to reignite a stalled career under Unai Emery, having larely struggled in West London, and his latest post suggested he was pleased to put his time at Stamford Bridge behind him.

After starting in Villa’s 3-1 win over Indonesia All Stars, the 22-year-old posted a photo on his Instagram story with the caption: “See you soon Bangkok! First start after 3 months. Happy to be enjoying my football again. 1% every day. Thanks Indonesia!”

Garnacho was unable to get himself on the scoresheet in Indonesia but showed some positive moments in his first outing in a Villa shirt.

Goals from Emiliano Buendia, Ross Barkley and 17-year-old Brian Madjio secured the victory for the Europa League winners.

Emery excited aboout ‘new chaper’

Villa are preparing for a season in which they will compete in Europe for the fourth time under Emery, having ended a 30-year trophy drought by triumphing in the Europa League final in May.

Since then, however, the squad has had something of an overhaul, with Morgan Rogers leaving for Chelsea for £117million, while key midfielder Youri Tielemans has also left to join Manchester United.

The Midlands club have brought in Yohan Manzambi and Joao Gomes, as well as Garnacho, and Emery said he is excited for what lies ahead with his new-look squad.

“I am really optimistic. How we are building the team, how we are with a lot of chances and how we are responding every day,” Emery said.

“I want to tell all our supporters: we are coming back again with a new spirit, a new chapter. Really, I am excited.”

“After the first two weeks, we did our work in Birmingham. Now this camp is important in terms of how we are going to get fit and to adapt with the new players.

“Tactically, how we can, as soon as possible, try to understand our structure with the players we have.”

Emery also noted that several members of the squad are still due to return following their World Cup commitments. “Keep going, try to avoid injuries, try to adapt as better as possible in our structure, the players who are joining us.”
