articles.title: Gvardiol: Maresca ‘perfect’ for Manchester City and players knew Guardiola exit was coming
articles.summary: Maresca took charge of his first Man City game vs Inter Milan
articles.content:
Gvardiol: Maresca ‘perfect’ for Manchester City and players knew Guardiola exit was coming

Maresca took charge of his first Man City game vs Inter Milan

Last Update:

Josko Gvardiol says new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is a “perfect one” for the club.

Ex-Chelsea manager Maresca has been installed as Man City’s new manager following Pep Guardiola’s departure after 10 hugely successful years in charge at the end of last season.

The Italian, a former assistant to Guardiola at City, has signed a three-year deal at the Etihad, having won the Championship with Leciester and the Club World Cup and Conference League at Chelsea.

And after his first game in charge as City lost to Inter Milan on penalties in Hong Kong, Gvardiol is encouraged by how things have started so far.

“The level is that high and he has been chosen with reason as the manager,” said Gvardiol.

“I think he has a quality, has some new ideas and also we need to see what we are going to do [with] the style of [play], the football we are going to play and the tactics.

“I think he is a perfect one, but of course, it takes time. It’s something totally new, it’s not easy to change the manager, so we will take time.

“It’s our job to help him as much as possible and also to listen to try to adapt as quick as possible.

“I met him, we spoke a little bit about my injury [and] also how we played, how I played before with Pep, and that’s it, more or less.”

Table of Contents

Gvardiol: ‘We could feel Guardiola exit was coming’

Guardiola’s exit was finally confirmed at the end of the 2025-26 season after speculation throughout the campaign that it could be his final campaign in charge.

And Gvardiol, who missed a significant part of the season through injury, said the players could feel his exit was imminent.

“Some would say he could have told us earlier, some would say not,” said Gvardiol.

“I think it was perfect timing because it can affect you mentally if he would have said it earlier.

“We knew at some point he has to tell us. He has been here for 10 years and it is time to rest a little bit and retire. We could feel it.

“[The 2024-25 season] he was in between, about to leave, then he stayed – great because it was another season to try to win something. Two seasons ago we struggled, 13 games without winning.

“Unfortunately it was time [for him] to go but who knows with him, maybe after six months when he gets the energy back.”

Dias could be Man City captain

Man City are yet to confirm who will be captain under Maresca next season after Bernardo Silva’s departure to Real Madrid. Centre-back Ruben Dias and Spain skipper Rodri are candidates to take on the captain’s armband, and Gvardiol spoke highly of the former’s credentials.

Asked about the club’s leadership group, Gvardiol said: “It’s difficult to tell you about this but we need to see.

“Ruben is one of the leaders in our team and he is probably going to be on the top now – maybe the most important one.

“He will need some guys who have been here for a longer time. So if that’s on me, I will take responsibility.”

articles.summary: Casemiro had a home debut to forget for Inter Miami
articles.content:
MLS: Casemiro scores horror own goal as Messi returns for Inter Miami and Lewandowski opens account for Chicago Fire

Casemiro had a home debut to forget for Inter Miami

Last Update:

Lionel Messi was back in Major League Soccer action following the World Cup, but new signing Casemiro’s own goal dampeneded the Argentine’s return as Inter Miami drew 2-2 with Colombus Crew.

Elsewhere, Robert Lewandowski scored his first goals for Chicago Fire in a 2-1 win over Charlotte FC, while Los Angeles FC and Vancouver Whitecaps drew 1-1 in a top-of-the-table clash.

Table of Contents

Inter Miami 2-2 Colombus Crew: Messi makes return in draw

Messi was unable to find the net on his Inter Miami return as they were held by Colombus Crew.

Luis Suarez scored his seventh goal in four games to open the scoring for the Herons in the 16th minute.

But the game was levelled in the 34th minute when new signing Casemiro turned the ball into his own net, moments after giving the ball away in his own half.

But Suarez turned provider just before half-time as Noah Allen headed Miami in front, before Brais Mendez’s free-kick on his Colombus debut earned a point for the visitors.

Chicago Fire 2-1 Charlotte FC: Lewandowski opens account

Lewandowski scored a brace on his home debut for Chicago Fire in a 2-1 win over Charlotte FC.

Moments after Pep Biel had put the away side in front, the former Barcelona striker picked up the ball on the edge of the box and fired a clinical finish into the left-hand corner.

Lewandowski then put the hosts in front in the 68th minute as he latched onto a cross and headed in the winner, bolstering fourth-place Chicago’s play-off hopes.

LAFC 1-1 Vancouver Whitecaps: Son and Muller on target

LAFC and Vancouver Whitecaps remain top of the Western Conference after a 1-1 draw.

Former Tottenham captain Heung-Min Son netted his fourth goal in four games to open the scoring before half-time, days after his MVP-winning performance in the MLS All-Star game.

But LA had to settle for a draw when ex-Bayern Munich striker Thomas Muller converted a penalty.

articles.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal: Arteta coy on transfer but insists Gunners ‘very ambitious’
articles.summary: Arsenal are said to be exploring a move for Vincius Jr
articles.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal: Arteta coy on transfer but insists Gunners ‘very ambitious’

Arsenal are said to be exploring a move for Vincius Jr

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are “very ambitious” and “very active” in the summer transfer market amid speculation over a move for Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior.

Arsenal are said to be exploring a move for the Brazilian winger, albeit Real are adamant they do not want to sell one of their star players.

Still, the Premier League champions are believed to be sounding out a move for the 26-year-old, who is in the final year of his contract. Real’s signing of left-winger Yan Diomande has also fuelled speculation they may be preparing for life after Vinicius.

Pressed on Vincius Junior after Arsenal’s 4-1 pre-season win over Girona, Arteta simply laughed off the question – but did say they were plotting an ambitious summer, with only Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier arriving so far.

“We are very active, trying to improve and evolve the team,” the Spaniard said. “That’s clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

Arteta ‘pleased’ with Tzolis debut

One left-winger already at the club impressed against Girona, with summer signing Tzolis scoring on his first appearance for the club since joining from Club Brugge.

Arteta said: “I’m already pleased with him. First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, the team and the connection he’s already generating with the boys.

“You’re going to love the player. [He’s] very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes [and is] really good [at] linking up.

“He’s a boy who comes with so much hunger as well and wants to prove this is a dream for him. We are here to help him.”

articles.title: Jose Mourinho issues ‘extremely tired’ Real Madrid squad verdict: ‘I’m worried’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho saw Real Madrid draw with Fiorentina on Saturday
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho issues ‘extremely tired’ Real Madrid squad verdict: ‘I’m worried’

Jose Mourinho saw Real Madrid draw with Fiorentina on Saturday

Last Update:

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has admitted to concerns over his missing players and described his depleted squad as showing “three faces” in their friendly draw with Fiorentina in Austria.

Smart finishes by Endrick and 18-year-old winger Alexis Ciria put Mourinho’s new club 2-0 ahead after 24 minutes against their Serie A opponents, only for Roberto Piccoli’s strike before the break and Moise Kean’s header during the second half to secure La Viola a positive result.

“[Our] fresh side played very well,” said Mourinho, who is in his second spell as boss after joining from Benfica in June, speaking to Real Madrid TV (via AS).

“With a first half of such high quality, [the team] could have easily have been winning three or four to zero.

“Then the game became much more physical, [Fiorentina] put us under pressure, and the second face emerged.”

Table of Contents

Real Madrid vs Fiorentina: Mourinho ‘liked everything’

Mourinho believes his starting centre-back pairing of 18-year-old Joan Martinez and 19-year-old Mario Rivas had a “fantastic game” but are “physically not yet at the level” to deal with former Juventus and Everton striker Kean.

“The third face, which I really liked, is the extremely tired team [who] still managed to be a team [and] managed to regain control of the game,” he added, predicting a “fantastic future” for Martinez and Rivas, who he said showed “tremendous class”.

The Portuguese singled out new signing Denzel Dumfries, who started on the right wing with Trent Alexander-Arnold, and Endrick, who was returning after Brazil’s World Cup campaign, as well as forward Carlos Espi, a recruit from Levante for around £21.4 million this week.

“[Dumfries and Endrick] trained for three days and played more than 70 minutes,” explained Mourinho. “A fantastic effort that means a lot to me. I thanked them for what they gave us. I liked everything.

“Then we brought in poor Carlos, who’s waking up from a dream. He trained for an hour yesterday and helped us today to understand what Real Madrid is all about.”

Real Madrid: Mourinho on Vinicius Junior, Brahim Diaz, Bernardo Silva

While Mourinho was “very happy” with his squad’s work, the 63-year-old is anxious about a lack of time on the training pitch with key players who are resting after the World Cup.

Madrid travel to Espanyol in their La Liga opener on August 22 (20:30 BST). “I’m worried about not having the others,” conceded Mourinho.

“I’d like to have three weeks with all of them too, but it’s not possible. Vini [Vinicius Junior], Brahim [Diaz] and Bernardo Silva arrive on Monday.

“Dumfries, Carlos, and Endrick will have more days of training… and so on until the others arrive. Of the seven first-team players we had available [against Fiorentina], two of them have only had three training sessions.

“This is Real Madrid with the players we have. As I told the lads before the match: Real Madrid is Real Madrid, even in friendlies.

“I had to put on the pitch the men – in quotes – I had available. We only worked yesterday; we did some organisational work.”

The result is the first time Jose Mourinho has failed to win since his return to Madrid, having overseen two friendly victories in July.

Real Madrid team vs Fiorentina

Mourinho did not make his first change until he brought on Jorge Cestero for Ciria in the 64th minute.

Espi came off the bench in the 75th minute. Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Aurelien Tchouameni, Ibrahima Konate and Marc Cucurella are among the players yet to return to training.

Antonio Rudiger has rejoined the squad after his post-World Cup break but the defender was not involved.

Real Madrid starting XI: Andriy Lunin, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Joan Martinez, Mario Rivas, Alvaro Carreras, Eduardo Camavinga, Federico Valverde, Arda Guler, Denzel Dumfries, Alexis Ciria, Endrick

Real Madrid substitutes: Sergio Mestre, Javi Navarro, Carlos Espi, Lamini Fati, Jesus Fortea, Jorge Cestero, Pablo Lacosta, Aimar Garcia, Daniel Yanez, Jacobo

articles.content:
Maresca picks out player who impressed him most in Manchester City debut

Enzo Maresca has given his thoughts on his first outing as Manchester City boss.

Last Update:

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca has praised Ryan McAidoo after the teenager caught the eye in the club’s pre-season opener against Inter Milan.

McAidoo, 18, made a lively impact from the bench during Saturday’s 1-1 draw in Hong Kong, repeatedly troubling the Inter defence before City were beaten on penalties.

The academy graduate, who operates on the right wing, twice went close to finding a late winner and earned praise from Maresca after the match.

“We were speaking with the club and since day one I said he is the kind of winger I love,” Maresca said.

“He is very aggressive one-v-one, he always tries, makes the right decisions. But he is very young and he needs the right path.

“If you look at the last clubs I was part of, I always asked for those kinds of wingers.

“You have to follow the right process, but then you need players out wide who can beat defenders one-v-one.

“Antoine [Semenyo], Savinho and Ryan were very good. We need to add more solutions for them and they will be better.”

McAidoo leads impressive academy outing

McAidoo made his senior debut for City in last season’s FA Cup win over Exeter City before playing a key role in the club’s FA Youth Cup triumph.

He was one of seven academy graduates to feature against Inter, with several more included in City’s squad for their three-match Asia tour.

Maresca said no decisions have yet been made over whether the club’s young players will remain with the first team this season or head out on loan.

“At the moment, with most of the young players, the idea was to see them during pre-season and then decide,” he said.

“We started 10 days ago and Ryan is working well. We are going to take the right decision. I am always very open with young players.

“At Leicester, it was a record number of debuts from the academy and at Chelsea it was also a record number of debuts from the academy.”

Man City away kit 2026/27: Full details on new shirt and strip

All you need to know about Man City's 2026/27 away kit

Last Update:

Reigning FA Cup and EFL Cup champions Manchester City have released their new Puma away shirt as part of the club’s kit for the 2026/27 season.

The shirt, which was unveiled in July as part of the club’s pre-season tour of Hong Kong, is black and yellow and finished with a swarm of worker bees.

Erling Haaland, Vivianne Miedema, Phil Foden, Bunny Shaw, Antoine Semenyo, Jade Rose, Omar Marmoush, Kerstin Casparij and Marc Guehi are among the stars to have shown off the kit.

Here are the key details on the release, including the story behind the design and how to buy the new kit.

Table of Contents

Man City away kit: When will Premier League side wear new shirt?

The kit was revealed in Hong Kong on July 30, with a floating vessel pitch hosting a local community tournament and player appearances.

City will wear it for the first time when they face Italian giants Inter in Hong Kong on August 1 (12:30 BST).

Manchester City away kit 2026/27 full design details

The bee is a familiar symbol around the streets of Manchester, described by City as demonstrating the “graft, unity and resilience” that “define” Manchester.

The kit aims to “channel the noise of the away end and the identity of the streets back home”. “Doesn’t matter if you were born in Manchester or just buzzin’ to be here,” City add. “The bee says you’re one of us.”

“I’ve never seen something like this floating pitch and I’m a little jealous of everyone who’s getting to play on it right now,” Foden said at the launch.

“The kit is something special, so I’m looking forward to wearing it this season as we do our best to make you all proud.”

Puma’s Dominique Gathier said the design aimed to give City’s players the best possible playing materials while “carrying real meaning for the city and its fans”.

“We wanted every detail to reflect the identity of this club and the culture around it,” explained Gathier.

“It’s a shirt built for the pitch but made to be worn with pride well beyond it.”

How to buy Man City 26/27 away kit

The kit is available from City’s online shop and the Etihad Stadium and Arndale and Trafford Centre shopping outlets in Manchester.

“The worker bee is one of Manchester’s most enduring and recognisable symbols and represents the values that have shaped our city for generations: hard work, resilience, community, and pride,” said Councillor Shazia Butt, Executive Member for Culture Leisure and Libraries at Manchester City Council.

“We’ve worked closely with [City and Puma] to ensure its use on the [kit] is authentic and respectful of its significance.

“Seeing the bee showcased to a global audience through one of Manchester’s most recognised institutions is a fitting celebration of our city, our people and the spirit that continues to define Manchester today.”

How much does the 26/27 Manchester City away kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Arsenal replica shirt is £85 or £90 for a long-sleeved version, while the authentic versions start at £130, with personalised or player names and numbers available at an additional cost.

Youth shirts start at £60. A baby kit is available for £45. The shorts cost between £30 and £48.

Accompanying socks cost between £18 and £20. A range of other clothing and items in the away colours are available.

When does Man City’s 2026/27 Premier League season start?

City face Arsenal in the Community Shield at Wembley Stadium on August 16 at 15:00 BST (10:00 ET / 07:00 PT).

Enzo Maresca’s side are at home to Bournemouth in their first match of the Premier League season. Here are the key details.

articles.title: BREAKING: UEFA loses confidence in FIFA boss Infantino
articles.summary: UEFA has lost confidence in FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.
articles.content:
BREAKING: UEFA loses confidence in FIFA boss Infantino

UEFA has lost confidence in FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.

Last Update:

UEFA has declared it has lost confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the collapse of his controversial proposal to sell stakes in the governing body’s competitions to private investors.

The proposal was officially abandoned on Saturday following widespread opposition from football’s major confederations, with UEFA having previously threatened to boycott FIFA competitions if the plans went ahead.

In a strongly-worded statement, European football’s governing body said the fallout had severely damaged confidence in FIFA’s leadership.

“The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family,” the statement read.

UEFA also accused Infantino of failing to deliver on the promises he made when he was elected FIFA president in 2016.

The investment proposal would have seen FIFA sell stakes in competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups to private investors, with member associations offered $40 million (£30m) in return for backing the plans.

However, resistance from UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation ultimately forced Infantino to abandon the project.

The FIFA president admitted on Saturday that the proposal had “created divisions” that were “no longer in the interest” of its original objective.

articles.title: FIFA abandon controversial World Cup plan after backlash
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino says he is scrapping his plan to commercialise the World Cup.
articles.content:
FIFA abandon controversial World Cup plan after backlash

Gianni Infantino says he is scrapping his plan to commercialise the World Cup.

Last Update:

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has abandoned his controversial proposal to sell stakes in the governing body’s competitions to private investors after facing overwhelming opposition from football’s major confederations.

Infantino confirmed the plan would no longer go ahead, admitting it had created divisions that were “no longer in the interest” of the project’s original objective.

The proposal would have offered FIFA’s 211 member associations $40 million (£30m) each in exchange for backing private investment in competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups.

However, UEFA threatened to boycott FIFA competitions if the plans proceeded, while Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) also rejected the proposal, leaving the FIFA president with little chance of securing the support needed.

“As a result, this proposal will not proceed,” Infantino said.

“Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve.

“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game.”

The announcement follows several days of mounting pressure on the 56-year-old, with senior FIFA figures distancing themselves from the proposal.

FIFA insiders ‘deceived’

Chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said the organisation’s own administration had been “deceived” over the project, while senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned, describing the proposal as “a bad deal for football” that would “mortgage football’s future”.

Concacaf, which governs football across North, Central America and the Caribbean, rejected the plan after a meeting of its member associations, while the AFC publicly backed UEFA and Concacaf’s stance.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also criticised the proposal, calling Infantino “the wrong man” to lead FIFA.

The collapse of the plan leaves Infantino facing increasing scrutiny ahead of the FIFA presidential election in March, where he is expected to seek a fourth term in office.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa welcomed the decision to withdraw the proposal.

“The future of global football must always be shaped through proper consultation, collective dialogue and respect for the established governance structures of our game,” he said.

Infantino had initially insisted FIFA would continue with the proposals despite opposition, arguing that “nobody is selling football”.

But with UEFA’s 55 members, Concacaf’s 35 associations and the AFC’s 46 members all opposed, the proposal no longer had a realistic path to securing the majority support required from FIFA’s 211 member associations.

The governing bodies in Africa and Oceania had planned to discuss the proposal later this month, while South American confederation CONMEBOL had requested further clarification before taking a position.

articles.title: Barcelona boss Flick backs Gordon but talks up Rashford: ‘I’ll miss him’
articles.summary: Hansi Flick has reflected on his decision not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently
articles.content:
Barcelona boss Flick backs Gordon but talks up Rashford: ‘I’ll miss him’

Hansi Flick has reflected on his decision not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently

Last Update:

Hansi Flick says he will “miss” Marcus Rashford after sending the on-loan forward back to Manchester United and signing Anthony Gordon to replace the England international.

Rashford helped Barca win La Liga last season, contributing 14 goals and 11 assists in 49 appearances before the Spanish side decided against paying a fee of around £30 million to keep him permanently.

“I really appreciate having worked with him,” said Flick (via Marca), who bought Three Lions winger Gordon for £69.3m from Newcastle in May.

“Loans don’t always lead to permanent transfers. I’m grateful for his work. I’ll miss him. But Anthony Gordon has arrived and he’s very keen to start working with us.”

Table of Contents

Barcelona signings: Flick ‘happy with the team’

Karim Adeyemi made his non-competitive Barca debut by playing the first 45 minutes of their first pre-season friendly at English second-tier club Birmingham City on Friday.

The Germany forward arrived for £18.8m from Borussia Dortmund this month but was overshadowed by 18-year-old Egypt international Hamza Abdelkarim, who scored twice in Barca’s 2-2 draw before they were beaten 3-2 on penalties.

“He has a lot of potential but he has things to improve,” Flick said of 24-year-old Adeyemi. “He’s only had a week of training. He can give us a lot.

“[Abdelkarim’s] very humble, has a good character and a lot of potential. He’s a striker and is well-positioned in the box. He’s very aware of the area, which is what I ask of a number 9.”

Flick was non-committal when he was asked about the prospect of Barca signing a striker. “I’m focused on the team I have,” he replied.

“I don’t talk about those who aren’t here. We have big goals this season, as always, and I’m happy with the team.

“What’s important is the team, the mentality, the attitude.”

Birmingham City vs Barcelona

Abdelkarim initially equalised by converting a 41st-minute penalty after being fouled by Christoph Klarer.

Birmingham had taken the lead in the 31st minute when August Priske headed in Alex Cochrane’s cross but Abdelkarim turned the scoreline around 15 minutes after half-time, sweeping in from close range when goalkeeper James Beadle spilled Roony Bardghji’s long-range effort.

Barcelona’s second goal was a deserved one on the balance of play and Birmingham, who are co-owned by NFL icon Tom Brady, responded admirably to regain control and equalise through new £6 million signing Jhon Solis’ finish from Christoph Klarer’s header.

Cochrane went closest to a winner by arrowing a drive against the top of the crossbar before Jack Robinson cleared Alex Gonzalez’s shot off the line during the closing stages.

Beadle made a superb double save during added time, springing to either side of his line to repel strikes by the impressive Roony Bardghji and Gonzalez, then made two saves in his team’s 3-2 shootout win.

What’s next for Barcelona?

Barca, who began their pre-season schedule without their World Cup stars at a sold-out stadium, face a club in Birmingham’s division when they meet Preston North End behind closed doors on Monday,

Spain players and newly-crowned world champions Lamine Yamal, Ferran Torres, Joan Garcia, Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Gavi, Dani Olmo and Pedri are among the stars absent from their trip.

Birmingham travel to fellow Championship club Swansea City in the EFL Cup first round on August 8 (15:00 BST).

Barcelona team vs Birmingham City

Alejandro Balde was on the bench as the left-back continued his injury comeback and winger Raphinha has taken part in individual sessions this week following an injury-hit 2025/26 and World Cup with Brazil.

Frenkie de Jong was not involved but has travelled with Barcelona and worked in the gym as the midfielder continues his recovery from a serious knee injury.

Barcelona starting XI: Wojciech Szczesny, Xavi Espart, Andreas Christensen, Gerard Martin, Jofre Torrents, Marc Casado, Ebrima Tunkara, Marc Bernal, Karim Adeyemi, Hamza Abdelkarim, Shane Kluivert

Barcelona substitutes: Hector Fort, Alejandro Balde, Ronald Araujo, Alvaro Cortes, Guille Fernandez, Brian Farinas, Tommy Marques, Raphinha, Roony Bardghji, Toni Fernandez, Fermin Lopez, Jordi Pesquer, Iker Rodriguez, Ibrahim Diarra, Oscar Gistau, Orian Goren, Aron Yaakobishvili, Alex Gonzalez

articles.title: Real Madrid open to selling Vinicius Junior if Brazilian does not lower wage demands
articles.summary: Real Madrid could sell Vinicius Junior this summer should he not sign a new contract with the club.
articles.content:
Real Madrid open to selling Vinicius Junior if Brazilian does not lower wage demands

Real Madrid could sell Vinicius Junior this summer should he not sign a new contract with the club.

Last Update:

Real Madrid are open to selling Vinicius Junior if they fail to reach an agreement over a new contract, according to reports.

The Brazil international is due back for pre-season training on Monday following his post-World Cup break, but uncertainty remains over his future with just one year left on his current deal.

Club officials are reportedly unwilling to improve their latest contract offer and believe the next move is down to Vinicius, who must decide whether to extend his stay at the Bernabeu or pursue a move elsewhere.

Table of Contents

Arsenal remain interested

Arsenal are understood to be monitoring the situation closely and believe they would be well placed to make a move if Vinicius decides to leave Madrid.

However, sources close to the 26-year-old insist there has been no contact with the Premier League champions.

Negotiations over a new contract have dragged on for months, with Vinicius previously deciding to postpone talks until after the World Cup.

The winger has been at Madrid since joining from Flamengo in 2018 and has developed into one of the world’s leading attackers, scoring in two Champions League finals and finishing runner-up in the 2024 Ballon d’Or voting.

Rodri and Diomande targets

Vinicius endured a frustrating campaign last season, reportedly becoming unhappy under former manager Xabi Alonso and showing his frustration after being substituted during El Clasico.

Madrid have been active in the transfer market this summer, adding Carlos Espi to their squad, while also closing in on deals for Yan Diomande and Manchester City midfielder Rodri.

Jose Mourinho’s side begin their pre-season schedule against Fiorentina in Austria on Saturday, with new signings Denzel Dumfries and Espi included in the travelling squad.

articles.title: Prime Minister Andy Burnham calls out Infantino as ‘wrong man’ to lead FIFA
articles.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has come under fire for trying to sell commercial rights to the World Cup.
articles.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham calls out Infantino as ‘wrong man’ to lead FIFA

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has come under fire for trying to sell commercial rights to the World Cup.

Last Update:

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign amid growing opposition to plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to a private equity group.

Burnham, who became Britain’s Prime Minister earlier this month, described the proposal as an “outrageous suggestion” as pressure continues to mount on Infantino following criticism from football’s continental governing bodies.

UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have all rejected the proposal, while UEFA’s 55 member associations have agreed to boycott FIFA competitions for as long as the plans remain active.

That would see major footballing nations including England, Germany, France and reigning world champions Spain refuse to compete in both the men’s and women’s World Cups unless the proposal is withdrawn.

Burnham speaks out

Speaking on Friday, Burnham became the first leader of a major nation to publicly call for Infantino to step down.

“My view is strengthening – this was an outrageous suggestion,” Burnham said.

“The idea that it could even be brought forward, in my view, shows that the FIFA president is the wrong man to lead the organisation.”

The Labour leader had already criticised the proposal earlier this week, insisting football should never be treated as a commercial asset.

“Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine,” Burnham wrote on social media.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.

“Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Eddie Howe breaks silence on Newcastle exit – ‘privilege of my lifetime’
articles.summary: Eddie Howe has given his first public reaction to leaving Newcastle
articles.content:
BREAKING: Eddie Howe breaks silence on Newcastle exit – ‘privilege of my lifetime’

Eddie Howe has given his first public reaction to leaving Newcastle

Last Update:

Eddie Howe says he gave his “life, heart and soul” to Newcastle in the head coach’s first statement since leaving the Magpies after nearly five years in charge on Thursday.

Englishman Howe’s departure, which came a day after a 4-1 friendly defeat to Championship club Bristol City, has been part of a turbulent summer for the club featuring the sales of England winger Anthony Gordon and Italy playmaker Sandro Tonali, with Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes also thought to be closing in on a move to Arsenal.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know, in my heart, that it’s the right one,” said Howe.

“I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made while I’ve been here and this one is no different.

“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.”

Table of Contents

Eddie Howe: Full statement on Newcastle exit

“After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United,” Howe said in a statement on Newcastle’s website.

“After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one.

“I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made while I’ve been here and this one is no different.

“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

“It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean – and will always mean – to me and my family.

“From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms.

“We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

“There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St James’ Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

“Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy [the 2024/25 EFL Cup] in 70 years.

“These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life. I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to [hierarchy] Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solis and everyone at [owners the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund], [executives] David Hopkinson [and Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

“I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

“Thank you to [backroom staff] Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

“A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it’s been an honour to have coached you all.

“Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day.

“To stand on the touchline at St James’ Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

“While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

“Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.”

Eddie Howe: What have Newcastle said about manager?

The club said Howe’s arrival at St. James’ Park came at a “pivotal moment” in November 2021, having been appointed shortly after the fund took over.

Newcastle noted that Howe steered them to the Champions League in 2023 and 2025 and reached the knockout phase for the first time in the club’s history last season, going out to Barcelona in the last 16.

“Along the way, Eddie helped deliver some of the most memorable moments in Newcastle United’s recent history,” they said.

“His passion, dedication and connection with the city, the club and its fans have been strong throughout his time in the north-east and he has helped to establish foundations that have positioned the club strongly for the future.”

Chief executive Hopkinson said Newcastle were “naturally disappointed” by Howe’s decision.

“Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone… and with a lasting place in the club’s history,” added Hopkinson.

“We remain immensely thankful for everything he has done for the club. On behalf of our owners, board, players, staff and supporters, I would like to extend sincere thanks to Eddie for his outstanding service and leadership and wish him and his family every success and happiness for the future.”

Wilson echoed Hopkinson’s tribute. Newcastle said the process to replace Howe is “at an advanced stage”, with Matthias Jassle expected to be appointed.

articles.title: BREAKING: Chelsea winger Mudryk free to play after FA and WADA agreement
articles.summary: Mykhailo Mudryk can resume his playing career with Chelsea after serving his suspension
articles.content:
BREAKING: Chelsea winger Mudryk free to play after FA and WADA agreement

Mykhailo Mudryk can resume his playing career with Chelsea after serving his suspension

Last Update:

Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk is eligible to play with immediate effect after the Football Association (FA) and World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) confirmed his ban for breaches of anti-doping regulations has now been served.

Mudryk was handed a four-year sanction by an independent regulatory commission after testing positive for a low concentration of the banned substance meldonium in October 2024.

But changes to WADA’s rules mean that if Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations (ADVRs) would have resulted.

However, following talks between Mudryk and the Football Association, with the agreement of WADA, the Ukraine international has accepted that he had committed the ADRVs he was charged with and agreed to a period of ineligibility equal to the time already served.

In a statement, the FA confirmed the 25-year-old is no longer ineligible and can now resume his career, with some reports suggesting he will fly out to Asia to join Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Table of Contents

The most difficult period of my career, admits Mudryk

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 and admits it has been a hugely challenging period in his life.

He said: “After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.

“I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future. This has been the most difficult period of my career.

“As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance. My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.

“I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period. I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my team-mates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout.

“I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case. My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch. Thank you to everyone who continued to believe in me. I look forward to the next chapter of my career.”

Chelsea now focused on reintegrating Mudryk into first-team squad

Mudryk joined Chelsea in January 2023 from Ukrainian club Shakhtar Donetsk in a deal worth an initial £59million, signing a contract until 2031.

He made 53 appearances for the West London club before being suspended.

His return is a boost for Chelsea, and new boss Xabi Alonso.

A Chelsea statement read: “From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

“We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

“We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.”

articles.title: Chelsea hit with FA fine and transfer sanctions after breaching agent rules
articles.summary: Chelsea have been hit with another sanction for breaking financial rules.
articles.content:
Chelsea hit with FA fine and transfer sanctions after breaching agent rules

Chelsea have been hit with another sanction for breaking financial rules.

Last Update:

Chelsea have been fined £10 million and handed a suspended transfer ban after admitting multiple breaches of Football Association rules relating to payments made to agents and third parties between 2009 and 2022.

The FA confirmed the Blues have also avoided a points deduction after a suspended six-point penalty was overturned on appeal, with the punishment instead reduced to financial sanctions.

The breaches were uncovered after Chelsea’s current owners, Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital, voluntarily reported 74 potential rule violations following their takeover of the club in 2022.

Chelsea admitted making £47 million in undisclosed payments to unregistered agents and third parties linked to player transfers between 2011 and 2018, during Roman Abramovich’s ownership.

As part of the punishment, the club received a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows, which will only come into effect if further breaches are committed before June 30, 2027.

The FA said it was continuing to investigate “individual misconduct arising out of this case”.

Chelsea’s initial financial penalty of £26 million was reduced after the club’s extensive cooperation with the investigation.

Chelsea get away with more rule breaks

The fine was first cut by a third to £17.25 million because of Chelsea’s self-reporting and what the independent regulatory commission described as “exceptional and unprecedented” cooperation.

It was then reduced to £11.4 million after the club entered an early guilty plea, before being lowered to £10 million to reflect separate financial penalties already imposed by UEFA and the Premier League.

The FA said the final sanction was “an appropriate penalty” that would both punish Chelsea and “deter similar misconduct and maintain the integrity of the game”.

The £10 million fine will be invested into grassroots football.

In its written reasons, the regulatory commission said: “Had the club not brought these matters to the attention of the FA, it is unlikely that they would have been discovered.”

The panel also explained that the suspended six-point deduction had been set aside because neither the FA nor the Premier League sought a sporting sanction.

The latest punishment follows another disciplinary case earlier this year, when Chelsea received a nine-month academy transfer ban and a £750,000 fine over breaches relating to the registration of youth players between 2019 and 2022.

articles.title: City boss Maresca dismisses reports of Real Madrid move for Rodri as ‘speculation’ and insists Spain skipper will return to Manchester
articles.summary: Manchester City face a fight this summer to keep key midfielder Rodri in the face of interest from Real Madrid
articles.content:
City boss Maresca dismisses reports of Real Madrid move for Rodri as ‘speculation’ and insists Spain skipper will return to Manchester

Manchester City face a fight this summer to keep key midfielder Rodri in the face of interest from Real Madrid

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca reiterated the importance of Rodri to Manchester City and claimed reports he is poised to join Real Madrid were just “speculation”.

The 30-year-old has 12 months left on his contract at the Etihad and is a key target this summer for Madrid with their president Florentino Perez performing a u-turn having said previously they weren’t interested in the former Atletico man.

Rodri is currently sidelined having undergone a minor back operation but that is not expected to prevent Madrid from making an offer in the next 48 hours that could rise to £51million.

Speaking before City’s pre-season clash with Inter Milan in Hong Kong tomorrow, Maresca said: “It’s just speculation at the moment. Rodri had the surgery last Monday; everything was fine. Now, some days off and he’ll be back with us when he finishes his holiday.

“The main focus for him when the season finished was the World Cup. Now, he is enjoying some rest after that and we didn’t have any conversations just focused on Rodri.”

Table of Contents

Rodri is ‘very important’ to City, says Maresca

Asked to outline the importance of the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, who was also the recipient of the 2026 World Cup Golden Ball for best player after captaining his country to the title, to City in his first season in charge, Maresca replied: “Very important. I said in the first press conference that any manager in the world wants Rodri because he’s a top player; so it’s important for me, the club and for everyone.

“But now, he needs his holiday – that’s very important when we start to play every three days.”

Having already lost Bernardo SIlva to Madrid this summer, City would be reluctant to sanction the departure of another experienced midfielder.

They have brought in England international Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and are believed to be closing in on Lille’s Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi.

City not done in the window just yet

And Maresca hinted City might be in the market for more players before the season gets underway next month.

He said: “We are talking with [sporting director] Hugo [Viana], with the club about some targets. It’s a normal situation when the transfer window is open, anything can happen. For sure, we are going to do something but we are looking at different positions.

“In this moment, we have, as you know, many young players here. Tomorrow, three of the senior players are going to arrive and slowly, the rest. I’m happy at the moment to work with the ones who are here.”

articles.title: I only joined Inter Miami to play with Lionel Messi, says Casemiro
articles.summary: Lionel Messi's presence at Inter Miami persuaded Casemiro to join the MLS side
articles.content:
I only joined Inter Miami to play with Lionel Messi, says Casemiro

Lionel Messi's presence at Inter Miami persuaded Casemiro to join the MLS side

Last Update:

Casemiro says he rejected several offers from around the world to join Inter Miami and play with “the God of football”, Lionel Messi.

The 34-year-old Brazil international left Manchester United in June when his contract expired and says he based his decision on moving to Major League Soccer on the opportunity to play with his fellow South American.

Casemiro, who has signed an initial 12-month deal with the option for a further two years, said: “For me, without a doubt, I am coming only to play with the best player of all time.

“I want to enjoy, I want to help him to keep winning because he is a winner. Another player is joining who wants to win, who wants to compete.

“I am where I want to be in MLS. I left United as a free agent, I had options in Italy, other teams in different places, but I am where I want to be … I want to enjoy being with him, helping him win and making him bigger. He’s one of, if not the god of football and I want to help.”

I dreamed of playing with Messi – Casemiro

Casemiro has experience of playing against Messi when the pair were rivals at Real Madrid and Barcelona and is now relishing the chance to help Miami clinch more silverware. Since Messi joined from Paris Saint-Germain, the Floridian club have won the 2023 Leagues Cup trophy, the 2024 Supporters’ Shield and 2025 MLS Cup.

They are currently second in the Eastern Conference.

“The amount of problems Messi gave me, of course I dreamed of playing with him,” added Casemiro, who made his Miami debut in the 1-0 win at CF Montreal on Saturday.

“I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed help from my team-mates. I am very happy that I am now with him, and I want to keep winning with him.”

Messi is back in Miami and regaining full fitness after an extended break following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final where they lost 1-0 to Spain.

He won’t be considered when Miami face the Columbus Crew this weekend.

articles.title: Infantino’s senior advisor quits; is this the beginning of the end for controversial FIFA president?
articles.summary: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino appears to have lost the support of his inner circle as the backlash against his FFE plan continues
articles.content:
Infantino’s senior advisor quits; is this the beginning of the end for controversial FIFA president?

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino appears to have lost the support of his inner circle as the backlash against his FFE plan continues

Last Update:

Gianni Infantino’s position as FIFA president was looking increasingly tenuous on Friday after one of his senior advisors quit as the backlash over the controversial FFE plan gained traction.

Infantino’s proposal to sell stakes in its flagship events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to investors and form a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) – could prove to be his downfall after a groundswell of opposition.

UEFA and CONCACAF outlined their disapproval yesterday and were joined on Friday by the Asian Football Confederation. Infantino requires 106 of the 2011 MAs to give their approval for the scheme to progress. The rejection from UEFA and CONCACAF means 96 have already said no, making the AFC’s input critical.

And while their statement did not necessarily indicate their 47 MAs would vote against the proposals, it is clear that is what they would advise.

The discord has also spread to Infantino’s inner circle with one of his right-hand men, Carlos Cordeiro, quitting in protest.

Former banker Cordeiro said in a damning statement: “It is a bad deal for FIFA’s Member Associations (MAs), a bad deal for football and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

“FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources. The organisation sits on billions of dollars in reserves and no debt. The FIFA president himself has highlighted the $15bn in revenue generated between 2022 and 2026. If MAs believe additional investment is needed to develop the game, FIFA already has the financial capacity to provide that support from its existing resources. Against that backdrop, selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense.”

Table of Contents

Who benefits from FFE, asks Cordeiro?

FIFA says Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – would lead the investor group. It has been reported Infantino would become the CEO of FFE and command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

Cordeiro added: “Most troubling of all is the absence of answers to fundamental questions. Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?”

Cordeiro’s decision to quit comes after a wounding 24 hours for Infantino.

Already bruised by UEFA saying their MAs would boycott any FIFA-sanctioned event until the proposal was dropped altogether, two more confederations voiced their opposition, the latest being the AFC.

Their statement read: “The AFC has observed with deep concern the developments of recent days relating to the proposed establishment of FFE and the uncertainty that has emerged across the global football community.

“The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game. Football should never have been placed in such a position.

“Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by UEFA and CONCACAF, as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward. The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world’s leading football nations. Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.”

AFC attack FIFA processes

The AFC statement also attacked the lack of due process in the FFE scheme and believes it is part of a wider problem.

It continued: “While the immediate debate centres on FFE, the AFC considers this issue extends far beyond a single proposal. Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed. While the AFC notes FIFA’s latest clarification on the proposal, the central concerns surrounding governance, institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered.

“A proposal of such significance, with the potential to affect the commercial, sporting and strategic future of world football, must not emerge through processes that leave Confederations, Member Associations (MAs) and even FIFA’s own governing bodies, including the FIFA Council, feeling sidelined. The primary objective for world football must be to ensure that decisions of such magnitude are being developed through processes that are anchored on transparency and command the confidence of the football community.

“This is not the first occasion where major stakeholders have been confronted with significant initiatives after the direction of travel appears to have already been determined. Such an approach undermines confidence in FIFA’s governance framework and diminishes the authority of its statutory bodies. No subsequent consultation process, however well intentioned, can replace early engagement with the appropriate FIFA bodies and the football family.

“The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform.”

FIFA blame media after backlash

FIFA responded this morning, blaming “incorrect media reports” for the negativity.

A FIFA statement read: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FFE and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

“FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.

“Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world. Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of FIFA.”

When will UEFA’s resolve be tested?

The first chance for UEFA to follow through on their boycott threat will come at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which gets underway on September 5 in Poland.

FIFA have said MAs will receive £30m each under the proposal and have access to an initial £15m if they back the plan by a deadline of September 19.

That raises the possibility of UEFA countries pulling out of the Under-20 tournament midway through.

articles.title: AFC side with UEFA and CONCACAF in major blow to FIFA’s World Cup sell-off plan
articles.summary: The Asian Football Confederation could have put the kibosh on Gianni Infantino's plans to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup
articles.content:
AFC side with UEFA and CONCACAF in major blow to FIFA’s World Cup sell-off plan

The Asian Football Confederation could have put the kibosh on Gianni Infantino's plans to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup

Last Update:

Gianni Infantino’s proposal to sell off part of FIFA’s major tournaments is looking in serious jeopardy after the Asian Football Federation (AFC) on Friday joined UEFA and CONCACAF in expressing its “serious concerns”.

FIFA’s idea is to sell stakes in its flagship events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to investors and form a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). FIFA says Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – will lead the investor group.

UEFA was quick to outline its disapproval with its 55 Member Associations (MAs) also vowing to boycott any FIFA-sanctioned event until the plan was shelved, while CONCACAF also gave it a thumbs down.

Infantino requires 106 of the 2011 MAs to give their approval for the scheme to progress. The rejection from UEFA and CONCACAF means 96 have already said no, making the AFC’s input critical.

And while their statement did not necessarily indicate their 47 MAs would vote against the proposals, it is clear that is what they would advise.

The statement read: “The AFC has observed with deep concern the developments of recent days relating to the proposed establishment of FFE and the uncertainty that has emerged across the global football community.

“The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game. Football should never have been placed in such a position.

“Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by UEFA and CONCACAF, as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward. The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world’s leading football nations. Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.”

Table of Contents

AFC attack FIFA processes

The AFC statement also attacked the lack of due process in the FFE scheme and believes it is part of a wider problem.

It continued: “While the immediate debate centres on FFE, the AFC considers this issue extends far beyond a single proposal. Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed. While the AFC notes FIFA’s latest clarification on the proposal, the central concerns surrounding governance, institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered.

“A proposal of such significance, with the potential to affect the commercial, sporting and strategic future of world football, must not emerge through processes that leave Confederations, Member Associations (MAs) and even FIFA’s own governing bodies, including the FIFA Council, feeling sidelined. The primary objective for world football must be to ensure that decisions of such magnitude are being developed through processes that are anchored on transparency and command the confidence of the football community.

“This is not the first occasion where major stakeholders have been confronted with significant initiatives after the direction of travel appears to have already been determined. Such an approach undermines confidence in FIFA’s governance framework and diminishes the authority of its statutory bodies. No subsequent consultation process, however well intentioned, can replace early engagement with the appropriate FIFA bodies and the football family.

“The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform.”

FIFA blames media for negative response to FFE scheme

The AFC’s stance is a major blow to FIFA and Infantino, in particular.

Having been criticised by UEFA and CONCACAF in the past 24 hours, FIFA responded this morning, blaming “incorrect media reports” for the negativity.

A FIFA statement read: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FFE and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

“FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.

“Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world. Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of FIFA.”

When will UEFA’s resolve be tested?

The first chance for UEFA to follow through on their boycott threat will come at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which gets underway on September 5 in Poland.

FIFA have said MAs will receive £30m each under the proposal and have access to an initial £15m if they back the plan by a deadline of September 19.

That raises the possibility of UEFA countries pulling out of the Under-20 tournament midway through.

Infantino advisor quits

The FFE scheme could result in the downfall of Infantino, who was expected to be a shoo-in to retain his position as president when the next elections are held in March. And his position was weakened further this morning when one of his senior advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, quit.

Former banker Cordeiro said in a damning statement: “It is a bad deal for FIFA’s MAs, a bad deal for football and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

“FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources. The organisation sits on billions of dollars in reserves and no debt. The FIFA president himself has highlighted the $15bn in revenue generated between 2022 and 2026. If MAs believe additional investment is needed to develop the game, FIFA already has the financial capacity to provide that support from its existing resources. Against that backdrop, selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense.

“Most troubling of all is the absence of answers to fundamental questions. Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?

Gianni Infantino and FIFA have blamed the media following opposition to their plans to sell off part of its major tournaments, including the World Cup

The world game’s governing body responded to widespread criticism of its idea on Friday and blamed “incorrect media reports” for the negativity.

UEFA and CONCACAF reject FIFA proposal

articles.title: AC Milan mourn loss of legend Franco Baresi
articles.summary: One of Italy's greatest ever players, Franco Baresi, has died at the age of 66
articles.content:
AC Milan mourn loss of legend Franco Baresi

One of Italy's greatest ever players, Franco Baresi, has died at the age of 66

Last Update:

AC Milan have announced the passing of former defender Franco Baresi, and said he “embodied the heart and soul” of the club.

Baresi, who was aged 66, was a legendary figure at San Siro after spending his entire 20-year playing career with the Rossoneri, making 719 appearances and helping them win six Serie A titles and three European Cups between 1977 and 1997.

A club statement read: “Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan, is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi’s memory. We must be strong and gather every bit of energy, even at this saddest of times.

“We lost Franco only a few months after his last public appearance in a packed San Siro, at the Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremony, an event on the world stage he helped make unforgettable.

“In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he’ll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever.”

Baresi helps Italy to World Cup triumph

A composed central defender, who was arguably ahead of his time due to his line-breaking passing ability, Baresi won 81 caps for Italy and was part of the squad that clinched the World Cup in 1982. He started the 1994 final as Italy lost to Brazil on penalties.

But it is at Milan where his loss will be most keenly felt.

He was named an honorary vice-president in 2020 and his number six shirt was retired for years later.

Baresi had been suffering from ill-health for some time and underwent lung surgery 12 months ago.

articles.title: CONCACAF joins UEFA in rejecting FIFA’s World Cup sell-off plan
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino and FIFA have suffered another blow in their efforts to sell World Cup rights.
articles.content:
CONCACAF joins UEFA in rejecting FIFA’s World Cup sell-off plan

Gianni Infantino and FIFA have suffered another blow in their efforts to sell World Cup rights.

Last Update:

CONCACAF has joined UEFA in opposing FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s controversial proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup’s commercial rights, dealing a major blow to the plans.

Following an emergency meeting on Thursday, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) confirmed its 41 member associations had rejected the proposal, citing concerns over the process behind the plan.

The decision comes after UEFA announced that its 55 member nations would boycott all FIFA competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, unless the proposal is abandoned.

CONCACAF, whose members include 2026 World Cup co-hosts the United States, Canada and Mexico, said it had “expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies.”

The United States Soccer Federation also backed the confederation’s position, stating it “stands with CONCACAF and its members”.

Infantino continues to push commercial route

Infantino unveiled plans earlier this week to sell a stake in FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE), a move that would reportedly raise $20 billion in exchange for influence over future World Cup broadcasting and commercial rights.

The proposal, backed by investment firm Thrive Capital, founded by Joshua Kushner, would generate more than $80 million for each of FIFA’s 211 member associations between now and 2037. FIFA members have until September 19 to vote on the proposal.

UEFA had already taken the unprecedented step of threatening to boycott all FIFA competitions while the proposal remains active.

In a statement, European football’s governing body said: “UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions.”

It added: “Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will.”

UEFA also criticised what it described as a lack of meaningful consultation, calling the process “a profound failure of leadership” by FIFA.

The growing opposition has also spread to Asia. Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa warned member associations that FIFA’s actions risked undermining continental football and suggested the proposal could not succeed without the backing of all six continental confederations.

articles.title: Harvey Elliott ready to prove himself on return to Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is ready to win his place back under new head coach Andoni Iraola.
articles.content:
Harvey Elliott ready to prove himself on return to Liverpool

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is ready to win his place back under new head coach Andoni Iraola.

Last Update:

Harvey Elliott has admitted he is determined to make the most of his return to Liverpool after describing his loan spell at Aston Villa as a difficult period in his career.

The midfielder moved to Villa Park last summer on a season-long loan deal, with an agreement in place that would have seen Unai Emery’s side sign him permanently for £35 million if he reached 10 appearances.

However, Villa opted against activating that clause early in the campaign, leaving Elliott with just nine appearances and 277 minutes of football before returning to Liverpool sooner than expected.

Emery later labelled the situation “embarrassing for everyone involved”, while Elliott has now opened up on the challenges he faced during his time away from Anfield.

“I wanted to go and explore something, come out of my comfort zone and do something that I thought personally would take me on as a player again,” Elliott said after Liverpool’s 1-0 pre-season victory over Wrexham in New York.

“But unfortunately it didn’t work out.”

Table of Contents

Elliott raring to go on return

The 23-year-old has since returned to Merseyside and has featured in both of Liverpool’s opening pre-season fixtures under new head coach Andoni Iraola, seeing the opportunity as a fresh start.

“Now I’m here and it’s kind of a second chance, if you want to call it that,” he added.

“Especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in, it’s another chance to impress and hopefully get in their good books.

“I wish Villa nothing but the very best. I had a lot of love for them and they treated me very well. Unfortunately, the situation happened but it’s another learning curve.

“I’m here now and I’m trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.”

Elliott came through Fulham’s academy before becoming the youngest player to feature in Premier League history when he made his debut aged 16. He joined Liverpool in 2019 and initially became a regular under Jurgen Klopp.

However, opportunities became more limited during Arne Slot’s title-winning campaign in 2024-25, with Elliott making 18 Premier League appearances before leaving on loan.

Midfielder opens up on mental difficulties

The midfielder admitted his time at Villa tested him mentally, despite ending the season with a positive achievement after helping the club win the Europa League.

“Mentally, it was a very tough one. It was a learning curve,” Elliott explained.

“It was an opportunity for me to experience something new, as much as I didn’t want to do it, and I don’t wish it upon any other player because it’s not nice at all.

“But I have no hard feelings. I’m on the other side of it now.

“I was able to get through it and achieve something at the end of the season as well. To be part of another historical moment for the club was a great situation.

“Right now, I’m just thinking about making sure I’m physically and mentally 100% and trying to impress on the pitch,” he said.

“When the right time comes to ask him [Iraola], that’s when I’ll go and ask.

“Ultimately, it’s just down to me. As long as I’m putting in the effort, hard work and desire on the pitch, then I feel like I have the opportunities.”

Elliott added that returning to Liverpool has reminded him why he loves playing for the club.

“I’m really happy to be back. Since the first day I walked through the door at training, I had a big beaming smile on my face.

“I’m wearing this strip again and putting this shirt on, and I just want to be free, play as much as I can and just enjoy it, because sometimes I don’t feel like I do it enough.

“Playing at Liverpool, there’s no better feeling.”

articles.title: Tonali reveals it took ’10 minutes’ for him to decide on Tottenham move
articles.summary: Sandro Tonali has opened up on his move from to Tottenham from Newcastle.
articles.content:
Tonali reveals it took ’10 minutes’ for him to decide on Tottenham move

Sandro Tonali has opened up on his move from to Tottenham from Newcastle.

Last Update:

Sandro Tonali says it took just “10 minutes” to decide Tottenham was the right move after meeting Roberto De Zerbi, with the new Spurs boss playing a key role in the club’s record-breaking £100m transfer.

The Italy international completed his switch from Newcastle earlier this summer and revealed a shared connection to hometown club Brescia helped convince him to move to North London.

Tonali said De Zerbi first made contact shortly after Tottenham secured Premier League survival, before the pair later met at the midfielder’s home outside Brescia.

“We spoke about Brescia and the difficult situation facing our club,” Tonali said, referring to the financial collapse of his boyhood side.

The 26-year-old also revealed their relationship stretches back almost a decade, with De Zerbi having tried to sign him during his time at Sassuolo.

Although Tonali held talks with another club, he said the decision quickly became clear.

“When you speak with a team, the first impression is a big thing and my impression was very positive,” he said.

“When you are happy after a 10-minute chat, it’s everything. Everything is perfect.”

London not a deciding factor in move

Tonali explained that London itself accounted for only a small part of his decision, insisting footballing reasons, De Zerbi and Tottenham’s recruitment plans were the overwhelming factors behind the move.

The midfielder admitted he and his family had previously hoped to return to Italy, but the size of his transfer fee ruled out that possibility.

“We had decided to come back to Italy but it was impossible because of the money,” he said.

“England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness and for my family.”

Despite leaving Newcastle after three-and-a-half years, Tonali stressed there were no hard feelings towards his former club.

He praised outgoing manager Eddie Howe, calling him “fantastic”, and said he hopes to remain close with both Howe and sporting director Ross Wilson.

Tonali also thanked Newcastle’s supporters, saying he wanted the Magpies to receive “the best deal” because they “deserve everything”.

Now Tottenham’s record signing, the Italy international accepts the £100m price tag will bring heightened expectations but insists it will not change him away from the pitch.

“I’m a normal person,” Tonali said. “When I go back to Italy, I go to my family, to my grandma and to my friends. If it is perfect for my family, it is perfect for me.”

articles.summary: John Stones has joined Inter Milan.
articles.content:
John Stones joins Inter Milan as a free agent

John Stones has joined Inter Milan.

Last Update:

John Stones has joined Inter Milan on a free transfer after signing a two-year contract with the Serie A champions.

The England international left Manchester City at the end of his contract earlier this summer, bringing an end to a trophy-laden 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium.

Inter confirmed the 32-year-old defender has signed a deal until June 2028.

Stones arrives in Italy after helping England finish third at the 2026 World Cup, where he started three matches for Thomas Tuchel’s side.

The centre-back joined City from Everton in 2016 and established himself as one of the Premier League’s standout defenders under Pep Guardiola.

During his time in Manchester, Stones won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and lifted the Champions League as part of City’s historic treble-winning campaign in 2023.

He made 295 appearances for the club, adding further silverware including five League Cups, three Community Shields, the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Club World Cup.

Stones now joins an Inter side that claimed the Serie A title last season, finishing 11 points clear of second-placed Napoli, as they look to defend their domestic crown under Cristian Chivu.
