articles.title: BREAKING: UEFA to boycott FIFA World Cup
articles.summary: UEFA has responded to Gianni Infantino's World Cup plans
articles.content:
BREAKING: UEFA to boycott FIFA World Cup

UEFA has responded to Gianni Infantino's World Cup plans

Last Update:

UEFA has opted to boycott the World Cup if FIFA’s plans to sell stakes in the tournament go ahead, the European administrative body for football has announced following a crisis meeting.

The move will “essentially kill” FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors, The Times has said.

You can read UEFA’s statement in full.

Table of Contents

Gianni Infantino: What are FIFA’s plans for World Cup?

Under the planned scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. In addition, it is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary of $64m as commissioner.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

UEFA responds after Infantino sets deadline

Infantino has subsequently written to all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they support the plan, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year.

However, Infantino gave those members a deadline of September 19 by which to accept to the one-time offer.

After the plans were revealed on Tuesday, UEFA said the proposals cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”.

And, following the news of Infantino’s offer, European football’s governing body published a further response.

“Today we have learned of Fifa’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan,” a UEFA statement read.

“But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.”

UEFA considering World Cup boycott

UEFA has previously successfully used the threat of a European boycott of the World Cup to defy Infantino, doing so in 2021 when he floated the idea of a biennial World Cup.

The 100th anniversary World Cup in 2030 is due to be held in large part in Europe, with Spain and Portugal set to host the tournament alongside Morocco. Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will also host games as part of the centenary celebration.

That makes the idea of a European boycott seem extremely unlikely but, with its member nations set to discuss their response to Infantino’s latest grand idea, that card is still very much on the table.

England’s Football Association joined the dissenting voices, while promising a more definitive response once full details are known.

“We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached,” the FA statement read.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

CONCACAF expresses concern

CONCACAF, the governing body that represents North America, Central American and Caribbean teams, also responded disapprovingly to news of the proposals.

A host of smaller nations that would seem likely to be among the biggest beneficiaries from Infantino’s scheme fall under CONCACAF, which expressed concern more on the grounds of process rather than the actual details of the plans.

“CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” a statement read.

“We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

“This is the framework within which CONCACAF operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.”

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) also made clear its frustration that it “was not consulted on the proposal.

It added that it is “disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels”.

FIFPRO urges FIFA to reconsider

The plans open the possibility of the World Cup being expanded further from 48 to 64 teams or being played more regularly than every four years to increase revenue for potential private investors.

And the European branch of FIFPRO, the world players’ union, pointed to concerns around the match calendar as it slammed the proposed scheme.

It said in a statement: “FIFPRO Europe has noted with deep concern the proposal to transform the FIFA World Cup and other FIFA competitions into investable assets for private capital, a move that would fundamentally and irreversibly reshape the incentives underpinning the competitions in which players work, compete and build their careers.

“Given the proposal’s potentially far-reaching implications for player welfare, the international match calendar and the future governance of the game, it is particularly troubling that a project of this magnitude has been developed largely behind closed doors and brought close to agreement without any meaningful engagement with those most affected. The decision to bypass the dialogue mechanisms recently established between FIFA and FIFPRO only reinforces these concerns.

“The proposal also raises fundamental concerns about the future governance of world football and the integrity of the game. Stakeholder participation in FIFA’s decision-making has always been limited. It must not now be displaced by commercial influence, allowing financial interests to outweigh the voices of those who play, support and sustain the game.  FIFPRO Europe cannot – and will never – support such a model.

“Within FIFA, neither FIFPRO nor players have a vote. Yet they will live with the consequences of these decisions long after the current FIFA leadership has moved on.

“The responsibility now lies with FIFA to reconsider its proposal without further delay. Every national football association, meanwhile, carries a responsibility that extends far beyond today’s financial returns or tomorrow’s commercial projections.

“Governments, public authorities, confederations, leagues, clubs and supporters also have a role to play in ensuring that football remains a public trust, not merely a commercial asset.

“FIFPRO Europe stands ready to work with every institution and stakeholder committed to protecting both the interests of players and the long-term integrity of the game. Football’s future deserves nothing less. And neither do the players who will shape it.”

The European Leagues, in a statement that received the full backing of the Premier League, labelled the proposals a “reckless and divisive development for world football”.

“The World Cup should not be for sale,” its statement read.

“It is not FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal.

“Football’s success has always been built on a pyramidal open structure and the delicate balance between domestic and international football. Commercial opportunities must support these foundations, not risk altering them.

“This opaque process and unilateral proposal are part of a long-term pattern in FIFA’s decision-making – a pattern which prompted the European Leagues to lodge a complaint with the European Commission on the basis that FIFA’s imposition of decisions on the international match calendar constitutes an abuse of dominant position that violates European competition law.

“Proposals relating to calendar and competitions, should be developed through transparent, accountable and inclusive processes, with meaningful engagement and consent from all stakeholders whose interests are affected, as explicitly requested by the Court of Justice of the EU in its 2023 Super League ruling. We have held productive meetings with the European Commission about this matter and have confidence that the legal decisions they take will continue to be in the best interests of fans and football communities.

“European Leagues will continue to work with UEFA to safeguard the long-term interests of the game. We have faith that Federations / National Associations around the world will do the same as they scrutinise this proposal from the FIFA President.”

articles.title: UEFA calls FIFA World Cup plan sell-off a ‘profound failure of leadership’
articles.summary: FIFA's plans for the World Cup are 'irresponsible', says UEFA
articles.content:
UEFA calls FIFA World Cup plan sell-off a ‘profound failure of leadership’

FIFA's plans for the World Cup are 'irresponsible', says UEFA

Last Update:

UEFA says its national associations will join the European football administrative body “with absolute determination” in opposing FIFA’s plans to sell stakes.

In an unequivocal statement following an emergency meeting about the proposals on Thursday, UEFA said it stood “as one” with its 55 members in believing that the plans had “no place in world football”.

“The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product,” warned UEFA. “It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies.

“It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent.

“No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.”

Table of Contents

Gianni Infantino: What are FIFA’s plans for World Cup?

Under the planned scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup.

The plan could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income.

In addition, it is claimed that Infantino – set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031 – would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary of $64m as commissioner.

“It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game,” said UEFA.

“This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

“Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

“There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

“Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

UEFA emphasised that European teams will not participate in FIFA competitions “for so long as these proposals remain alive”.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

You can read UEFA’s statement in full.

UEFA responds after Infantino sets deadline

Infantino has  written to all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they are supportive, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year.

However, Infantino gave those members a deadline of September 19 by which to accept  the one-time offer.

After the plans were revealed on Tuesday, UEFA said the proposals cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”.

articles.title: Rashford posts emotional farewell to Barcelona with return officially ruled out
articles.summary: Marcus Rashford has said goodbye to Barcelona after a successful year on loan at the club.
articles.content:
Rashford posts emotional farewell to Barcelona with return officially ruled out

Marcus Rashford has said goodbye to Barcelona after a successful year on loan at the club.

Last Update:

Marcus Rashford has confirmed his departure from Barcelona after returning to Manchester United following the end of his loan spell at Camp Nou.

The England forward spent the 2025-26 season with the Spanish champions and helped the club secure LaLiga and the Spanish Supercopa, but Barcelona decided against activating their option to sign him permanently for around €30 million.

Rashford took to social media to thank Barcelona, their supporters and everyone involved at the club after his spell in Spain came to an end.

“I’m very grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here such a positive and memorable experience,” Rashford wrote.

“I’ve enjoyed every moment and will take many special memories with me. I wish the club and all its supporters the very best of luck and every success in the season ahead.”

The 28-year-old is currently on holiday after representing England at the World Cup, where Thomas Tuchel’s side finished third, but he is expected to return to Manchester United training at Carrington in early August.

Rashford’s Man Utd career unclear

However, Rashford’s position at Old Trafford remains unclear, with a return to Michael Carrick’s squad not guaranteed despite his successful season in Spain.

Rashford enjoyed one of the most productive campaigns of his career at Barcelona, scoring 14 goals and providing 14 assists in 49 appearances across all competitions.

Despite those numbers, Barcelona opted against completing a permanent transfer, with the club believed to have concerns over the financial package required to make the deal happen.

The Catalan giants had remained interested in bringing Rashford back either on another loan or for a reduced fee, but the arrivals of Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi appear to have changed their plans.

Gordon joined Barcelona from Newcastle United in a deal worth around £69 million, while Adeyemi arrived from Borussia Dortmund for an initial fee of approximately £20 million.

Manchester United are still expected to listen to offers for Rashford, with reports suggesting the club would ideally like to receive up to £35 million for a permanent departure.

Carrick has previously refused to rule out Rashford playing a role at United again, insisting that a decision over his future will be made at the appropriate time.

articles.title: Disruption set to continue at Newcastle with Guimaraes poised to join Arsenal
articles.summary: Bruno Guimaraes is poised to join Arsenal from Newcastle this summer.
articles.content:
Disruption set to continue at Newcastle with Guimaraes poised to join Arsenal

Bruno Guimaraes is poised to join Arsenal from Newcastle this summer.

Last Update:

Arsenal are increasingly confident of completing the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, with the Brazil midfielder keen to make the move to the Premier League champions.

The Gunners have tracked Guimaraes throughout the summer and, according to multiple reports, optimism is growing that a deal can be agreed.

Arsenal are expected to improve on their £70million offer, with a package worth around £80m likely to be enough to secure the 28-year-old’s signature.

Guimaraes is due back for Newcastle training in the coming days, although the Magpies insist formal negotiations between the clubs have yet to take place.

Arsenal prepared to spend after Rogers snub

Arsenal’s pursuit of the midfielder comes after they walked away from a move for Morgan Rogers.

The North London club valued the England international at £80m and chose not to match Chelsea’s eventual £117m deal, instead turning their focus towards Guimaraes.

Newcastle, meanwhile, face the prospect of another major departure during a turbulent summer. Sandro Tonali has already joined Tottenham, while Anthony Gordon has completed a move to Barcelona.

The uncertainty comes just days after Eddie Howe stepped down as Newcastle head coach following five years in charge.

Saudi Pro League-winning coach Matthias Jaissle is expected to succeed him, with the club now facing the challenge of rebuilding ahead of the new season while trying to retain one of their most influential players.

articles.title: UEFA statement in full as European nations confirm boycott of FIFA events
articles.summary: UEFA has issued a withering statement in opposition to FIFA's plans to sell off part of its major tournaments to commercial investors. Read it in full here...
articles.content:
UEFA statement in full as European nations confirm boycott of FIFA events

UEFA has issued a withering statement in opposition to FIFA's plans to sell off part of its major tournaments to commercial investors. Read it in full here...

Last Update:

UEFA today gave an unequivocal thumbs down to FIFA’s plans to sell off part of its major tournaments, stating football “is not for sale”.

Here is the statement in full:

UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

But our opposition goes far beyond process.

The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.

articles.title: Brazil set to start rebuild under Ancelotti with Australia tour
articles.summary: Brazil have confirmed a tour of Australia at the end of 2026.
articles.content:
Brazil set to start rebuild under Ancelotti with Australia tour

Brazil have confirmed a tour of Australia at the end of 2026.

Last Update:

Brazil will face Australia in a two-match friendly series in Queensland this September as part of the 2026 Queensland Football Series.

The five-time world champions will take on the Socceroos at Queensland Country Bank Stadium in Townsville on September 25 before meeting again at Brisbane’s Suncorp Stadium on September 29, with the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) confirming the fixtures on Thursday

The matches will mark Brazil’s return to Australia and provide Carlo Ancelotti’s side with their first fixtures following the 2026 World Cup.

Having gone out in disappointing fashion, it is the head coach’s first opportunity to rebuild a squad who have struggled to compete at major tournaments recently.

The tour will give Australian supporters a rare chance to watch one of international football’s most successful nations, with the CBF describing the matches as another “important international commitment”.

Brazil also set for India tour

Carlo Ancelotti’s side have also confirmed they will make history by playing in India for the first time, with a friendly against the Indian national team scheduled for October 3 at Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.

Announcing the fixture, the Brazilian Football Confederation described it as an “unprecedented chapter” in the national team’s history.

“It will be a special encounter with a country that hosts the largest international fanbase of the Brazilian National Team and that, for generations, has followed the history of Brazilian football with immense affection and passion,” the CBF said.

“We are eager to live this moment alongside millions of Indian fans.”

Reports in Brazil have also suggested the Selecao could round off the year by competing in a four-team tournament in Singapore during the November international window, although those plans have not yet been officially confirmed by the Brazilian Football Confederation.

articles.title: Shearer questions timing of Howe’s departure and predicts season of struggle for crisis-club Newcastle
articles.summary: Eddie Howe has left Newcastle with 38-year-old German Matthias Jaissle set to replace him on Tyneside. The club's former striker Alan Shearer is worried about the season ahead.
articles.content:
Shearer questions timing of Howe’s departure and predicts season of struggle for crisis-club Newcastle

Eddie Howe has left Newcastle with 38-year-old German Matthias Jaissle set to replace him on Tyneside. The club's former striker Alan Shearer is worried about the season ahead.

Last Update:

Alan Shearer has questioned the timing of Eddie Howe’s departure from Newcastle and predicted a “tough season” ahead for the Tyneside club.

Howe stood down on Thursday as head coach at St James’ Park after five years in charge, the news coming just hours after his team were thrashed 4-1 at Bristol City in a pre-season friendly.

It has been a turbulent summer for Newcastle with Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali having left and captain Bruno Guimaraes desperate to join Arsenal.

And Shearer believes it would have been better if the 48-year-old had offered to go at the end of last season.

He told Betfair: “If something was going to happen, you would have thought it would have happened at the end of last season so it would have given Newcastle time to prepare.

“I don’t know what’s gone on, whether it was the end of last season, whether it was the summer, whether he feels they can’t continue to sell his best players.

“I don’t think it’s a great look for what’s happening at the minute with Newcastle. We’re selling all our best players. The fans are seeing [Alexander] Isak go, the fans are seeing Tonali go, the fans are seeing Gordon go. My guess is it’s probably only a matter of time before Bruno goes.”

Table of Contents

Newcastle’s new transfer model fails to convince Shearer

Newcastle have made some signings over recent weeks but have gone for up-and-coming talents such as Ewen Jaouen, Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Traore.

And Shearer is not convinced that is a recipe for success.

“I’d like to see Newcastle sign players, because it’s alright having this bold new look of going for young, hungry players who are 30 or 40 million pounds. But also, the Premier League is tough. You need some experienced heads in there as well,” he added.

“There’s no doubt this season’s going to be a tough one for Newcastle. You can’t keep selling your best players in the hope that you’re going to get to where you want to get to. What I would like is stability.”

Howe led Newcastle to the EFL Cup in 2025 – the club’s first major trophy in 70 years – but his relationship with an expectant fanbase turned sour last season with a 12th-placed finish as well as home-and-away defeats to bitter rivals Sunderland.

Jaissle will have to navigate ‘tricky waters’ at Newcastle – Shearer

Matthias Jaissle is rumoured to be Howe’s replacement. The 38-year-old German is currently at Al-Ahli, who, like Newcastle, are owned by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund.

Jaissle won the Austrian Bundesliga with RB Salzburg and has led Al-Ahli to two Asian Champions League successes but Shearer is wary of bringing someone in with no Premier League experience.

“Clearly, he’s got a great record in Saudi [but] clearly, he’s very young and inexperienced,” said the former Newcastle striker. “The Premier League is a beast of a league. It’s a big ask for anyone to come in and take over after what Eddie’s done. If Jaissle does come in, you’re asking a 38-year-old to navigate very, very tricky waters.”

articles.title: De Zerbi promises another transfer ‘bomba’ at Tottenham but identity of potential signing remains a mystery
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has hinted Tottenham are on the verge of another major signing
articles.content:
De Zerbi promises another transfer ‘bomba’ at Tottenham but identity of potential signing remains a mystery

Roberto De Zerbi has hinted Tottenham are on the verge of another major signing

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi claims Tottenham are on the verge of a “bomba” signing and suggested it would be an attacking player.

Spurs have already spent almost £230million this summer on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke, as well as bringing in free agents Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on high wages, to bolster a squad that has limped to successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League.

Last season’s narrow escape appears to have altered the mindset in North London and the board have provided plenty of backing for De Zerbi, and the Italian claims the spending is not over yet.

Speaking on the pre-season tour of Australia – Spurs take on Chelsea in Sydney on Saturday – he said: “The transfer market is not finished for sure, but we have completed 60% of our project. Now we have another bomba.”

Having confirmed the player in question was an attacker, and not long-time target Savinho, he added: “I don’t love working with plan A, plan B, plan C. It is plan A, full stop, because all players are not the same. We have to increase the number of goals.”

De Zerbi was not willing to reveal the identity of the target but the likes of former Barcelona loanee Marcus Rashford, Rafael Leao and Cody Gakpo have been linked with the club in recent weeks.

Romero’s ‘will’ to leave Tottenham

As well as players coming in, there is expected to be plenty of movement the other way with Lucas Bergvall likely to depart along with captain Cristian Romero while the future of England full-back Djed Spence remains uncertain.

Spence’s stock has risen following an excellent World Cup and he has been linked with Everton and Inter Milan.

De Zerbi has said previously he will only work with players who want to be at Tottenham, and he repeated that message again, adding: “I repeat what I said to Djed, and to Lucas. I would like you to stay if you want to stay. If you don’t want to stay, if you want to leave, then you have to leave.”

Romero appears certain to move on. The Argentina defender has attracted plenty of criticism during his time at Spurs but De Zerbi says Romero has shown “unbelievable behaviour” since he joined the club in March but it is his “will” to leave.

“At the beginning of my time in April I had, I don’t know, one million individual meetings. And the players told me if they are [staying] here [or not],” he said.

“I said: ‘Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave. If you don’t help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me.'”

articles.title: BREAKING: Chelsea complete signing of France international Lacroix
articles.summary: Chelsea have made another summer signing by bringing in Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace
articles.content:
BREAKING: Chelsea complete signing of France international Lacroix

Chelsea have made another summer signing by bringing in Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace

Last Update:

Chelsea have signed France international Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace.

The 26-year-old has signed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge after Chelsea paid a reported £52million to prise him away from Selhurst Park.

Lacroix is the fifth summer signing for new boss Xabi Alonso, following on from Morgan Rogers, Marco Palestra, Geovany Quendra and Harrison Bettoni.

“I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club. Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment,” Lacroix told the club’s official website.

“When I spoke with the manager, I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

“We want to win. When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it’s something that we can achieve. The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can’t wait to contribute.”

Table of Contents

Summer of churn at Chelsea

Chelsea have balanced the books partially by offloading Marc Cucurella (£51.8m) to Real Madrid, Andrey Santos (£50m) to Manchester United and Alejandro Garnacho on loan to Aston Villa.

Palestra could form a new central defensive pairing with Lacroix, who was one of the standout players in another impressive season for Palace in 2025/26.

He made 55 appearances in all competitions, and started in the Eagles’ 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano in the final of the Conference League.

Lacroix’s form earned him a call-up to the France squad for the World Cup and he appeared in three games, including Les Bleus’ 6-4 defeat to England in the third-fourth place play-off.

His sale represents another clever piece of business for Palace who signed Lacroix from Wolfsburg for £15.4m from Wolfsburg two years ago.

Palace sad to see Lacroix depart

Palace chairman Steve Parish said of Lacroix: “Max has been fantastic since he came to the club, being a huge part of our trophy winning seasons and building a special bond with everyone at the club and the supporters.

“Thank you Max, for everything, and all the very best for the next phase of your career.

“As outstanding a figure off the pitch as he has been on it, we are all grateful to him for the role he has played over the last two seasons, and – although we are sad to bid him farewell – we do so wishing him the very best for the future.”

articles.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle, the incoming Newcastle boss?
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle is poised to become the new coach of Newcastle but what do we know of the 38-year-old?
articles.content:
Who is Matthias Jaissle, the incoming Newcastle boss?

Matthias Jaissle is poised to become the new coach of Newcastle but what do we know of the 38-year-old?

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle is the overwhelming favourite to become the new head coach of Newcastle following the departure this morning of Eddie Howe.

Jaissle is relatively unknown in the United Kingdom but has carved out a big reputation in Asia, helping Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli to back-to-back Champions League successes.

Table of Contents

Jaissle profile

Born: April 5, 1988 in Nürtingen, GermanyPlaying Career: Hoffenheim (2007-2014)Appearances: 60Managerial Career: FC Liefering (2021), RB Salzburg (2021-2023), Al-Ahli (2023- )

Jaissle’s career takes off thanks to Rangnick

Jaissle’s playing career was disrupted when he suffered a serious ACL injury playing for Hoffenheim against Hannover in 2009. He was never the same when he returned and eventually hung up his boots in 2014.

Ralf Rangnick had brought him to Hoffenheim but had subsequently moved on to RB Leipzig and he offered Jaissle the opportunity to start his coaching career in the German club’s youth department.

He gradually worked his way through the ranks – leaving briefly to become Alexander Zorniger’s assistant at Danish club Brondby – before being named head coach of the Under-18s at Salzburg, who like Leipzig are part of the Red Bull network of clubs.

Promotion followed, first when he was named boss of Salzburg’s feeder club FC Liefering and then shortly afterwards came the top job, succeeding Jesse Marsch.

Aged 33, he had the biggest job in Austrian football and he ran with it, developing a reputation for high-energy, high-press football as Salzburg, who had a hugely talented squad that included the likes of Benjamin Sesko, Karim Adeyemi, Noah Okafor and Brenden Aaronson, cruised to a league and cup double in his first season in charge.

Saudi opportunity arises for Jaissle

He repeated the feat in the 2022/23 season before being sacked after it emerged he had been discussing a switch to Al-Ahli.

“Yes, you’re not the first person to see it as a remarkable move,” he told The Athletic in January.

“But back then, it was really spontaneous. I wish the timing had been different, but sometimes that’s how it is in football. There’s interest, or an offer, and then you need to decide quickly.

“But for me, the thought back then was obviously — and let’s be completely honest — that financially it was something I just had to consider. But the other part was the chance to coach a team who had just got promoted into the first league, with a huge fanbase and with some big stars – some superstars, really – and it was a big step for me.”

Howe repeatedly refused to discuss Saudi’s human rights record – claiming he didn’t have time to research it properly – but Jaissle admitted he had given it thought.

“Yes, I’d read the headlines but at the same time I was aware that the country was taking some positive steps to open up,” he claimed. “There is a positive energy, that things are better than before and will keep getting better in the future. Not just in the club but across the city and country, especially among the young people.

“Obviously, change doesn’t happen overnight. It will take time. It’s growing so fast and that gives you hope for the future. I’ve seen for myself that in many ways they are on the right path.

“And I wanted the challenge. I wanted to coach abroad, in a different culture, and to work in English, which is not my native language.

“So, I saw it as a chance to develop as a coach. I’m still young, but I felt I was experienced enough to manage the expectations and the players, and to lead the team in the way that I had in Salzburg and for my style of play to be recognisable.”

He took over an Al-Ahli squad packed with players who had carved out a reputation in Europe’s major leagues – Roberto Firmino, Riyad Mahrez, Franck Kessie and goalkeeper Edouard Mendy while Ivan Toney joined shortly after.

Al-Ahli recorded third, fifth and third Pro League finishes in his three seasons in charge but his real success came continentally with Champions League trophy wins in 2025 and 2026.

What is his Jaissle’s playing style?

Jaissle is a disciple of Rangnick and the Red Bull system that is built on high press.

He said: “I want stress on the opponent as soon as possible. And when we win the ball, I want to go as quickly as possible towards the opponent’s goal. I’m very vertical in that approach.”

At Salzburg he showed his versatility by adopting different systems domestically in games where his side would dominate possession and in Europe where they would have to sit back.

“In Austria, we often faced teams who played a low block, but adaptation was always really important,” he explained. “In the league, we could play our way, using the identity we had in the academy, up through Liefering, and into the first team.

“But sometimes in the Champions League, I would try to do the same thing. You can’t always do that. You have to be smarter. There are times in the game where you have to play deep, which was not natural to us, and when you have to change the depth of your back four or alter the space between the defenders.

“That helped prepare me for coming to Saudi Arabia. I had a squad that was completely different in profile, and I had to think much more game-to-game about formation, how and when to press, and that forced me to become much more flexible — to develop as a coach.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Eddie Howe set to leave Newcastle
articles.summary: Eddie Howe has informed Newcastle of his wish to leave the club
articles.content:
BREAKING: Eddie Howe set to leave Newcastle

Eddie Howe has informed Newcastle of his wish to leave the club

Last Update:

Eddie Howe has stood down as Newcastle boss, according to The Athletic.

Al-Ahli coach Matthias Jaissle is reported be his replacement having led the Saudi Arabian side, who like Newcastle are owned by the country’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), to two Asian Champions League successes.

Howe took charge in November 2021, shortly after the club’s takeover by PIF, and earned cult status on Tyneside by leading them to their first domestic silverware in 70 years when they won the 2025 EFL Cup.

But cracks started to appear last season with criticism of his tactics and substitutions as Newcastle could only manage a 12th-placed finish in the Premier League with his reputation diminished further by home-and-away defeats to bitter rivals Sunderland.

Table of Contents

Newcastle’s difficult pre-season convinces Howe it is time to go

A difficult pre-season – Newcastle were beaten 4-1 at Championship side Bristol City last night – has convinced Howe to walk away and he is now eager to take a break from the game.

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer and captain Bruno Guimaraes is also pushing for a move to Arsenal.

In their stead, Newcastle have signed several youngsters as they look to operate differently in the transfer market.

Jaissle has developed big reputation in Asian football

Jaissle, 38, may not be known in the United Kingdom but he has developed a big reputation in Asia with a brand of high-intensity, attacking football that has produced great success.

The German moved to Saudi Arabia in 2023 after two successful seasons with RB Salzburg, claiming back-to-back league and cup doubles in Austria.

As a player, he spent his entire career with Hoffenheim as a central defender but was forced to retire aged 26 after failing to recover from an ACL injury.

He was integrated into the Leipzig coaching programme by Ralf Rangnick and eventually took over as head coach in 2021.

articles.title: Ngumoha emerges as potential Mo Salah replacement with winner as Liverpool beat Wrexham
articles.summary: Liverpool are short of right-sided wingers but Rio Ngumoha showed his versatility by playing there, and scoring, against Wrexham
articles.content:
Ngumoha emerges as potential Mo Salah replacement with winner as Liverpool beat Wrexham

Liverpool are short of right-sided wingers but Rio Ngumoha showed his versatility by playing there, and scoring, against Wrexham

Last Update:

Rio Ngumoha suggested he could be the answer to Liverpool’s right-sided problem with the only goal as Andoni Iraola maintained his 100% start as Reds boss with a 1-0 victory over Wrexham in New York.

Liverpool are believed to be in talks with Paris Saint-Germain over the signing of Bradley Barcola, who would add another option on the left wing alongside Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike, Florian Wirtz and new signing Victor Munoz.

Ngumoha is also comfortable on the left but came on at half-time last night and operated from the opposite flank – a position that has been filled by Mohamed Salah in recent years – and showed his versatility with a bright display that was capped with a goal, albeit a scruffy one with a huge deflection taking the ball into the net.

The 17-year-old told the club’s official website: “I just want to play and start as many games as I can. These games are a really good showcase to show the manager, because it’s a fresh start for everyone. It’s really important and it’s good.

“All the coaching staff are just telling me to play my normal game really, whether that’s going inside or outside. I’ve been working on it in training anyway, playing on the right and the left. Just being unpredictable really.”

Table of Contents

Nyoni also impresses for Liverpool

Iraola named a young side with Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremy Jacquet all remaining in Chicago. And that allowed Trey Nyoni to showcase his talents once again after an impressive showing in the 4-2 win over Sunderland on Saturday.

Iraola said: “Trey is very good on the ball, very calm, he reads the situations well. We’re forcing him in the work without the ball, in the press, and he is absolutely doing very well. I think the timings of the jumps are very good. He is always confident on the ball so we encourage him. Sometimes even if he loses the ball, ‘Try to find the No.10, try to find the No.9, even balls in behind, look a little bit further’ because he can do it, because he is so good.

“At the end, he is a midfielder who, I always say, you have to ask for the ball sometimes with pressure – and he doesn’t feel this pressure. Even when he has one opponent quite close, he asks for that ball and he’s confident, he doesn’t rush. For me, that is very valuable.”

It was another useful outing overall for Liverpool, who play Leeds next on Sunday.

“I think overall we were more solid than the other day,” added Iraola. “It was a different kind of game, the pitch is quite narrow and there are not a lot of spaces. But I think we had good spells. And even if the other day maybe you score more goals and it looks nicer, I think today we were more a team and more collective.

“We are sometimes arriving late, but I think it’s a step forward, since especially the first half against Sunderland. That is more of a reference than the second half. Slowly, slowly I hope every game we are closer and closer. We start to add new bodies, because now we are playing with a lot of the young players. Slowly, slowly we have to add the senior players that are starting to train with us, so we can arrive to the beginning of the season in a good place.”

Big-name quartet to return for Liverpool against Leeds

Liverpool should have more players available at the weekend with Jacquet expected to make his Reds debut following his summer switch from Rennes.

Iraola said: “Yes, my idea is for Ryan, for Florian, for Alex, for even Jeremy Jacquet to have their first minutes against Leeds. We’ll see how many minutes they can play but we have to start slowly, slowly integrating more of the senior players that have had less training sessions. I think they should be ready on the weekend to have their first minutes.”

articles.summary: CAF responded very differently to UEFA and other confederations.
articles.content:
CAF to ‘assess and evaluate’ Infantino’s controversial World Cup proposals

CAF responded very differently to UEFA and other confederations.

Last Update:

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has notably elected not to criticise FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, saying it will “assess and evaluate” the proposals.

There has been outrage across world football after FIFA confirmed the plans on Tuesday.

Under Infantino’s proposed scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. It is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns $64m annually.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each receiving a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

Infantino subsequently contacted all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they support the proposals, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year and giving the associations a deadline of September 19 by which to accept to the one-time offer.

European football’s governing body UEFA has vehemently criticised the plans, saying they cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”. The AFC and CONCACAF have each criticised the lack of proper process, while former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has said the governing body risks “losing its soul” if the plans are implemented.

However, CAF, which oversees a host of smaller member associations that would stand to be among the biggest beneficiaries from the proposed scheme, responded in a very different way.

A CAF statement read: “The Confederation Africaine de Football (“CAF“) received correspondence today from FIFA on the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative, in accordance with the consultation process that is currently underway with FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council.

“As part of this consultation process, the CAF President, Dr Patrice Motsepe, will host a meeting of the CAF Executive Committee next week, to inter-alia, assess and evaluate the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative.

“CAF also encourages its Member Associations to examine the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and participate in the consultation process in accordance with CAF and FIFA’s regulations and established procedures.

“CAF is committed to continue consulting and working together with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Football Confederations and stakeholders in support of increasing financial and other resources for the development and growth of football in Africa and worldwide.”

articles.title: Newcastle suffer friendly defeat at Bristol City as defensive issues laid bare
articles.summary: The Magpies' third pre-season game did not go to plan.
articles.content:
Newcastle suffer friendly defeat at Bristol City as defensive issues laid bare

The Magpies' third pre-season game did not go to plan.

Last Update:

Newcastle United suffered a pre-season humbling as the Premier League side were beaten 4-1 by Championship Bristol City at Ashton Gate on Wednesday.

The Magpies, who have seen two key players sold this summer in the form of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, were without all but one of their players who featured at the World Cup, with Anthony Elanga the sole exception.

New signings Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure did not feature, while captain Bruno Guimaraes — who is reportedly keen to move to Arsenal — is not due to return to training until Friday after his exertions with Brazil in North America.

Still, even with the likes of Tino Livramento, Malick Thaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Miley, Yoane Wissa, Will Osula and Nick Woltemade also out of the squad, manager Eddie Howe will have been far from pleased with the performance.

Table of Contents

Murphy and Botman struggle as Newcastle beaten

Newcastle went close early through Sean Neave, before Bristol took the lead when a fine free-kick from Sam Greenwood flew in off the crossbar.

It was 2-0 when Lorent Tolaj fired past Ewen Jaouen, though he appeared to get away with a foul in the build-up on Newcastle defender Sven Botman, who endured a chastening evening.

Max Bird made it 3-0 with a low finish five minutes into the second half after makeshift right-back Jacob Murphy casually conceded possession, with his efforts in tracking back thereafter leaving a lot to be desired.

Harvey Barnes, fresh from signing a new long-term contract, pulled one back with a low finish from a Jacob Ramsey lay-off after Matheos Ferreira won the ball high up the pitch.

But a disappointing night was capped by an own goal from Botman as the centre-back inadvertently turned a left-wing cross beyond Nick Pope, his struggles and those of Murphy highlighting the need for Newcastle to add at full-back and at the heart of the defence in a transfer window that has already seen them make four signings.

Ipswich lose to Osasuna, Lookman doubles up for Atleti

Meanwhile, Newcastle’s Premier League rivals Ipswich Town suffered a 2-1 home defeat to LaLiga side Osasuna.

Miguel Auria gave Osasuna the lead before Chuba Akpom equalised for Gary O’Neil’s men.

But Osasuna clinched victory 10 minutes from time as Raul Moro found the net with a fierce strike from outside the box.

An all-LaLiga friendly saw Atletico Madrid continue their preparations with a 4-1 win over Getafe.

Ademola Lookman was on target twice for Diego Simeone’s men, whose final two pre-season games come against Manchester United and Manchester City.

articles.summary: Blatter has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.
articles.content:
FIFA would ‘lose its soul’ under controversial World Cup scheme, Blatter warns

Blatter has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.

Last Update:

Sepp Blatter has warned that FIFA will lose its soul if it implements a controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

There has been outrage across world football after FIFA confirmed the plans on Tuesday.

Under the scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. In addition, it is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary of $64m as commissioner.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

Infantino has subsequently written to all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they support the plan, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year.

However, Infantino gave those members a deadline of September 19 by which to accept to the one-time offer.

European football’s governing body UEFA has vehemently criticised the plans, saying they cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”.

And former FIFA president Blatter, who resigned in 2015 amid a corruption probe and was subsequently banned for eight years by the body’s ethics committee, has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.

“Football belongs to no individual and to no institution. It ⁠belongs to the people,” Blatter told Reuters.

“If FIFA were transferred into a profit-oriented corporate structure, ​it would lose its soul.”

Blatter has criticised his successor on numerous occasions, slamming the decision to expand the World Cup to 48 teams, the award of the 2034 tournament to Saudi Arabia and the suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun’s ban for a last-16 tie with Belgium at this year’s competition after apparent influence by US president Donald Trump.

“The FIFA World Cup is not a commercial asset ​that belongs to a ​handful of executives,” Blatter added. “It is part of the cultural heritage of world football. FIFA is the guardian of the World Cup, not its owner. There is a ​fundamental difference.

“The beneficiaries should be the game itself — from grassroots football to the highest international ​level — not outside investors seeking returns.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Bournemouth forward Kroupi set for at least three months out after foot surgery
articles.summary: It is a huge blow to new Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Bournemouth forward Kroupi set for at least three months out after foot surgery

It is a huge blow to new Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.

Last Update:

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is set to miss three to four months after undergoing foot surgery.

Kroupi, who enjoyed a stunning first season in the Premier League, had been linked with the likes of Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Tottenham.

But any hope of a transfer for the 20-year-old is over for now after The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported Kroupi is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Kroupi reportedly sustained the injury during Bournemouth’s pre-season trip to Austria. He travelled back to England for treatment before having surgery on Wednesday.

Bournemouth had stood firm amid significant interest in Kroupi, making it clear they had no desire to sell him.

But the Cherries now face being without him until October or November in a significant blow to new boss Marco Rose.

Kroupi injury leaves big void for Bournemouth

Kroupi joined Bournemouth from Lorient in February 2025 but spent the remainder of the 2024-25 campaign on loan at the Ligue 1 club.

He starred in his debut Premier League campaign as Bournemouth qualified for the Europa League in what proved to be Andoni Iraola’s final season in charge.

Kroupi was Bournemouth’s top scorer last term with 13 goals in 2025-26, all of which came in the Premier League.

While Bournemouth still have Evanilson to play through the middle of their attack, Kroupi’s injury increases the pressure on the likes of Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier to contribute goals as they attempt to hit the ground running under Rose while competing on two fronts.

Antoine Semenyo, who left for Manchester City in January, was second behind Kroupi for Bournemouth last season with 10 goals. Tavernier scored eight, Evanilson netted six, while Rayan contributed five. Kluivert, who dealt with injury for much of the season, scored twice.

Bournemouth could still lose one of their stars to another club. Alex Scott has been linked with a host of Premier League clubs and is said to be champions Arsenal’s alternative midfield target if they fail to prise Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

Rose takes charge of his first official game as Bournemouth boss on August 23, when they open the season away at Manchester City.

articles.title: “I’m here to bring Italy back” – Mancini promises glorious return
articles.summary: Mancini steered Italy to the Euros title in 2021
articles.content:
“I’m here to bring Italy back” – Mancini promises glorious return

Mancini steered Italy to the Euros title in 2021

Last Update:

Roberto Mancini has set out to win a major trophy once again with Italy as he starts a second stint in charge of the national team.

Former Manchester City boss Mancini, 61, won the delayed Euro 2020 title against England at Wembley.

But he left in 2023 after failing to reach the 2022 World Cup and shockingly inherits an Italian side who have now missed three World Cups in a row.

“I’m here to bring Italy back to where it deserves to be,” he said at his unveiling.

“Regardless of what happened in 2023, the goal is always to win and play well. I’m convinced the players are there and that they’re good, especially the young ones.

“I’d like to win a major trophy, maybe even two. I’d like to build a project with the national team.”

Italy have won four World Cups but have failed to make it past the group stage since their most recent title in 2006.

Mancini will first have to qualify for the Euros back in England in 2024 before hoping to end that long wait for a return on the global stage.

He said: “If Italy qualified for the World Cup, as would be normal, they would still be a team aspiring to reach the final, even if they weren’t among the favourites.

“We want to become a team to beat: now we’ll prepare for the European Championship and then we’ll think about the World Cup.”

Mancini’s first game in charge will be a Nations League match against Belgium in September.

articles.title: BREAKING: FIFA charges Argentina players over World Cup final conduct and opens case over Falklands banner
articles.summary: Argentina's conduct after the semi-final and proved extremely controversial.
articles.content:
BREAKING: FIFA charges Argentina players over World Cup final conduct and opens case over Falklands banner

Argentina's conduct after the semi-final and proved extremely controversial.

Last Update:

FIFA has charged several Argentina players for their conduct in the aftermath of their World Cup final defeat to Spain and opened proceedings against the country’s Football Association for the display of a banner relating to the Falkland Islands after the semi-final win over England.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after an uninspiring final was settled by Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Ugly scenes followed at the end, with several Spain players accosted by Argentina counterparts. Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, as he grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

FIFA confirmed on Wednesday it had levelled three charges for assault against Paredes, while also charging Nahuel Molina (two counts, one completed and one attempted) and assistant coach Roberto Ayala (one count). Ayala was involved in confrontation with Spain’s Dani Olmo and promised to apologise in person to the Barcelona star.

Nahuel Molina (one count) and Thiago Almada (one count) have also been charged for unsporting behaviour, as has Spain midfielder Gavi (one count).

FIFA added that those accused would have the opportunity to present their position before a decision by the disciplinary committee.

In addition, the Argentinian Football Association (AFA) looks set to face action for the team’s actions after La Albiceleste came from behind to beat England 2-1 in the semi-final.

Amid the celebrations, several Argentina players posed with a banner that read  “Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine).”

Britain and Argentina went to war over the Falklands in 1982, with the 74-day conflict resulting in the deaths of 649 Argentine soldiers, 255 British combatants and three civilians. The Falklands remain a British controlled territory, though Argentina insists the archipelago in the South Atlantic is its possession.

A formal investigation was demanded by the British government, and a case has been opened against the AFA for the team “using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

The proceedings against the AFA also relate to “team misconduct” “discrimination and racist abuse” and “order and security at matches”.

The FIFA statement read: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has opened proceedings against the Argentinian Football Association for potential breaches of article 13 paragraph 2 c) (Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature), article 14 paragraph 5 (Team misconduct), article 15 (Discrimination and racist abuse) and article 17 (Order and security at matches) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026.”

articles.title: ‘I would like him to stay’ – but De Zerbi won’t guarantee Tottenham midfielder Bergvall a starting place
articles.summary: Will the Swede stay with Spurs?
articles.content:
‘I would like him to stay’ – but De Zerbi won’t guarantee Tottenham midfielder Bergvall a starting place

Will the Swede stay with Spurs?

Last Update:

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi says he wants midfielder Lucas Bergvall to stay at the club and develop into a ‘top player’ but will not promise the Sweden international a starting role.

De Zerbi has spent big this summer in recruiting Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Mateus Fernandes from London rivals West Ham.

That has seemingly pushed Bergvall, 20, down the pecking order and he has been linked with moves to Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

Bergvall started as Spurs’ pre-season continued with a penalty shootout win in Sydney and De Zerbi said after the game that his midfielder’s future remains unclear.

“I’m always being very clear with him and with you. I would like that he stays with us,” said De Zerbi.

“I think he’s potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don’t want to convince anyone to stay. Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay.

“He can find the space if he stays with us. The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad – not just 11 players – especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons.

“Football is going in a clear direction – to compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don’t want 24, but 21, 22 of a high level.”

Bergvall started in a deeper midfield role in Sydney alongside Archie Gray, a position it is reported that he facours. But De Zerbi has doubts over his ability to play there.

De Zerbi continued: “He wants space. He wants to play as a double pivot as a position. I can’t give, for any player in the world, their place in the first XI guaranteed.

“I want to be honest with the players. I want to be clear. I don’t want to make the first mistake. In terms of position, I can’t give a guarantee. It’s right when he wants to play as a central midfielder.

“But to play as a central midfielder, sometimes it is to attack, sometimes to keep the holder, to move the ball faster. He has to improve.”

articles.title: Henderson has Brentford contract terminated as he closes in on move to Chelsea
articles.summary: Chelsea have edged closer to the surprise signing of Jordan Henderson after the England midfielder left Brentford
articles.content:
Henderson has Brentford contract terminated as he closes in on move to Chelsea

Chelsea have edged closer to the surprise signing of Jordan Henderson after the England midfielder left Brentford

Last Update:

Jordan Henderson has left Brentford ahead of his anticipated move to Chelsea.

The 36-year-old spent just 12 months at the Gtech Community Stadium, making 34 appearances for the Bees after joining from Ajax, but has now had his contract terminated.

That paves the way for a move across London to Stamford Bridge with Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso eager to add some experience to a young squad.

Henderson is renown for his professional attitude and Alonso is hoping that influence will inspire a group that limped to 10th in the Premier League last season.

The England international told Brentford’s official website: “I leave Brentford with a lot of gratitude for the opportunity the club gave me, and for the support and care shown to me and my family from day one.

“Coming back to the Premier League was really important to me, and Brentford gave me that chance. I’ll always be thankful for that.

“I hope I was able to play my part in helping the team through an important period for the club. We achieved a lot together last season, and it’s something everyone involved should be proud of.

“Brentford is a special football club. It’s ambitious, progressive and full of good people. From the owners and leadership, to the coaching staff, the players and everyone behind the scenes, it’s been a privilege to be part of it.”

Henderson could be joined at Chelsea by Welbeck

Henderson started out at Sunderland before a big-money move to Liverpool in 2011. He made 492 appearances for the Merseyside club, taking over from Steven Gerrard as captain and lifting six major trophies, including the Premier League and Champions League.

A short, ill-advised move to Al-Ettifaq in Saudi Arabia was followed by a spell with Ajax before he joined Brentford.

Henderson’s switch to Chelsea is likely to be completed in the coming days and he could be joined by another thirtysomething in Danny Welbeck.

The Brighton forward is also a target for Chelsea, who are currently on a pre-season tour of Asia.

articles.title: Real Madrid 2026/27: Rodri, Diomande and Cucurella – how the XI could look under Mourinho
articles.summary: Real Madrid are making significant moves in the transfer market and if they can secure their targets, they will have a significantly stronger XI next season
articles.content:
Real Madrid 2026/27: Rodri, Diomande and Cucurella – how the XI could look under Mourinho

Real Madrid are making significant moves in the transfer market and if they can secure their targets, they will have a significantly stronger XI next season

Last Update:

Real Madrid have endured two trophyless seasons with the 2025/26 campaign arguably one of the worst in the club’s illustrious history with dressing room discord undermining the efforts of Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa.

Having strengthened his position as president by seeing off the challenge of Enrique Riquelme, Florentino Perez brought Jose Mourinho back to the Santiago Bernabeu and tasked with him with returning the club to glory both domestically and in Europe.

Perez promised to spend big as part of his new mandate but progress so far has been steady rather than spectacular with Marc Cucurella the most lavish investment, the Spain full-back brought in from Chelsea for a fee that could rise to £51.8million.

Denzel Dumfries arrived from Inter Milan for £17.1m while experienced duo Bernardo Silva and Ibrahima Konate joined on free transfers after their contracts expired at Manchester City and Liverpool respectively.

However, that level of prudence is set to end with two big-name players seemingly set to join the Mourinho revolution.

The first will be Yan Diomande, the Ivory Coast winger. Madrid have been locked in talks with RB Leipzig for several weeks and, after a brief stand-off, a resolution appears close.

The 19-year-old is likely to cost Madrid in the region of £102m, making him the most expensive African player of all time. The fee also represents a remarkable piece of business for Leipzig, who signed him from Leganes for £17m just 12 months ago.

Diomande is likely to be joined in the Spanish capital by Rodri. Manchester City’s insistence on keeping the Ballon d’Or and World Cup winner appears to have weakened and talks have reportedly started that would see the 30-year-old return to La Liga after a glorious seven-year spell at the Etihad.

Madrid are not just making progress on players coming in.

Vinicius Jr’s long-standing contract issue is drawing to a conclusion with Madrid’s latest offer likely to be accepted. The Brazilian has less than 12 months left on his current deal, prompting Premier League champions Arsenal to make tentative enquiries, a move that appears to have galvanised Madrid into getting a deal done.

The addition of Diomande and Rodri, as well as keeping Vinicius Jr, would require a huge outlay from Madrid but would provide Mourinho with a new-look line up that would surely get the 15-time European champions back on the right footing.

Here is how they could line-up next season:

Table of Contents

GOALKEEPER

Thibaut CourtoisNo change here with Courtois well-established as one of the best goalkeepers in the world. The giant Belgian is a key cog in the Madrid machine.

DEFENDERS

Right-backDenzel DumfriesThe Netherlands international has been one of the stand-out right-backs in European football over the past few years and his willingness to drive forward and support the attack ought to give Madrid a new dimension.  Right-back was a problem last season with Trent Alexander-Arnold struggling for full fitness and Dani Carvajal falling out of favour. That often led to Federico Valverde playing out of position but that should not happen this term.

Central DefenderIbrahima KonateKonate will probably get the nod over Dean Huijsen due to his physicality. Struggled with off-field issues at Liverpool last season and remains prone to the odd mistake but is set to make up a rugged central pairing with Antonio Rudiger.

Central DefenderAntonio RudigerThe Germany international is now 33 but remains an important member of the Madrid side. Quite similar to Konate in playing style, Rudiger is also an influential voice in the Madrid dressing room. Has been accused of not always using his status wisely but his combative nature is likely to sit well with Mourinho.

Left-backMarc CucurellaThere will be no lack of fight in the Madrid defence next season with Cucurella another who will bring a competitive edge. The outstanding full-back at the World Cup, Cucurella will end Madrid’s problem down the left of their defence.

MIDFIELDERS

RodriThe best in the world in the holding midfield role and arguably the best ever. The Spain international controls the tempo of the game, always looks to play forward and pass through the lines and also comes up with important goals. If Madrid can prise him away from City, it would transform their prospects overnight.

Federico ValverdeEndured a pretty woeful 2025/26 season that saw him shunted between midfield and defence and ended in a training ground fracas with Aurelien Tchouameni that saw him hospitalised. There were bright spots, a brilliant hat-trick against Manchester City in the Champions League, that showed again what he is capable of. The Uruguayan will benefit from some Mourinho love.

Jude BellinghamBellingham is another who struggled to find top gear last season but a brilliant World Cup with England means he should be full of confidence ahead of the new campaign. Technically good, physically strong and good with the ball at his feet – Bellingham possesses every quality required in a modern-day midfielder.

ATTACKERS

Right-wingYan DiomandeYes, Diomande has predominately played on the left but at just 19 years of age, there is no reason why he can’t learn the skills required to play on the opposite side. Quick, strong and deadly in a one-on-one, he will provide great balance to a Madrid attack that has looked lop-sided at times.

Left-wingVinicius JrThe Brazil international often looked disinterested last season and the Bernabeu crowd were quick to let him know they were not impressed. The 26-year-old, who will return to Spain with a new look, will likely use that as fuel to show he is still the star player that has tormented defences over the years. That will be music to Mourinho’s ears.

StrikerKylian MbappeLike Vinicius, Mbappe has endured a love-hate relationship with the Madrid fanbase at times. The ability is unquestionable and his record in Spain of 86 goals across two seasons show he is the perfect man to lead the attack.

articles.title: ‘I made a lot of mistakes’ – Amorim says he learned a lot from Man Utd failings
articles.summary: Former United boss is now with AC Milan
articles.content:
‘I made a lot of mistakes’ – Amorim says he learned a lot from Man Utd failings

Former United boss is now with AC Milan

Last Update:

Former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim admitted he ‘made a lot of mistakes’ during his tenure at Old Trafford.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 63 games, winning just 24 with 18 draws and 21 defeats.

Amorim took charge in November 2024 – and was described as the ‘head coach’ by United at the time – but has failed to implement the ideas that made him one of Europe’s most highly regarded tacticians during his time at Sporting CP.

The club finished 15th in the Premier League in his first season, just four points above the relegation zone, with Amorim’s preferred 3-4-3 formation being a regular talking point.

He has now arrived at AC Milan and says he is ready to learn from his errors at the Serie A giants.

“They [Milan] appointed me because they felt I was the right guy for the way I want to play,” Amorim told Sky Italia. “They want to play the same way, but I think they signed me not just for my success, but also for my experience with a top club like Manchester United.

“They understood that I was prepared for this job, not just because of my past success, but also because of my failures. I think it helped a lot in those meetings.”

When asked what went wrong at United, Amorim said: “The first thing is that it doesn’t matter anymore. That is the feeling. There’s a history, then something happens, the context changes, and you focus on the next challenge.

“I learned a lot. It would be hard to point to one thing, but the important thing that I clearly know is that I made a lot of mistakes.

“When you do this kind of reflection, and you understand that it was not just their fault, but also my fault, I think you can be a better coach and a better man.”

Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season and will be in the Europa League.

articles.title: ‘I made history’ – Neymar confirms he has retired from Brazil duty
articles.summary: Neymar retires as Brazil's record goalscorer
articles.content:
‘I made history’ – Neymar confirms he has retired from Brazil duty

Neymar retires as Brazil's record goalscorer

Last Update:

Neymar has retired from international duty with Brazil following their disappointing World Cup.

The 34-year-old is his nation’s record goalscorer with 80 goals in 130 caps and scored in a fourth World Cup with a penalty against Norway.

But he could not save Carlo Ancelotti’s side from an early exit and struggled for fitness throughout.

Back with Santos and back in the headlines, the former Barcelona forward has now confirmed he will not play in the famous yellow shirt again.

“My time with the national team is over. I made history, I was very happy, I gave my all, my life,” he said.

“I always fought and gave my best for this jersey, but I think I don’t want it anymore.”

Neymar made his Brazil debut in 2010, scoring on his debut against the USA. He was a star at the 2014 World Cup until he injured his back and without him Brazil were humiliated 7-1 by Germany in the semi-final.

He won the Confederations Cup in 2013 and was runner-up in the Copa America of 2021 but retires after being unable to guide Brazil to a major honour.

Neymar received criticism in the Brazilian press this week after he took part in a poker tournament while he was returning to full fitness following the World Cup.

The 34-year-old celebrated in his comeback match by pretending to deal poker cards, having explained at the time of the reports that he had trained with Santos and been given permission to pursue his pastime.

Former Al-Hilal, Paris-Saint-Germain and Barcelona playmaker Neymar now has six goals in this season’s Serie A, scoring his first club goals since May 10 on his first Santos appearance since May 17.
