articles.title: Jurgen Klopp confirmed as new head coach of Germany and threatens to quit if media hassle his family
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp has returned to management with his native Germany
articles.content:
Jurgen Klopp confirmed as new head coach of Germany and threatens to quit if media hassle his family

Jurgen Klopp has returned to management with his native Germany

Last Update:

Jurgen Klopp has been appointed as the new head coach of Germany.

Klopp has signed a four-year contract that will take him through to the 2030 World Cup having received the unanimous backing of the German Football Association supervisory board.

It sees the former Liverpool boss return to the dugout for the first time since he left Anfield at the end of the 2023/24 season. Since then the 59-year-old has worked as Red Bull’s global head of football.

At his presentation in Frankfurt, he said: “It is a great honour to sit here today. What has happened to me in the last few days is like a movie that goes through your head. Where did it all start, where did you come from? I already had an idea of how big the role of the national coach is but when you are associated with it, you feel the greatness and responsibility even more.”

The DFB also confirmed the appointments of Peter Krawietz, Pep Lijnders and Sven Bender as Klopp’s assistants while former Arsenal defender Per Mertesacker will take on the role of DFB managing director for sport from the start of 2027.

Table of Contents

If you go after my family, I am gone – Klopp warns German media

While the atmosphere at the news conference was jovial, Klopp also had a word of warning for the assembled media.

“I’m not doing this job for myself, I’m doing it for you,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated Julian Nagelsmann. I’m taking it even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated Thomas Tuchel.

“If you go after my family, I’m gone. If you think I’m rubbish, tell me to my face and I’ll leave immediately, without asking for any compensation.

“Jurgen Klopp has no career after the national team. This is ideally the highlight of my career.”

Jurgen Klopp’s first four games as Germany boss

Sep 24: Netherlands (A)

Sep 27: Greece (H)

October 1: Serbia (H)

October 4: Greece (A)

Klopp tries to limit expectations

Klopp attended the 2026 World Cup as a pundit and watched as Nagelsmann’s Germany crashed out at the round of 32 stage, losing on penalties to Paraguay.

And he has warned against expecting too much, too soon.

“The expectations in Germany are madness. Imagine if Nagelsmann had said ‘we want to get to the semi-finals?’ What would have people said?” he added.

“Of course, we want to achieve the highest goals. We should realise that we need time for this.

“We need a realistic expectation. Players will get opportunities that do not yet expect it. Because I like to be brave. I always have been and I will remain so. I want to work with players who play a football that everyone likes. This is not always successful immediately, but I want to get people to go home after the game and say, ‘wow!’

“Counterpressing will be an important topic, a stable formation, a clear football idea. The teams that could win the World Cup played with four men at the back. We will do the same. We will also play with wingers. The playmakers of today’s generation are on the wing.

BREAKING: Chelsea close in on Lacroix after fee agreed with Crystal Palace

Xabi Alonso is close to securing another major target after Chelsea and Crystal Palace agreed a fee for France defender Maxence Lacroix

Last Update:

Chelsea have had a bid accepted by Crystal Palace for defender Maxence Lacroix.

The France international will cost the Blues in the region of £52million and is currently undergoing a medical with the West London club, according to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano.

There were suggestions Axel Disasi would move in the opposite direction but that is not thought to be the case.

Lacroix is expected to sign a six-year contract at Stamford Bridge as Chelsea continue another summer of lavish spending.

Chelsea spending continues

The 26-year-old will join a squad that has recently been bolstered by the signings of Morgan Rogers (£117m), Geovany Quenda (£43.3m) and Marco Palestra (£43m).

Chelsea have balanced the books partially by offloading Marc Cucurella (£51.8m) to Real Madrid, Andrey Santos (£50m) to Manchester United and Alejandro Garnacho on loan to Aston Villa.

Palestra could form a new central defensive pairing with Lacroix, who was one of the standout players in another impressive season for Palace.

He made 55 appearances in all competitions, and started in the Eagles’ 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano in the final of the Conference League.

Lacroix’s form earned him a call-up to the France squad for the World Cup and he appeared in three games, including Les Bleus’ 6-4 defeat to England in the third-fourth place play-off.

His sale represents another clever piece of business for Palace who signed Lacroix from Wolfsburg for £15.4m from Wolfsburg two years ago.

articles.title: Albertini: Guardiola can’t fix Italy while academies ignore young players
articles.summary: Pep Guardiola is one of the options - alongside Roberto Mancini, Andre Pirlo and Antonio Conte - to become Italy coach but former Azzurri midfielder Demetrio Albertini is not 100% convinced he will succeed until wider issues are addressed
articles.content:
Albertini: Guardiola can’t fix Italy while academies ignore young players

Pep Guardiola is one of the options - alongside Roberto Mancini, Andre Pirlo and Antonio Conte - to become Italy coach but former Azzurri midfielder Demetrio Albertini is not 100% convinced he will succeed until wider issues are addressed

Last Update:

Pep Guardiola would struggle to succeed as Italy coach due to institutional problems in Serie A, according to former Azzurri midfielder Demetrio Albertini.

Guardiola has held talks with the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) regarding the vacant head coach job and, although there is no agreement yet, the possibility of former Manchester City boss Guardiola making a swift return to football remains.

Italy won Euro 2020 but have failed to reach the last three World Cups as they struggle to find an identity.

Guardiola would provide that but Albertini is not convinced the Spaniard’s possession-heavy philosophy would necessarily work in Italy, given it is not taught in academies from a young age.

He told AS: “About Pep Guardiola, what to say… We are talking about one of the greatest, without a doubt. But you have to be convinced that you can work here [in Italy]. You must understand if your philosophy can marry up.

“Let’s see… Italy, its DNA, differs from Spain in the way it interprets soccer. We have to implement a pathway for our young talents. I think that, in Italy, today, it is not designed. In Spain, with its unique style, yes. You can’t change the DNA.”

Table of Contents

Italy can achieve success in other ways – Albertini

Guardiola is on an FIGC shortlist that also contains Roberto Mancini, Antonio Conte and Andre Pirlo as they look for a successor to Gennaro Gattuso.

And Albertini, who is a former FIGC vice-president, insists Italy can still achieve success even if Guardiola is not appointed.

He added: “We are talking about a national team coach, not a club coach. It’s not the same. Sometimes, there are many diverse philosophies that can work very well in international football. We don’t have a philosophical journey like the Spanish one, but we do have four World Cups and two European Championships.

“Soccer is wonderful because it brings you closer to victory in different ways. If we think about the final of the World Cup, if we had reached penalties… Who says that Argentina would not have won, even if it had played differently. The diversity of interpretation of the game is enormous. And, yes, you may like one or the other more.”

Youth needs to be given a chance in Italy

Albertini suggested the national team would struggle irrespective of the coach until the mindset of overlooking young players changed.

In the 2024/2025 season, just 1.9% of total minutes in Serie A were taken by Italy-eligible players under the age of 21 – the second lowest in the top 50 leagues globally. Only the United Arab Emirates Pro League managed fewer.

“Do you know how many Spanish champions at the last World Cup played in the reserves?” he asked. “I think 22 out of 26. If we go back, to 2010, more than 20 again. In short, about 90%. Rodri, for example, do you know how many games he played in the reserves (Villarreal B)? More than 40. We are talking about the Spain captain, Ballon d’Or…. That is a training process.

“Today few Italian footballers are prepared to compete in Serie A. Very few. Few clubs have the courage to bet on local talents. So they will never be able to mature or reach higher levels. Potential is slowed down.

“In Spain, a 17-year-old talent has opportunities to prove who he is. They immediately make him play with the older players. They give him options. One after another. Today, in my country, there are no 17- or 18-year-olds in Serie A. Not even on the bench.”

articles.title: Who is JJ Gabriel? Why Manchester United have to be patient with ‘big talent’
articles.summary: JJ Gabriel has impressed for Man United at youth level
articles.content:
Who is JJ Gabriel? Why Manchester United have to be patient with ‘big talent’

JJ Gabriel has impressed for Man United at youth level

Last Update:

With JJ Gabriel nearing a Premier League debut for Manchester United, head coach Michael Carrick has explained why the 15-year-old has been promoted astonishingly early.

Having included Gabriel in first-team training since his appointment in January, Carrick says the forward has been “doing really well”.

“JJ is a big talent,” acknowledged Carrick. “We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development.”

Why has Gabriel impressed Carrick and when could he play for the first team? Here’s what we know about the academy sensation.

JJ Gabriel has two goals for @ManUtd in their #FAYouthCup campaign so far ⚽️Will he add to his tally tonight? 🔴📺 Watch live on the Emirates FA Cup YouTube channel pic.twitter.com/yV2oB3Qtwm

Table of Contents

JJ Gabriel stats: Why Man United are excited about forward

In his first season as a regular at Under-18 Premier League level, Gabriel scored his 21st goal in 23 appearances in all competitions in a win over title rivals Manchester City on March 21.

He netted hat-tricks against Derby County and Liverpool and the goal against City was the seventh consecutive match in all competitions in which Gabriel had scored, finding the net 10 times in total across those games and contributing an assist.

“JJ is a fantastic talent,” Under-18s lead coach Darren Fletcher said, via United’s website. “I’ve enjoyed working with him immensely, getting to know him.

“He’s a young lad with a massive hype. There’s a lot of noise around him – and deservedly so, because he’s a really talented kid.”

A post shared by Manchester United (@manutd)

When could JJ Gabriel play for Manchester United?

Premier League rules state that players must be 15 by August 31 in a season to feature for a first team in the campaign.

Gabriel was 15 on October 6, so he will not be eligible to feature in the league until 2026/27.

With many of United’s first-team players at the World Cup this summer, the chances could rise of Gabriel playing for the first team during pre-season.

Two break-out teenage stars of this Premier League campaign – Arsenal’s Max Dowman and Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha – first caught most supporters’ eye when they shone for their clubs during pre-season last year.

Ruben Amorim, who left his role as permanent manager in January, was the first boss to involve Gabriel in the first-team squad and Carrick, who improved United’s form considerably after initially becoming interim head coach until the end of the season, will surely be tempted to give him minutes now he has landed the job permanently.

Age rules are different for the FA Cup, leading to Fletcher being asked if he was going to give Gabriel a place in his matchday squad before overseeing a third round defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion in January.

“He could be, but he’s not going to be,” replied Fletcher, who briefly took charge between Amorim’s exit and Carrick’s arrival.

“Anybody could be picked. I’m super excited by his talent, but the most important thing is that he keeps developing.

“He’s doing fantastically well but he’s still got lots to learn. He’s developing within there, but the world’s his oyster and he just needs to go on his journey. His time will come in due course.

“For just now, it’s a little bit early, I think. A lot of people would agree with me, but I couldn’t speak highly enough of JJ.”

Which positions can JJ Gabriel play in?

United have used Gabriel in central midfield, attacking midfield, as a centre-forward and on the left wing. “He works hard,” said Fletcher, discussing Gabriel’s attitude and personal qualities.

“The first thing I say is he loves football. He loves training; he loves playing, he loves having the ball, he loves expressing himself.

“He makes fantastic decisions; he’s just got an enthusiasm for the game that’s amazing. A 15-year-old with a bright future ahead of him.

“He’s got an amazing family and amazing support around him, and he’s someone we’re delighted to have at the club.

“We just hope he keeps improving, learning every day and keeps being the boy that he is really, enjoying playing football and going and expressing himself and scoring lots of goals so that Manchester United Under-18s win every game. Then I’ll be a happy man.”

JJ Gabriel England record

Gabriel has won six caps for England at Under-15 level and three at Under-16 level. His first international goal is yet to come.

He was called up at Under-17 level for the first time in March 2026 for matches against Faroe Islands, Israel and Estonia at training base St George’s Park.

The Irish Mirror reported that Gabriel was born and raised in the UK but is eligible to play for England, Ireland, Cyprus and Trinidad and Tobago through his Irish father, Cypriot mother and Trinidadian grandfather.

Will JJ Gabriel become United’s youngest-ever player?

Gabriel could follow in the footsteps of the likes of Ngumoha and Dowman by breaking records at his club.

Ngumoha became the Reds’ youngest-ever scorer with a goal against Newcastle this season when the winger was four days shy of his 17th birthday.

Attacking midfielder Dowman became the youngest scorer in the history of the Premier League with a solo goal against Everton at the age of 16 years and 73 days.

At 15 years and 10 months old when the 2026/27 season is scheduled to start, Gabriel has a little time on his side to become United’s youngest-ever player and almost the whole season in which to become their youngest player in the modern era.

He will also have more than a year to break Norman Whiteside’s landmark as their youngest scorer. Here’s how the records look for the Red Devils.

articles.title: Elliot Anderson labels City ‘Kings of Manchester’ after sealing £116m move
articles.summary: Anderson stoked the Manchester derby flames after joining City.
articles.content:
Elliot Anderson labels City ‘Kings of Manchester’ after sealing £116m move

Anderson stoked the Manchester derby flames after joining City.

Last Update:

Elliot Anderson declared Manchester City to be the ‘Kings of Manchester’ after sealing a £116million move from Nottingham Forest.

City confirmed the completion of the deal on Thursday, with the England midfielder becoming their fourth signing of the summer.

The 23-year-old has enjoyed a rapid rise since his move from Newcastle United to Nottingham Forest in 2024. His transfer preceded a season in which Newcastle ended their 70-year domestic trophy drought with victory in the EFL Cup, with Forest losing in the semi-finals of the FA Cup in that campaign before going out at the same stage of the Europa League last term.

And Anderson, who featured in every game at the World Cup as England finished third, is excited at the chance to compete for the first silverware of his career under new City boss Enzo Maresca.

Anderson aims Manchester derby dig at United

Speaking about the Manchester derby, which will be contested again at Old Trafford on September 13, Anderson took aim at City’s arch rivals Manchester United with a not so subtle dig.

“It’s one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I’ve known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester,” Anderson said in an interview with City’s website. “It’ll be a great fixture and I can’t wait to be involved in something like that.

“They’re [City] winners, they’re relentless, and that’s the sort of team I want to be a part of – champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they’ve dominated, so that’s why I wanted to join.

“It’s happened quite quick, but I think I always believed I could get to this point and this is where I want to be. Now that I’m here, I’ll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.”

Director of football Hugo Viana, also a former Newcastle midfielder, said of Anderson: “Elliot is one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now.

“He offers energy, outstanding work rate and an exceptional range of passing. His improvement in recent years has been really impressive and underlines his desire to be the best player he can be.

“At just 23, there is plenty of opportunity for development over the coming years and we feel he can become a complete midfielder. Manchester City is the best place for him to develop his game and keep improving, we are glad that he sees things the same way as we do.

“I look forward to seeing Elliot working with us ahead of the new season. I’m sure every City fan is excited to see what he can do.”

Nottingham Forest make first signing under Glasner

Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of Xaver Schlager, making the Austria midfielder their first acquisition under new head coach Oliver Glasner.

The 28-year-old, who has also had spells with Liefering and Red Bull Salzburg, reunites with Glasner, with whom he worked during his stint with Wolfsburg.

And Schlager, who played in all four of Austria’s games at the World Cup, is excited at the chance to work with his compatriot again.

“I am very happy and proud to be here, and I want to give my everything for the club and its supporters.”

articles.title: 2026 Transfer window: What are the five biggest deals of the summer?
articles.summary: What are the biggest transfers of the 2026 summer window?
articles.content:
2026 Transfer window: What are the five biggest deals of the summer?

What are the biggest transfers of the 2026 summer window?

Last Update:

The 2026 summer transfer window has already delivered another flurry of eye-watering deals, with Premier League clubs once again setting the pace in Europe’s market.

England’s top flight has comfortably outspent its rivals, while clubs in Spain, Italy, Germany and France have also invested heavily in a bid to strengthen ahead of the new season.

English clubs dominate the biggest moves completed so far, accounting for all five of the largest transfer fees before July 23.

Central midfielders have emerged as the premium asset of this summer’s market, while Chelsea have once again demonstrated their willingness to spend whatever it takes to land their top targets.

Below, we rank the five biggest transfers completed so far this summer.

Table of Contents

5. Anthony Gordon (Newcastle United to Barcelona) – £69m

Few predicted Anthony Gordon would be the player Barcelona prioritised this summer, but the England international’s move to Catalonia could prove one of the smartest pieces of business of the window.

The Spanish champions have spent years navigating financial restrictions, making Gordon’s £69 million arrival all the more significant. While reports differ over the value of potential add-ons, the guaranteed fee is enough to place the winger among the biggest transfers of the summer.

Barcelona have long admired Gordon’s relentless work rate, direct running and ability to press from the front, qualities that make him a natural fit for Hansi Flick’s high-intensity system.

Still only 25, the former Everton man also offers the kind of long-term value the club have increasingly sought in the transfer market.

For Newcastle, the sale represents a sizeable profit on a player who developed into one of the Premier League’s most dangerous wide forwards.

Yet questions will inevitably be asked after Barcelona were repeatedly linked with Marcus Rashford before eventually turning their attention to Gordon.

4. Mateus Fernandes (West Ham United to Tottenham) – £85m

Tottenham wasted little time smashing their transfer record by agreeing an £85m deal for Mateus Fernandes.

The Portugal international became the first marquee central midfielder to change clubs this summer, setting the tone for what has quickly become the transfer window’s defining trend. Elite midfielders have never been more valuable, and Tottenham were prepared to pay.

Fernandes arrives after suffering relegation with West Ham, a circumstance that did little to diminish his reputation across Europe.

Comfortable receiving possession under pressure, capable of progressing the ball through midfield and mature beyond his years, he is viewed as a player around whom Spurs can build for the next decade.

The fee inevitably raised eyebrows. Spending £85m on a player whose previous club had just dropped into the Championship invited criticism, but Tottenham clearly believe the market has changed. Proven central midfielders in their early twenties are now commanding premiums previously reserved for elite forwards.

Only time will tell whether Fernandes justifies the price tag, but Tottenham have made it clear they believe he can become one of Europe’s outstanding midfielders.

3. Sandro Tonali (Newcastle United to Tottenham) – £92.5m

If Mateus Fernandes was Tottenham’s statement of intent, Sandro Tonali was the move that truly shocked European football.

The Italy international joined Spurs for an initial £92.5m, with the deal capable of reaching £100m through performance-related add-ons. It represents one of the biggest signings ever completed by a club not competing in the Champions League.

Tonali’s desire to leave Newcastle played a significant role. With a return to Serie A financially difficult, London emerged as his preferred destination, allowing Tottenham to capitalise on the situation.

Tonali brings experience, leadership and technical quality that instantly raises the level of their midfield, while his ability to dictate matches should help accelerate the club’s rebuild.

There will inevitably be those who argue Tottenham have overpaid. Spending close to £100m on any midfielder carries risk, but transfer fees continue to rise across Europe.

In the current market, Tottenham clearly decided this was the price required to secure one of the world’s elite midfielders.

2. Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) – £116m

For a brief period, Elliot Anderson became the most expensive British footballer in history.

Manchester City agreed a staggering £116m deal to prise the midfielder away from Nottingham Forest, beating fierce competition for one of England’s brightest talents.

Manchester United had also monitored Anderson, but City’s willingness to break their own transfer record effectively ended the race.

The transfer also shines a spotlight on Newcastle’s decision to sell Anderson without inserting a sell-on clause.

Having departed St James’ Park for a comparatively modest fee, his extraordinary rise means the Magpies will not benefit from one of the biggest transfers in British football history.

City view Anderson as a cornerstone of their next generation. Dynamic in possession, relentless out of it and capable of influencing games in multiple midfield roles, he possesses the attributes required to thrive in Pep Guardiola’s demanding system.

1. Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa to Chelsea) – £117m

Chelsea have made headlines with blockbuster transfers for much of the past four years, and Morgan Rogers is the latest addition to that list.

The West London club paid £117m to sign the Aston Villa star, making him the most expensive British footballer ever and the biggest transfer completed anywhere in the world this summer.

The fee is remarkable not only because of its size, but because Chelsea continue to spend aggressively despite missing out on Champions League football.

Questions surrounding the club’s finances have done little to slow their activity in the transfer market, with Rogers identified as the marquee addition to spearhead the next phase of their project.

For Aston Villa, the deal represents an extraordinary return on investment and provides significant financial flexibility.

With more than a month of the transfer window still remaining, Chelsea’s record-breaking deal could yet be eclipsed.

articles.title: Arsenal: Tzolis delights in ‘amazing’ Emirates switch after Gunners seal £34m deal
articles.summary: Tzolis will fill a void on the left wing for the Gunners.
articles.content:
Arsenal: Tzolis delights in ‘amazing’ Emirates switch after Gunners seal £34m deal

Tzolis will fill a void on the left wing for the Gunners.

Last Update:

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

The Greece international has joined on a long-term deal, with Arsenal not specifying the exact length of the 24-year-old’s contract after the Belgian club accepted an offer in the region of £34 million for his services.

Tzolis becomes Arsenal’s third signing of the summer after defender Piero Hincapie’s loan move was made permanent and the Gunners signed backup goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

Tzolis, who has previously played in the Premier League with Norwich City and had spells with hometown club PAOK, Twente and Fortuna Dusseldorf, enjoyed a stunning 2025/26 season with Brugge.

Tzolis provided 17 goals and 23 assists as Brugge regained the Belgian Pro League title, also scoring twice and setting up one goal to help Brugge reach the play-off round of the Champions League, in which they lost to Atletico Madrid.

Tzolis will fill the void on the left wing following Leandro Trossard’s move to Besiktas and is relishing the chance to play regularly at Emirates Stadium, having made his Premier League debut at Arsenal’s home.

“It’s absolutely amazing to sign for such a big club – the champions of England. I’m very proud to be part of this team for the next season,” Tzolis told Arsenal.com.

“When my agent was saying maybe it was a possibility, I was already excited. Afterwards, it was getting more serious – and now I’m here.

“I had a nice conversation [with manager Mikel Arteta]. It was around an hour. We talked about everything: the club, myself, his plans, about me, of course, and about the team. It was only positive things.

“I’m a direct player; I go for goals or assists. That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.

“I can say more or less that I know the level of the Premier League. I know it’s the best league in the world. Of course it’s different if you play for Norwich or Arsenal; you have the ball more as a player of Arsenal. So we attack more the other teams.

“It’s very physical. The league and the quality is very high, so I’m prepared for that. Also in the Champions League it’s quite high, so I believe every game is like a Champions League game here in Premier League.”

Tzolis eager to open Arsenal account after Brugge frustration

Tzolis played against Arsenal in the Champions League last season, but was unable to find the net as Brugge were frustrated in a 3-0 defeat.

Now he is eager to open his account for the Gunners, who will face Manchester City in the Community Shield on August 16 before taking on newly promoted Coventry City in their Premier League opener five days later.

“I love to watch football,” Tzolis added. “I know everything about the Premier League, I know everything about Arsenal.

“I watched so many games this year and especially we played against each other. It was 3-0 in our stadium [during the group stage on December 10].

“I can say it was the most difficult team to attack against that I’ve played so far.

“We played against other big teams but, against Arsenal, we had the most difficulties to make clear chances.

“We had some chances, but not very clear. They were very efficient also and scored three amazing goals against us, it was a fair result in the end.

“It’s actually incredible that I made my Premier League debut at the Emirates. I was saying this the other day to my family – it was a great memory.

“I was in love with the stadium. I was always saying it was one of the best stadiums I’ve played in. In the end we lost 1-0, but I really liked my first game so I’ll always remember that I played here at Emirates. I’m looking forward to playing again more.

“My targets are to win titles, of course. For everybody, the target is there – [to win] as many as possible. And to have as much as possible game time with the team – then the rest will come, I’m sure about that.

“For me, the most important [element] is to settle well in the team, have a good feeling, play as much as possible and then we’ll be very good, I believe.

“I’m very proud to be part of this amazing team. I’m looking forward to meeting everybody on the pitch, at the stadium, and to scoring my first goal at the Emirates.”

articles.title: Newcastle in communication with Liverpool over Keegan tribute for Premier League opener
articles.summary: Tributes have poured in since Keegan's passing on Monday.
articles.content:
Newcastle in communication with Liverpool over Keegan tribute for Premier League opener

Tributes have poured in since Keegan's passing on Monday.

Last Update:

Newcastle United have confirmed they are in communication with Liverpool to ensure Kevin Keegan’s memory is “marked fittingly” before their Premier League opener.

Former Newcastle manager Keegan died on Monday aged 75 after his family announced in January that he had been diagnosed with stage-four cancer.

Tributes have poured in for Keegan in the wake of his passing, and Newcastle confirmed their plans to honour his life throughout their pre-season schedule while providing an update on the steps being taken ahead of the Liverpool game on August 23.

Newcastle’s first team, the Under-21s and the women’s team will wear black armbands for all of their respective pre-season fixtures. A minute’s silence will be held before Saturday’s friendly with neighbours Gateshead, who will also wear black armbands, while Keegan’s image will be displayed on the big screen in the seventh minute of the game at Bristol City and home matches with Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, and in the women’s team’s meeting with Inter Milan.

Regarding the Liverpool game, Newcastle said: “The opening Premier League match of the 2026-27 season sees Newcastle United hosting Liverpool – where Kevin made 323 appearances between 1971 and 1977.

“To ensure his memory is marked fittingly before the game, the club is in communication with Liverpool and will work closely with supporter groups, including its Fan Advisory Board, the Newcastle United Supporters Trust and Wor Flags, as well as the Premier League, to shape tributes.”

Keegan is a legendary figure in Newcastle’s history, having sensationally joined the club in 1982 when they were in the old Second Division and he was the PFA Players’ Player of the Year. The move essentially ended Keegan’s England career but he quickly became a hero on Tyneside, helping the Magpies to promotion in his second and final season as a player in the 1983-84 campaign.

He returned as manager eight years later, rescuing the club from relegation to the third tier for the first time before building one of the most celebrated sides in Premier League history following promotion. Keegan’s ‘Entertainers’ twice finished second in the Premier League, famously letting slip a 12-point lead at the top in 1995-96 as they were edged out by Manchester United.

Keegan later had managerial spells with Fulham, England and Manchester City, before a brief and ill-fated return to Newcastle in 2008.

Also a much-loved figure in Liverpool’s history, Keegan joined the Reds from Scunthorpe United in 1971, Keegan won three First Division titles, the FA Cup — scoring twice against Newcastle in the 1974 final — the European Cup and two UEFA Cups in a six-year spell at Anfield that saw him score 100 goals, forming a superb partnership with John Toshack.

He then moved to Hamburg, twice winning the Ballon d’Or in his time there as he lifted the Bundesliga title, before returning to England to join Southampton and then ending his playing career at Newcastle.

Keegan won 63 caps for England, scoring 21 goals, and captained his country. However, he featured in just two major tournaments, Euro 1980 and the 1982 World Cup, as his prime coincided with a period in which England missed out on qualification for two successive World Cup finals.

articles.title: Arsenal home kit 2026/27: Watch the video and see photos of Premier League winners including Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard in new shirt design, cost of jersey, how to buy strip
articles.summary: All you need to know about Arsenal's new home kit
articles.content:
Arsenal home kit 2026/27: Watch the video and see photos of Premier League winners including Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard in new shirt design, cost of jersey, how to buy strip

All you need to know about Arsenal's new home kit

Last Update:

Premier League champions Arsenal have released their new Adidas home shirt as part of the club’s kit for the 2026/27 season.

Familiar sponsors Emirates feature prominently on the front of the shirt, which was announced in May and “celebrates the close connection” between the club and its fans.

The red shirt has a patterned red collar and white sleeves. The shorts are white with red trim and details of Arsenal’s home Emirates Stadium feature as part of the design.

Eberechi Eze, Martin Odegaard and Alessia Russo are among the stars to have shown off the kit. Here are the key details on the release.

Table of Contents

Arsenal home kit 2026/27: When will it be worn first?

Arsenal’s last match of the 2025/26 season is the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday.

They are yet to confirm when the design will debut, with pre-season fixtures a possibility for its first use if it is not worn until preparations for the 2026/27 season begin,

Midfielder Odegaard said wearing the shirt “means representing something much bigger than ourselves”.

“We carry the pride and belonging felt by our supporters around the world,” he added, speaking as the club released a promotional video showing personal conversations between players and fans.

“Our connection with them inspires us and I feel so proud to wear this kit and to honour what this badge and what Arsenal stands for.”

How to buy Arsenal 26/27 home kit

The kit is available from Arsenal’s online shop and superstore. Replica and authentic versions are available, with the latter exactly reflecting the kit worn by the players.

Buyers receive a card they can scan on their phone offering access to an “exclusive portal” featuring player voice notes and the chance to leave messages of their own.

Long-sleeve and short-sleeve versions are available.

How much does the 26/27 Arsenal kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Arsenal replica shirt is £85 or £90 for a long-sleeved version, while the authentic versions start at £120, with personalised or player names and numbers available at an additional cost.

Youth shirts start at £60, while a baby kit is available for £40. The shorts cost between £30 and £45.

Goalkeeper shirts cost between £65 and £85, and a range of other merchandise in the new home design is available, including t-shirts, backpacks and bucket hats.

When does Arsenal’s 2026/27 Premier League season start?

The first round of Premier League matches in 2025/26 will be on the weekend of August 22 2026.

The season will end on May 30 2027.

When are Arsenal’s 2026/27 fixtures released?

The Premier League fixtures for the 2026/27 season will be released on June 19 at 10:00 BST, which is 05:00 ET or 02:00 PT.

articles.title: Japan confirm Moriyasu succession plan
articles.summary: Moriyasu will bow out as coach next year.
articles.content:
Japan confirm Moriyasu succession plan

Moriyasu will bow out as coach next year.

Last Update:

Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu will continue in his role until the end of the 2027 Asian Cup, when he will replaced by Go Oiwa.

Moriyasu said after Japan’s last-32 exit at the 2026 World Cup that he would take time to consider his future.

And it has been confirmed he will not lead the Samurai Blue into the 2030 tournament.

Next year’s Asian Cup will be held in Saudi Arabia, where Japan will attempt to mark Moriyasu’s final competition in charge by winning it for the fifth time and the first time since 2011.

Oiwa, the coach of the Under-21 team, will then take over. He will also continue in his role with the U21s and the Under-23 side as Japan attempt to qualify for the 2028 Olympic Games.

The Samurai Blue had high hopes of winning a World Cup knockout game for the first time in their history at the 2026 World Cup but, after finishing as runners-up in their group behind the Netherlands, they suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Brazil to end their tournament one round shy of the last 16.

Japan led through Kaishu Sano’s 29th-minute strike, but a Casemiro header levelled things for Brazil, who then completed the turnaround with a 95th-minute winner from Gabriel Martinelli.

Moriyasu took charge in July 2018 following their last-16 exit in the World Cup finals in Russia. He led them to the 2019 Asian Cup final, which they lost to Qatar, before guiding Japan to wins over Germany and Spain as they won their World Cup group in 2022 before going out on penalties to Croatia.

With Japan’s performance in North America coming three years on from a disappointing quarter-final exit at the Asian Cup, Moriyasu came under scrutiny for a defensive approach in attempting to protect Japan’s lead against Brazil.

Moriyasu will have the chance to go out on a high at the Asian Cup, in which Japan have been drawn alongside Qatar, Thailand and Indonesia in Group F.

articles.content:
Barcelona confirm signing of Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund

Barcelona have completed the transfer of Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

Last Update:

Barcelona have completed the signing of Germany forward Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

The deal is worth an initial £19million, with a further £6m in performance-related add-ons. Dortmund will also receive a percentage of any future profit Barcelona make should Adeyemi be sold.

The 24-year-old becomes Barcelona’s second signing of the summer following the arrival of England winger Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Head coach Hansi Flick was instrumental in bringing Adeyemi to Camp Nou, having previously handed the forward his senior Germany debut during his time in charge of the national team.

Adeyemi adds versatility to Barcelona’s attack, with the ability to play across all three forward positions.

He leaves Dortmund after four seasons, having joined the Bundesliga club from RB Salzburg in 2022. During his time in Germany, he scored 36 goals in 146 appearances across all competitions.

Despite strengthening their frontline with the additions of Adeyemi and Gordon, Barcelona are still expected to pursue another striker before the transfer window closes.

The club’s current attacking options also include Lamine Yamal, Raphinha and Ferran Torres.

articles.title: Newcastle fill key void as they agree £35m deal for Monaco midfielder Bamba
articles.summary: Bamba will become Newcastle's fourth signing.
articles.content:
Newcastle fill key void as they agree £35m deal for Monaco midfielder Bamba

Bamba will become Newcastle's fourth signing.

Last Update:

Newcastle United have agreed a deal to sign midfielder Aladji Bamba from Monaco.

According to multiple reports, Bamba is travelling to Tyneside for a medical after an agreement was reached on a €41million (£35m) package.

Newcastle will pay an initial £30m, with the remainder coming in the form of add-ons.

The 20-year-old is set to become Newcastle’s fourth signing of what has been another testing summer for the Magpies.

Newcastle have already signed France Under-21 goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, Ivory Coast winger Bazoumana Toure and another midfielder in 18-year-old Sean Steur, who joined from Ajax.

Bamba only broke into Monaco’s first team last season, making 25 appearances in all competitions, with 12 of them starts. A primarily defensive midfielder, Bamba provided two assists in his 18 Ligue 1 games.

The focus on youth represents a shift in approach from Newcastle, who have seen Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali leave for Barcelona and Tottenham respectively. There remain questions around the future of captain Bruno Guimaraes amid interest from Arsenal.

Newcastle have also missed out on two priority targets in the form of Victor Munoz and Johan Manzambi. Munoz signed for Liverpool while Manzambi opted to join Aston Villa.

But in Bamba they appear to have landed a player who fills a long-time hole for manager Eddie Howe.

Newcastle fill key void as Bruno speculation lingers

While Newcastle’s midfield trio of Tonali, Guimaraes and Joelinton was regularly praised as one of the best in the Premier League in previous seasons, they have long since lacked a true defensive midfielder.

The absence of a number six became increasingly apparent last season as Newcastle’s form dipped and they slumped to a disappointing 12th-placed finish.

Too often, opponents were able to find significant space between defence and midfield and put Newcastle under significant pressure. The 2025-26 campaign marked the first in which they conceded more league goals (55) than they scored (53) since the 2021-22 camapign, when Howe came in after the Saudi-led takeover and rescued the club from relegation.

While he is inexperienced, Newcastle will hope Bamba can fix that issue having impressed in his first season in Ligue 1.

Per Opta, Bamba won 9.1 duels per 90 minutes in Ligue 1 in 2025-26, the most of any midfielder to play 500-plus minutes.

Though Newcastle have addressed one issue in midfield, they could yet need to find a replacement for talismanic skipper Guimaraes, should he indeed get his wish of a move to Arsenal.

While reports from Newcastle have insisted the club has not received a formal approach from the Gunners, the Premier League champions are expected to intensify their efforts to sign the Brazil star. Newcastle are said to value Guimaraes at £100m.

And with Joe Willock reportedly in talks over a move to Besiktas, at least one more midfield incoming appears likely for Newcastle before the end of the transfer window.

articles.summary: James Trafford could be on his way to Leeds from Manchester City.
articles.content:
Leeds in talks with Manchester City over James Trafford transfer as Newcastle cool interest

James Trafford could be on his way to Leeds from Manchester City.

Last Update:

Leeds are in talks with Manchester City over the signing of goalkeeper James Trafford, with the England international understood to favour a move to Elland Road.

Leeds are in the market for a new first-choice goalkeeper after Karl Darlow left the club on a free transfer to join Manchester United.

Trafford, 23, returned to Manchester City from Burnley last summer after progressing through the club’s academy.

He expected to become City’s first-choice goalkeeper but instead spent most of the 2025-26 season as Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy following the Italian’s arrival on deadline day.

Speaking in February, Trafford admitted the role was “not what I expected” and said he had tried to avoid finding himself in that position.

Newcastle remained interested in the goalkeeper after attempting to sign him last summer, but have also explored alternative options, including Parma’s Zion Suzuki and Brighton’s Carl Rushworth.

The Magpies have already signed Ewen Jaouen from Reims, while current first-choice goalkeeper Nick Pope could leave if another senior shot-stopper arrives, although the latest reports suggest interest has cooled.

Leeds still have Lucas Perri, who joined from Lyon last summer, and Alex Cairns on their books, but are keen to strengthen between the posts ahead of the new season.

Trafford made 17 appearances for City during the 2025-26 campaign, featuring throughout both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup as Pep Guardiola’s side lifted both trophies.

Before returning to the Etihad Stadium, Trafford established himself as Burnley’s first-choice goalkeeper over two seasons, playing a key role in Scott Parker’s side winning promotion to the Premier League after conceding just 16 goals in 46 Championship matches during the 2024-25 season.

He made his senior England debut in March, earned a second cap later that month and was included in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for this summer’s World Cup.

articles.title: MLS round-up: Inter Miami win without Messi as Griezmann and Lewandowski make debuts
articles.summary: Catch up with the latest action from Major League Soccer.
articles.content:
MLS round-up: Inter Miami win without Messi as Griezmann and Lewandowski make debuts

Catch up with the latest action from Major League Soccer.

Last Update:

Major League Soccer returned from its six-week World Cup break on Wednesday night with a statement of intent from the competition’s biggest names, and it was a 39-year-old Uruguayan, not the two marquee European arrivals making their debuts, who stole the show.

Table of Contents

Miami march on without Messi

Inter Miami handled business at Nu Stadium, beating Chicago Fire 3-2 in a pulsating return to action.

With Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul taking extended rest following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final, it fell to Luis Suarez to keep Miami’s momentum alive.

The veteran Uruguayan delivered, scoring twice to send the Herons to a fifth consecutive victory and take his tally for the season to eight goals.

Chicago opened the scoring through an own goal in the 18th minute before Suarez stepped up from the spot in the 28th to level, converting coolly after David Ruiz was fouled inside the box by Jack Elliott.

German Berterame put Miami ahead before the break, but Puso Dithejane came off the bench to equalise in the 67th minute with a first-touch finish from inside the area.

It looked as though the points might be shared until homegrown midfielder Preston Plambeck arrived in the 87th minute to score his first-ever MLS goal and send Nu Stadium into raptures.

Miami are now five points behind Nashville SC in the Supporters’ Shield race, with a Matchday 18 trip to CF Montreal coming up on Saturday.

Lewandowski’s debut falls flat

It was an eventful night for Chicago despite the defeat, with legendary Polish striker Robert Lewandowski making his long-awaited MLS debut as a starter at Nu Stadium.

Having arrived in the United States only a little over a week ago, the 37-year-old came off the bench at half-time and offered glimpses of his quality without being able to change the outcome.

Head coach Gregg Berhalter was measured in his assessment of what to expect from Lewandowski in the weeks ahead, tempering expectations while making clear the impact will come.

“It was a priority for us to get him on the field today,” Berhalter said. “He’s only trained for seven or eight days, so we expect him to make a big impact as he continues to get fit.

“Like any player, you build up, you get strong, you get your power, and then you’re good. The timing is different for every player. We’re not in preseason right now, we’re in the middle of a season, and that’s something to consider.”

Griezmann off the mark immediately

It is hard to imagine Antoine Griezmann’s Orlando City debut going any better than it did on Wednesday night in California.

The 35-year-old Frenchman, signed from Atletico Madrid in March and the club’s all-time leading scorer with 211 goals in 488 appearances across his two spells in the Spanish capital, announced himself to the Orlando faithful as the Lions hammered San Jose Earthquakes 4-0 at PayPal Park.

Eduard Atuesta was the creative force behind the performance with three assists, but it was Griezmann who provided the moment the crowd had been waiting for.

David Brekalo opened the scoring in the seventh minute with an unmarked header from Atuesta’s perfectly placed free kick. Ivan Angulo made it 2-0 in the 29th minute, ripping a low shot past Angus Gunn with no pressure to speak of. Then, 48 minutes in, Griezmann got his moment.

Justin Ellis picked off a pass in the attacking third and found the Frenchman, who slipped past a trio of defenders before firing a low shot inside the near post.

Griezmann led the game in chances created with five, led Orlando for touches and passes, and stayed on for the full 90 minutes.

The result lifts Orlando to 10th in the Eastern Conference, just two points behind DC United for the final play-off position.
